A 70-year-old woman who was treated in hospital for Clostridioides difficile infection last winter asks her GP for antibiotics for a cough and sore throat that look viral. The GP advises against them and she asks how antibiotics led to her bowel infection.

Which explanation is most accurate?
UN692.correct_answer: Antibiotics kill protective gut bacteria, letting C. difficile multiply and make toxins

UN692.stem: An 81-year-old man is on day six of an admission for pneumonia, treated with intravenous co-amoxiclav and then a cephalosporin. Over the last 24 hours he has had five episodes of foul-smelling, loose stool with lower abdominal cramps. He has not vomited, no other patients on the bay are unwell, and his white cell count has risen. Which cause is most likely?

UN692.presentation: Infection Control in Suspected Meningococcal Disease
UN692.stem: A 4-year-old boy is brought to the paediatric emergency department with a high fever, lethargy and a spreading non-blanching purpuric rash on his legs. Intravenous ceftriaxone is given immediately and he is to be admitted. A nurse asks which infection control precautions staff should use while caring for him. What is the most appropriate answer?
UN692.correct_answer: Droplet precautions in a single room

UN692.stem:
A newly qualified nurse in a general practice treatment room tells a colleague that she only uses gloves, aprons and careful sharps disposal for patients known to have an infection such as hepatitis or HIV. Her colleague explains how standard infection control precautions should be applied.

Which statement is correct?
UN692.correct_answer: They apply to every patient in every setting, at all times

UN692.presentation: C. difficile relapse within 12 weeks — antibiotic choice
UN692.stem: A 76-year-old woman had a first episode of Clostridioides difficile infection treated with a course of oral vancomycin, and her diarrhoea settled. Three weeks after her symptoms resolved, she develops watery diarrhoea again, and a stool sample is positive for C. difficile toxin. She is not severely unwell. Which treatment is most appropriate?
Several days after completing a course of a broad-spectrum antibiotic, a patient develops profuse watery diarrhoea and crampy abdominal pain. Which diagnosis must be considered?

UN732.presentation: Evaluating A New Hand Hygiene Policy
UN732.stem: After introducing a new hand hygiene protocol, a hospital compares its infection rates from before and after the change. What does this activity most likely represent?

A foundation doctor is asked to insert a peripheral intravenous cannula in a 58-year-old woman on a medical ward who needs intravenous antibiotics. The doctor has just taken blood from the patient in the next bed. Which measure is most important to reduce the risk of a cannula-related bloodstream infection?
UN732.correct_answer: Perform hand hygiene and use aseptic non-touch technique throughout

UN732.stem:
On a surgical ward, an FY1 doctor adjusts the infusion pump settings and moves the bedside table out of the way. She then turns to palpate the abdomen of a 68-year-old man who had a bowel resection two days ago.

Which step is most important at this point to protect the patient from infection?
UN732.correct_answer: Decontaminate her hands with alcohol rub before touching him

UN732.stem: A public health registrar is classifying local health programmes. One of them invites men in their 65th year for a single abdominal ultrasound to detect aortic aneurysms before they cause symptoms. Which level of prevention does this programme represent?
In a study of hand-hygiene compliance, staff wash their hands far more often during the weeks they know an observer is present on the ward than at other times. Which phenomenon best explains this?

A healthcare assistant in a care home tells the visiting doctor that she does not bother cleaning her hands between residents because she always wears gloves when helping them wash.

Which statement should the doctor use to correct her?
UN732.correct_answer: Hands must be cleaned before gloves go on and after they come off

UN732.stem: A 75-year-old man with diabetic kidney disease, stage 4 on his most recent bloods, is on the surgical ward five days after a bowel resection. He has developed a fever, abdominal tenderness and rising inflammatory markers. The surgical team request a contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen today to look for an anastomotic leak or collection. He is euvolaemic and not in heart failure. What is the most important measure to reduce his risk of contrast-associated acute kidney injury?
UN732.correct_answer: Give intravenous volume expansion before and after the contrast

UN732.stem: A 60-year-old man is recovering after a primary PCI for a STEMI. He has no contraindications. Which combination best represents appropriate secondary-prevention drug therapy at discharge?
UN732.correct_answer: Dual antiplatelet therapy, a statin, an ACE inhibitor and a beta-blocker

UN735.stem: A 61-year-old woman has confirmed hypertension on home monitoring. Her GP advises lifestyle changes and recommends starting an antihypertensive. She says she feels perfectly fit and asks why she should take a tablet every day. Which explanation is most accurate?
UN735.correct_answer: Lowering her blood pressure reduces her future risk of stroke, heart attack and kidney disease

UN735.stem:
A 63-year-old lorry driver with intermittent claudication in his right calf is seen in the vascular clinic. He smokes heavily and asks why the team keeps stressing that he should stop, as his legs are the problem rather than his lungs.

Which explanation is most accurate?
UN735.correct_answer: Smoking speeds up the build-up of atherosclerosis in his arteries

UN735.stem: A traveller preparing for a trip to a country where hepatitis A is endemic has never been vaccinated against it. What is the main reason to offer hepatitis A vaccination before departure?
UN735.correct_answer: It reduces the risk of acquiring hepatitis A infection

UN735.stem: A 5-year-old girl has been diagnosed with scabies at her GP surgery and prescribed permethrin cream. Her father asks why he, his wife and their teenage son must also apply the cream on the same day, as none of them is itching. Which explanation is most accurate?
UN735.correct_answer: Contacts may already be infested without itch, because symptoms take weeks to appear

UN735.stem: A mass vaccination campaign reduces how easily an infection spreads through a community, which in turn protects some unvaccinated individuals who have not personally received the vaccine. What term describes this indirect, population-level protection?
A doctor diagnoses a patient with a notifiable infectious disease. The patient asks the doctor to keep it confidential and not tell anyone. What is the doctor's obligation?
UN735.correct_answer: Notify the relevant public health authority, as required by law

UN735.stem: What is the usual mode of transmission for hepatitis A?
A trial reports that a treatment reduces the event rate from 20% to 12%. What is the number needed to treat (NNT)?

UN874.stem: A 24-year-old man attends a sexual health clinic. Three days after unprotected sex with a new partner he developed stinging on passing urine, and since yesterday a thick, yellow-green discharge has been staining his underwear. He has no genital ulcers, rash or fever. Which organism is most likely responsible?

UN874.presentation: STI Screening in an Asymptomatic Patient
UN874.stem: A 27-year-old woman who has recently started a new sexual relationship asks whether she should have a sexual health screen even though she has no symptoms. What is the most appropriate response?
UN874.correct_answer: Discuss appropriate testing according to sexual history and risk

UN874.stem: A 22-year-old man telephones his GP surgery with three days of stinging when passing urine and a clear discharge from the tip of his penis. He started a new sexual relationship a fortnight ago and did not use condoms. He has no fever or loin pain. How should he be managed?
UN874.correct_answer: Arrange testing for sexually transmitted infections, ideally via a sexual health clinic

UN874.stem:
A 30-year-old man attends a sexual health clinic after condomless sex with a new partner. While his screening samples are taken, he asks whether any of the infections being tested for can be prevented by a vaccine. He is particularly worried about one that can be passed on through blood as well as through sex.

Which infection on the list can he be vaccinated against?

A 22-year-old woman attends a sexual health clinic with a week of bilateral lower abdominal pain, pain deep inside during intercourse and bleeding after sex. She has a new sexual partner and they do not use condoms. Her temperature is 37.9°C. On bimanual examination there is tenderness in both adnexa and pain on moving the cervix. A pregnancy test is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN874.presentation: Asymptomatic sexual contact of early syphilis
UN874.stem: A 34-year-old man attends a sexual health clinic because his regular male partner was diagnosed with primary syphilis last week. They last had sex 10 days ago. He has no symptoms, and examination of the genitals, mouth, skin and lymph nodes is normal. He has no drug allergies. Blood is taken for syphilis serology. What is the most appropriate management?
UN874.correct_answer: Offer epidemiological treatment for syphilis today

UN874.presentation: Epididymo-orchitis with gonococcal infection — antibiotic choice
UN874.stem:
A 23-year-old man attends a sexual health clinic with 4 days of right scrotal pain and swelling and a urethral discharge. He had condomless sex with a new partner 2 weeks ago. The epididymis is tender and swollen, the testis lies normally, and torsion is considered unlikely. Microscopy of a urethral smear shows Gram-negative intracellular diplococci. He has no drug allergies.

Which treatment is most appropriate?

A 34-year-old man attends a sexual health clinic because of a sore on the shaft of his penis that appeared ten days ago. He had condomless sex with a new male partner about four weeks ago. The lesion is a single, firm, clean-based ulcer that does not hurt even when pressed. There are rubbery, non-tender enlarged nodes in both groins. He feels well. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN875.stem: A 22-year-old man telephones his GP surgery with three days of stinging when passing urine and a clear discharge from the tip of his penis. He started a new sexual relationship a fortnight ago and did not use condoms. He has no fever or loin pain. How should he be managed?
UN875.correct_answer: Arrange testing for sexually transmitted infections, ideally via a sexual health clinic

UN875.presentation: STI Screening in an Asymptomatic Patient
UN875.stem: A 27-year-old woman who has recently started a new sexual relationship asks whether she should have a sexual health screen even though she has no symptoms. What is the most appropriate response?
UN875.correct_answer: Discuss appropriate testing according to sexual history and risk

UN875.presentation: Anogenital warts in pregnancy — treatment choice
UN875.stem: A 27-year-old woman who is 20 weeks pregnant attends the sexual health clinic with several small, soft, non-keratinised warts on the vulva. Her screen for other sexually transmitted infections is negative. After discussion, she would like the warts treated rather than waiting until after the birth. Which treatment is most appropriate?

UN875.presentation: Early syphilis with penicillin anaphylaxis — alternative antibiotic
UN875.stem: A 34-year-old man is diagnosed with secondary syphilis in a sexual health clinic. He has a documented history of anaphylaxis to amoxicillin. He has no neurological, eye or ear symptoms and his HIV test is negative. Which antibiotic is the most appropriate alternative to penicillin?

A public health doctor is comparing the same rapid chlamydia test used in two settings: a sexual health clinic, where the infection is common among people tested, and a community screening programme, where it is much less common. The test's sensitivity and specificity are the same in both settings. Compared with the community programme, how does the probability that a positive result is a true positive differ in the sexual health clinic?

UN875.presentation: Rationale for Partner Notification in Gonorrhoea
UN875.stem: A patient is diagnosed with gonorrhoea, and the sexual health clinic asks whether their recent partners can be contacted and offered testing. Why is partner notification important?
UN875.correct_answer: To identify and treat contacts and reduce onward transmission

UN875.stem: A 34-year-old man attends a sexual health clinic worried about difficulty maintaining erections and delayed ejaculation. He has a regular partner, no new sexual contacts and no genital symptoms. His GP started sertraline for generalised anxiety eight weeks ago, and the problems began a few weeks later. What should be a central part of his assessment?
UN875.correct_answer: Review his current medicines for adverse effects

UN875.stem:
A man is newly diagnosed with HIV infection. He is asymptomatic and his CD4 count is 450 cells/mm³.

According to UK (BHIVA) guidelines, what is the most appropriate next step in his management?
UN875.correct_answer: Start ART immediately, regardless of the CD4 count

UN946.presentation: Blood cultures in suspected bacterial meningitis
UN946.stem:
A 34-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department with a high fever, intense headache and neck stiffness that came on over the last 12 hours. Bacterial meningitis is suspected. She is conscious, her airway is safe and she has no rash.

Which investigation should be taken without delay as part of her first assessment?

A 66-year-old woman receiving chemotherapy for ovarian cancer is admitted with rigors and a fever, and neutropenic sepsis is suspected. Intravenous antibiotics are being prepared. Which investigation should be taken first, as long as it does not delay the antibiotics?

UN946.presentation: Sickle cell disease — long-term antibiotic prophylaxis
UN946.stem: A 3-year-old boy with sickle cell disease (HbSS), diagnosed through newborn screening, is reviewed in the paediatric haematology clinic. He is well, his routine immunisations are up to date and he has no drug allergies. His parents ask which daily medicine will protect him from serious bacterial infection. Which long-term antibiotic prophylaxis is most appropriate?

UN946.presentation: Antibiotic Request for a Viral Infection
UN946.stem: A patient with a straightforward viral upper respiratory tract infection, and no features suggesting bacterial infection, asks their doctor for antibiotics. What is the most appropriate response?
UN946.correct_answer: Explain why antibiotics are unlikely to help; give symptomatic advice and safety-netting

UN946.stem: A 54-year-old man with a mechanical aortic valve is referred to the acute medical unit by his GP after ten days of fevers, aches and fatigue. On arrival he is alert, his observations are stable and there is no obvious source of infection. The team suspects prosthetic valve endocarditis. Which investigation should be done before any antibiotic is given?
UN946.correct_answer: Three sets of blood cultures from separate venepunctures

UN946.presentation: Antibiotic Choice in a Patient on Warfarin
UN946.stem: A patient taking warfarin for a mechanical heart valve requires antibiotic treatment for a chest infection. Which of the following antibiotics carries the greatest risk of significantly raising the INR?

An 81-year-old care home resident is admitted to the emergency department with a suspected chest infection. She is confused, hypotensive and tachypnoeic, and she has been assessed as being at high risk of severe illness or death from sepsis. Blood cultures have been taken. When should antibiotics be given?

UN946.presentation: Bacterial meningitis — CSF and Gram stain
UN946.stem:
A 14-month-old boy is brought to the emergency department. His GP treated him for a painful left ear four days ago, but over the last day he has become feverish, irritable and reluctant to feed, and he cries when his legs are moved. His neck is stiff and there is no rash. After blood cultures and a first dose of intravenous ceftriaxone, a lumbar puncture is performed. The fluid is cloudy, with a very high white cell count made up mainly of neutrophils, a raised protein, and a glucose well below half of the simultaneous blood value. Gram staining shows Gram-positive cocci in pairs.

Which interpretation of these findings is most accurate?

UN968.stem: A woman has fever with rigors, loin pain and tenderness, and dysuria with urinary frequency. Urine dipstick is positive for nitrites and leucocytes. What is the most appropriate management?
UN968.correct_answer: Send a urine culture and start empirical antibiotics per local guidance

UN968.stem: A 30-year-old woman has fever with rigors, loin pain and tenderness in the renal angle, with dysuria and urinary frequency. Urine dipstick is positive for nitrites and leucocytes. She is able to tolerate oral fluids and is haemodynamically stable. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A patient's urine dipstick is positive for nitrites and leucocyte esterase. In a patient with urinary symptoms, what does this most suggest?

UN968.presentation: Suspected ANCA vasculitis with AKI — bedside test
UN968.stem: A 59-year-old man is admitted with 6 weeks of nasal crusting, blood-stained nasal discharge and joint pains, and more recently haemoptysis. His creatinine has risen from 85 to 210 micromol/L over a week; his potassium is 4.6 mmol/L. Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA) testing has been sent. Which bedside investigation is most important now to help establish the cause of his kidney injury?
When urinary symptoms are grouped into categories based on the phase of the bladder cycle they affect, which option below belongs in the 'storage' group?
A 3-year-old girl presents with fever, vomiting, and abdominal pain. She has no urinary symptoms. Urine dipstick is positive for leucocytes and nitrites. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN968.correct_answer: Send urine for culture and start empirical oral antibiotics

UN968.stem: A 61-year-old man sees his GP with 2 days of fever, dysuria, urinary frequency and perineal pain. Rectal examination reveals an exquisitely tender prostate. He is not septic, can take oral medication and has no drug allergies. A midstream urine sample has been sent for culture. Which oral antibiotic is most appropriate to start?

UN968.presentation: Persistent pelvic pain in a man
UN968.stem:
A 41-year-old man has had five months of aching discomfort in the perineum and above the pubis, with urinary frequency and pain on ejaculation. He has had no fever or loin pain, his urine dipstick and culture are negative, and he is otherwise well.

Which diagnosis should be considered?

UN1216.stem:
A 31-year-old woman sees her GP with a widespread seborrhoeic dermatitis-like rash, recurrent oral thrush and a recent episode of shingles. She has no known risk factors and is worried about what is causing these problems. The GP thinks HIV infection is possible.

What is the most appropriate approach?
UN1216.correct_answer: Explain why testing is advised and offer it with her verbal consent

UN1216.presentation: STI Screening in an Asymptomatic Patient
UN1216.stem: A 27-year-old woman who has recently started a new sexual relationship asks whether she should have a sexual health screen even though she has no symptoms. What is the most appropriate response?
UN1216.correct_answer: Discuss appropriate testing according to sexual history and risk

UN1216.stem: A 22-year-old man telephones his GP surgery with three days of stinging when passing urine and a clear discharge from the tip of his penis. He started a new sexual relationship a fortnight ago and did not use condoms. He has no fever or loin pain. How should he be managed?
UN1216.correct_answer: Arrange testing for sexually transmitted infections, ideally via a sexual health clinic

UN1216.stem: A 26-year-old woman has a positive HIV test at a sexual health clinic during routine screening. She feels well and has no symptoms. Her CD4 count is within the normal range and her viral load is moderately raised. She asks whether she can wait a few years before taking any medication. What is the most appropriate advice?
UN1216.correct_answer: Offer antiretroviral therapy now, whatever her CD4 count

UN1216.stem:
A 29-year-old woman has a reactive fourth-generation HIV test confirmed at the sexual health clinic. Before discussing treatment and the need for prophylaxis against opportunistic infections, the team wants to know how far her immune system has been damaged.

Which blood test gives this information?

UN1216.presentation: Rationale for Partner Notification in Gonorrhoea
UN1216.stem: A patient is diagnosed with gonorrhoea, and the sexual health clinic asks whether their recent partners can be contacted and offered testing. Why is partner notification important?
UN1216.correct_answer: To identify and treat contacts and reduce onward transmission

UN1216.presentation: Anogenital warts in pregnancy — treatment choice
UN1216.stem: A 27-year-old woman who is 20 weeks pregnant attends the sexual health clinic with several small, soft, non-keratinised warts on the vulva. A 30-year-old man attends a sexual health clinic after condomless sex with a new partner. While his screening samples are taken, he asks whether any of the infections being tested for can be prevented by a vaccine. He is particularly worried about one that can be passed on through blood as well as through sex.

Which infection on the list can he be vaccinated against?

Which investigation should be taken without delay as part of her first assessment?

A 57-year-old woman arrives at the emergency department with rigors, a heart rate of 118/min and a blood pressure of 96/60 mmHg. She is being managed for suspected sepsis and blood cultures have been taken, but no obvious cause has been found yet.

Alongside starting treatment, what else is a priority in her assessment?
UN1275.correct_answer: Actively search for the source of infection

UN1275.stem: An 81-year-old care home resident is admitted to the emergency department with a suspected chest infection. She is confused, hypotensive and tachypnoeic, and she has been assessed as being at high risk of severe illness or death from sepsis. Blood cultures have been taken. When should antibiotics be given?

Which investigation should be done before any antibiotic is given?
UN1275.correct_answer: Three sets of blood cultures from separate venepunctures

UN1275.stem: A patient with a suspected infection has a serum lactate of 4.5 mmol/L, a temperature of 38.9°C and a low blood pressure. What is the most appropriate immediate response?
UN1275.correct_answer: Implement the Sepsis Six within 1 hour

UN1275.stem: On the acute medical unit, a 45-year-old woman admitted with loin pain and rigors becomes drowsy over the next hour. She is now cold and clammy with a falling blood pressure and a rising heart rate, and she has not passed urine since admission. What is the most appropriate course of action?
UN1275.correct_answer: Activate the sepsis pathway, taking cultures and starting time-critical treatment without delay

UN1275.stem: An 82-year-old man is seen in the emergency department with fever and new confusion three days after a urinary catheter change. Blood cultures are sent and a venous gas shows a lactate above the normal range. The foundation doctor asks what this result tells the team. What is the best interpretation?
UN1275.correct_answer: Organs and tissues may not be receiving enough oxygen

UN1325.stem: A 66-year-old woman receiving chemotherapy for ovarian cancer is admitted with rigors and a fever, and neutropenic sepsis is suspected. Intravenous antibiotics are being prepared. Which investigation should be taken first, as long as it does not delay the antibiotics?

Which investigation should be taken without delay as part of her first assessment?

A 68-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate attends the emergency department with one day of a hot, swollen and very painful left knee. She cannot move it or bear weight. Her other joints are no worse than usual. Her temperature is 38.4 degrees C and pulse 102 bpm. She has no prosthetic joints. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
UN1325.correct_answer: Aspirate the joint for urgent Gram stain and culture, take blood cultures, then start empirical IV antibiotics

UN1325.stem: On the acute medical unit, a 45-year-old woman admitted with loin pain and rigors becomes drowsy over the next hour. She is now cold and clammy with a falling blood pressure and a rising heart rate, and she has not passed urine since admission. What is the most appropriate course of action?
UN1325.correct_answer: Activate the sepsis pathway, taking cultures and starting time-critical treatment without delay

UN1325.stem: A 34-year-old man with acute myeloid leukaemia is on the haematology ward a week after induction treatment. During the night he becomes hot and has a shaking episode. His most recent blood count showed almost no neutrophils. He is alert and talking. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN1325.correct_answer: Assess him urgently and give intravenous broad-spectrum antibiotics without delay

UN1325.stem:
On the postnatal ward, a 2-day-old boy born at term after prolonged rupture of membranes is noted by the midwife to be sleepy and not waking for feeds. His temperature is 35.9°C, he is breathing fast with grunting, and his skin looks mottled. His capillary glucose is normal.

What is the most appropriate immediate management?
UN1325.correct_answer: Take blood cultures and start intravenous antibiotics immediately

UN1325.stem: An 81-year-old care home resident is admitted to the emergency department with a suspected chest infection. UN1325.correct_answer: Actively search for the source of infection

UN1434.presentation: Uncomplicated dyspepsia — NICE test and treat
UN1434.stem: A 52-year-old man presents with epigastric discomfort and bloating. He has no alarm features and has taken no prior medication for symptoms. What is the most appropriate initial management according to NICE?
UN1434.correct_answer: Test and treat for H. pylori

UN1434.stem: For many months, a 24-year-old woman has had pelvic pain that flares specifically around menstruation and also during sex; a urine dipstick has already ruled out infection as the cause. Which underlying condition fits best?

A 22-year-old man telephones his GP surgery with three days of stinging when passing urine and a clear discharge from the tip of his penis. He started a new sexual relationship a fortnight ago and did not use condoms. He has no fever or loin pain. How should he be managed?
UN1434.correct_answer: Arrange testing for sexually transmitted infections, ideally via a sexual health clinic

UN1434.stem: A 20-year-old man attends a sexual health clinic with three weeks of intense itching that keeps him awake. There are itchy reddish-brown nodules on his penis and scrotum and fine wavy tracks on the sides of his fingers. His girlfriend, with whom he shares a bed, has started itching around her waist. What is the most appropriate management approach?
UN1434.correct_answer: Treat him and his girlfriend at the same time, even if her symptoms are mild

UN1434.presentation: Rationale for Partner Notification in Gonorrhoea

UN1434.correct_answer: To identify and treat contacts and reduce onward transmission

UN1434.stem:
Two weeks after returning from a holiday in the Caribbean, a 38-year-old man sees his GP with five days of fever, a widespread itchy red rash and severe pain and swelling in his wrists, fingers and ankles on both sides. He recalls many mosquito bites. He has had no diarrhoea, urethral discharge or new sexual partners, and no joint is hot and red.

Which diagnosis is most likely?

UN1434.presentation: Severe period pain in an adolescent
UN1434.stem:
A 16-year-old girl has had cramping pelvic pain with every period since she was 13, and it has worsened each year. She now misses school for two or three days each month, and ibuprofen and paracetamol only partly help. She is not sexually active, and her abdominal examination is normal.

Which diagnosis should be suspected?

A 23-year-old woman comes in with lower abdominal discomfort and an unusual discharge, and moving her cervix on examination causes marked tenderness. If her pelvic infection goes untreated, which long-term complication is she at risk of?

UN1435.presentation: HIV post-diagnosis — when to start treatment
UN1435.stem: A patient is newly diagnosed with HIV and is asymptomatic with a well-preserved CD4 count. What is the most appropriate approach to antiretroviral therapy?
UN1435.correct_answer: Start antiretroviral therapy regardless of CD4 count

On the second day after a hip replacement, a 71-year-old woman has a painful, distended bladder and a bladder scan confirms urinary retention. The foundation doctor is preparing to insert a urethral catheter on the ward.

Which approach is essential for this procedure?
UN1560.correct_answer: Explain the procedure, obtain her consent and use aseptic technique

UN1560.stem: A foundation doctor is asked to insert a peripheral intravenous cannula in a 58-year-old woman on a medical ward who needs intravenous antibiotics. UN1560.correct_answer: Perform hand hygiene and use aseptic non-touch technique throughout

UN1560.presentation: Fever without a source — blood cultures before antibiotics
UN1560.stem: A 63-year-old man is admitted with 3 weeks of intermittent fevers, night sweats and fatigue. He had a dental extraction 6 weeks ago. Temperature is 38.6°C, blood pressure 128/76 mmHg and he is alert. There is a new soft pansystolic murmur at the apex. Urinalysis shows microscopic haematuria. Chest X-ray is normal. He has not received any antibiotics. Which is the most appropriate next investigation?
UN1560.correct_answer: Three blood culture sets from separate sites

UN1560.presentation: Blood cultures in suspected bacterial meningitis
UN1560.stem:
A 34-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department with a high fever, intense headache and neck stiffness that came on over the last 12 hours. Bacterial meningitis is suspected. She is conscious, her airway is safe and she has no rash.

Which investigation should be taken without delay as part of her first assessment?

A 54-year-old man with a mechanical aortic valve is referred to the acute medical unit by his GP after ten days of fevers, aches and fatigue. On arrival he is alert, his observations are stable and there is no obvious source of infection. The team suspects prosthetic valve endocarditis. Which investigation should be done before any antibiotic is given?
UN1560.correct_answer: Three sets of blood cultures from separate venepunctures

UN1560.stem:
A foundation doctor on a surgical ward is asked to take blood cultures from a 66-year-old man with rigors two days after a bowel resection. A senior nurse reminds her to clean the skin with chlorhexidine in alcohol, let it dry, avoid touching the site again and disinfect the bottle tops before inoculating them.

What is the main purpose of this careful technique?
UN1560.correct_answer: To avoid contaminating the sample and producing false-positive results

UN1560.stem: A 68-year-old woman who had a mechanical aortic valve replacement four years ago is admitted with three weeks of intermittent fevers, sweats, fatigue and weight loss. There is a new early diastolic murmur, small haemorrhages under the conjunctivae, and her urine dipstick shows blood. She is alert, with a blood pressure of 128/74 mmHg and no signs of sepsis or heart failure. What is the most important initial investigation?
UN1560.correct_answer: At least three sets of blood cultures from separate venepunctures before antibiotics

UN1562.presentation: Antibiotic Request for a Viral Infection
UN1562.stem: A patient with a straightforward viral upper respiratory tract infection, and no features suggesting bacterial infection, asks their doctor for antibiotics. What is the most appropriate response?
UN1562.correct_answer: Explain why antibiotics are unlikely to help; give symptomatic advice and safety-netting

UN1562.correct_answer: Explain that antibiotics are not routinely indicated; give symptomatic advice

UN1562.stem: A 45-year-old woman has three days of coryza, sore throat and a dry cough, with no fever. Examination is normal. She asks for antibiotics because they 'always work'. What is the most appropriate management?
UN1562.correct_answer: Explain it is viral, offer symptomatic advice and safety-net

What is the most appropriate response?
UN1562.correct_answer: Explain that antibiotics are unlikely to help, and give advice on symptom care and when to seek help

UN1562.stem: A 25-year-old man presents with 2 days of sharp central chest pain that is worse on lying down and better on sitting forward. He had a viral upper respiratory tract infection 2 weeks ago. ECG shows saddle-shaped ST elevation in multiple leads with PR depression. What is the most likely diagnosis and first-line treatment?

Between episodes he is completely asymptomatic. There is no personal history of atopy, no eczema, and no family history of asthma. What is the most appropriate diagnosis?

He asks for antibiotics because they have always worked for him in the past. Which principle should most guide the GP's prescribing decision?

A 7-year-old child presents with sudden onset of scattered petechiae and easy bruising 2 weeks after a viral upper respiratory tract infection. He is systemically well. FBC shows isolated thrombocytopenia (platelets 12 × 10⁹/L), Hb 125 g/L, and WBC 7.5 × 10⁹/L. What is the most likely diagnosis and management?
UN1562.correct_answer: Immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) — observe (most resolve spontaneously)

UN1563.correct_answer: Explain that antibiotics are unlikely to help, and give advice on symptom care and when to seek help

He is flying abroad next week and insists that he must have antibiotics to clear it up before then, saying a previous doctor always gave him some. The GP believes antibiotics are unnecessary and could cause harm. What is the most appropriate response?
UN1563.correct_answer: Explain why antibiotics are not appropriate, decline to prescribe, and give self-care and safety-netting advice

Which principle is the GP demonstrating?

ECG shows QTc of 540 ms. She develops polymorphic ventricular tachycardia with twisting of QRS complexes around the isoelectric line. What is the arrhythmia and immediate treatment?
UN1563.correct_answer: Torsades de pointes — IV magnesium sulphate 2g

UN1563.stem: A 3-year-old has a few days of mild fever, painful mouth ulcers, and a vesicular rash on the palms of the hands and soles of the feet. He is otherwise well and eating a little less. What is the most appropriate management?
UN1563.correct_answer: Supportive care (fluids, analgesia) — it is self-limiting

UN1565.correct_answer: Switch to an appropriate narrower-spectrum antibiotic if suitable

UN1565.correct_answer: Switch to the narrowest antibiotic that will be effective

UN1565.correct_answer: Prescribe antibiotics only when there is a clinical indication, so asymptomatic bacteriuria is not treated

UN1573.correct_answer: RIPE for 2 months, then rifampicin and isoniazid

UN1573.stem: A 55-year-old man who has never smoked has a telephone consultation with his GP. He developed a cold in the spring and has had a dry, tickly cough ever since, now four months later. He feels otherwise well, has no breathlessness and has not coughed up blood. How should his cough be classified?

A 45-year-old man who works as a bus driver is diagnosed with sputum smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis after months of cough and weight loss. His wife, who shares his bedroom, is referred to the TB service for contact screening.

By which route is she most likely to have been exposed?
UN1573.correct_answer: Inhaling droplet nuclei released when he coughs

UN1573.stem: A 33-year-old nurse who works on a neonatal unit is diagnosed with sputum smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis after investigation of two months of cough and weight loss. The respiratory team is about to start treatment. Apart from starting treatment, what is the most appropriate action for the diagnosing doctor?
UN1573.correct_answer: Notify the local health protection team so contact tracing can begin

UN1573.stem: A 34-year-old woman recently recruited from a country with a high incidence of tuberculosis attends occupational health before starting work as a nurse on a UK ward. She feels well, with no cough, fever, night sweats or weight loss. An interferon-gamma release assay is positive and her chest X-ray is normal. HIV test and liver function tests are normal. What is the most appropriate management?
UN1573.correct_answer: Three months of isoniazid (with pyridoxine) and rifampicin

UN1573.presentation: Silicosis with new cavitation — investigation for tuberculosis
UN1573.stem:
A 62-year-old man who worked for 30 years as a stonemason has known silicosis. He sees his GP with 6 weeks of productive cough, night sweats and 5 kg weight loss. His temperature is 37.9°C. A chest X-ray shows a new cavitating lesion in the right upper lobe on a background of nodular upper-lobe changes.

Which investigation is most appropriate next?
UN1573.correct_answer: Sputum for acid-fast bacilli microscopy and culture

UN1573.stem: A patient is diagnosed with active pulmonary tuberculosis. What is the most appropriate standard initial drug regimen?
UN1573.correct_answer: Rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol, with pyridoxine

She has no prosthetic heart valve, implanted device or central venous line, her temperature settled within hours, and she is now eating and mobilising. Repeat cultures show no growth.

What is the most likely explanation?
UN1740.correct_answer: Contamination of the blood culture by skin organisms

UN1740.stem: A new blood test for a disease is reported to have a sensitivity of 90%. What does this figure actually tell you?
UN1740.correct_answer: 90% of people with the disease will test positive

UN1740.presentation: Prolonged fever with weight loss and lymphadenopathy
UN1740.stem:
A 41-year-old woman has had 5 weeks of fevers up to 38.8°C, drenching night sweats and 6 kg weight loss. Examination shows several small, rubbery, non-tender lymph nodes in the neck and both groins, with no other abnormality. Her lymphocyte count is low, but her other blood count results are normal. Renal and liver function, urinalysis, urine culture, repeated blood cultures and chest X-ray are normal. She has never had an HIV test.

Which test should she be offered next?
UN1740.correct_answer: HIV antigen and antibody blood test

UN1740.stem: A 33-year-old man presents febrile, muddled and fitting repeatedly on one side of his body; the clinical picture is thought to represent brain inflammation of viral origin. Without waiting for test results, which drug should be given to cover this possibility?

On the second day after a hip replacement, a 71-year-old woman has a painful, distended bladder and a bladder scan confirms urinary retention. The foundation doctor is preparing to insert a urethral catheter on the ward.

Which approach is essential for this procedure?
UN1741.correct_answer: Explain the procedure, obtain her consent and use aseptic technique

UN1741.stem: A patient with a suspected infection has a serum lactate of 4.5 mmol/L, a temperature of 38.9°C and a low blood pressure. What is the most appropriate immediate response?

UN1745.correct_answer: Droplet precautions in a single room

UN1745.stem: A patient is diagnosed with active pulmonary tuberculosis. What is the most appropriate standard initial drug regimen?
UN1745.correct_answer: Rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol, with pyridoxine

A newly qualified nurse in a general practice treatment room tells a colleague that she only uses gloves, aprons and careful sharps disposal for patients known to have an infection such as hepatitis or HIV. Her colleague explains how standard infection control precautions should be applied.

Which statement is correct?
UN1745.correct_answer: They apply to every patient in every setting, at all times

UN1745.stem: A 46-year-old man living in a homeless hostel sees the visiting GP. UN1746.correct_answer: Notify the local health protection team now, on clinical suspicion

UN1746.correct_answer: Notify the local health protection team on clinical suspicion of measles

UN1838.stem: A 17-year-old footballer recovering from confirmed glandular fever asks his doctor when he can safely return to training and matches. Why is he advised to avoid contact sport for several weeks?

A 19-year-old has a sore throat, fever, marked cervical lymphadenopathy and lethargy, with atypical lymphocytes on the blood film. Which is the most appropriate advice?
UN1838.correct_answer: Avoid amoxicillin and contact sports (risk of rash and splenic rupture)

UN1838.stem: A 16-year-old boy has infectious mononucleosis confirmed on a blood test. He has a sore throat and marked tiredness but is eating and drinking, and he has no breathing difficulty or abdominal pain. His mother asks when he can go back to school. What is the most appropriate advice?

She feels a little better and asks her GP whether she can play in a match next weekend. What is the main reason to advise her against this?

UN1838.presentation: Acute pericarditis in an amateur athlete — return to sport
UN1838.stem: A 24-year-old man who plays amateur football has low-risk acute pericarditis and is being treated at home with ibuprofen, colchicine and a proton pump inhibitor. At review after 5 days his chest pain has gone, but his C-reactive protein (CRP) is still raised. He asks whether he can play in a match this weekend. Which is the most appropriate advice?
UN1838.correct_answer: Avoid strenuous exercise until symptoms and CRP have normalised

UN1838.stem:
A 20-year-old man who plays football for a semi-professional team is about to be discharged after a 4-day admission with myocarditis following a viral illness. His chest pain has settled, troponin is falling and he has had no arrhythmias. He asks whether he can return to full training next week.

What is the most appropriate advice?
UN1838.correct_answer: Avoid competitive sport until cardiology review

UN1839.stem: A 3-year-old boy has a fever and a rash of small purple-red spots that do not fade when pressed. He is floppy and very difficult to wake. What is the most important diagnosis to consider?

A 19-year-old student presents with fever, confusion and hypotension. There is a rapidly spreading non-blanching purpuric rash. Neck stiffness is absent. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
UN1839.correct_answer: Immediate IV ceftriaxone (do not delay for investigations)

UN1839.presentation: Infection Control in Suspected Meningococcal Disease
UN1839.stem: A 4-year-old boy is brought to the paediatric emergency department with a high fever, lethargy and a spreading non-blanching purpuric rash on his legs. Intravenous ceftriaxone is given immediately and he is to be admitted. A nurse asks which infection control precautions staff should use while caring for him. What is the most appropriate answer?
UN1839.correct_answer: Droplet precautions in a single room

UN1839.presentation: Fever, Neck Stiffness and Non-Blanching Rash
UN1839.stem: A university student presents with fever, a severe headache, neck stiffness and a rash that does not fade under pressure. She is becoming increasingly drowsy. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN1839.presentation: Fever with a spreading non-blanching rash
UN1839.stem:
An 18-month-old girl is collected early from nursery because of a fever. Over the next three hours her parents notice tiny purple spots on her legs that do not disappear when pressed, and more are appearing on her trunk. She is miserable, her hands and feet are cold, and she cries when her legs are moved.

Which diagnosis must be assumed?

A 19-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by his flatmate with a few hours of fever, headache, vomiting and aching legs. He is drowsy but rousable. Which examination finding would most strongly suggest meningococcal septicaemia?
UN1839.correct_answer: Non-blanching petechiae on the trunk and legs

UN1839.stem: A 19-year-old woman has fever, severe headache, neck stiffness and photophobia, and is becoming drowsy. She has a non-blanching purpuric rash. Suspected meningococcal meningitis with septicaemia. What is the most appropriate immediate management?

A 19-year-old university student presents to ED with a 6-hour history of fever, headache, vomiting, and myalgia. He is tachycardic (HR 110 bpm), hypotensive (BP 96/58 mmHg), and has a widespread purpuric rash that is non-blanching. He is confused. What is the single most important immediate action?
UN1839.correct_answer: IV ceftriaxone 2 g now — do not wait for investigations

UN1853.presentation: STI Screening in an Asymptomatic Patient
UN1853.stem: A 27-year-old woman who has recently started a new sexual relationship asks whether she should have a sexual health screen even though she has no symptoms. What is the most appropriate response?
UN1853.correct_answer: Discuss appropriate testing according to sexual history and risk

UN1853.stem: A 34-year-old man attends a sexual health clinic worried about difficulty maintaining erections and delayed ejaculation. He has a regular partner, no new sexual contacts and no genital symptoms. His GP started sertraline for generalised anxiety eight weeks ago, and the problems began a few weeks later. What should be a central part of his assessment?
UN1853.correct_answer: Review his current medicines for adverse effects

UN1853.stem: A 22-year-old woman attends a sexual health clinic with a week of bilateral lower abdominal pain, pain deep inside during intercourse and bleeding after sex. She has a new sexual partner and they do not use condoms. Her temperature is 37.9°C. On bimanual examination there is tenderness in both adnexa and pain on moving the cervix. A pregnancy test is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old man telephones his GP surgery with three days of stinging when passing urine and a clear discharge from the tip of his penis. He started a new sexual relationship a fortnight ago and did not use condoms. He has no fever or loin pain. How should he be managed?
UN1853.correct_answer: Arrange testing for sexually transmitted infections, ideally via a sexual health clinic

UN1853.presentation: Persistent conjunctivitis in a sexually active adult — investigation
UN1853.stem:
A 23-year-old woman sees her GP with 4 weeks of a red, sticky right eye. A week of chloramphenicol eye drops has not helped. Vision is normal and there is no pain or photophobia. There are follicles on the lower lid conjunctiva and a tender lymph node in front of the right ear. She started a new sexual relationship 3 months ago and has noticed increased vaginal discharge.

Which investigation is most appropriate?
UN1853.correct_answer: Conjunctival swab for chlamydia nucleic acid testing

UN1853.presentation: Asymptomatic sexual contact of early syphilis
UN1853.stem: A 34-year-old man attends a sexual health clinic because his regular male partner was diagnosed with primary syphilis last week. They last had sex 10 days ago. He has no symptoms, and examination of the genitals, mouth, skin and lymph nodes is normal. He has no drug allergies. Blood is taken for syphilis serology. What is the most appropriate management?
UN1853.correct_answer: Offer epidemiological treatment for syphilis today

UN1853.stem:
A 52-year-old woman receives an NHS invitation to breast screening and asks her GP what it is for. She has no symptoms and no family history. Her friend believes screening means she will never get breast cancer, and that she would not need to report a lump found between appointments.

What best describes the purpose of the programme?
UN1853.correct_answer: To find breast cancer early in women without symptoms

UN1853.presentation: Rationale for Partner Notification in Gonorrhoea
UN1853.stem: A patient is diagnosed with gonorrhoea, and the sexual health clinic asks whether their recent partners can be contacted and offered testing. Why is partner notification important?
UN1853.correct_answer: To identify and treat contacts and reduce onward transmission

UN1854.presentation: Rationale for Partner Notification in Gonorrhoea
UN1854.stem: A patient is diagnosed with gonorrhoea, and the sexual health clinic asks whether their recent partners can be contacted and offered testing. Why is partner notification important?
UN1854.correct_answer: To identify and treat contacts and reduce onward transmission

UN1854.stem: A 22-year-old woman has post-coital bleeding and a mucopurulent cervical discharge. A nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT) is positive for Chlamydia trachomatis. What is the most appropriate management?
UN1854.correct_answer: Doxycycline, plus partner notification and testing

UN1854.stem: A 27-year-old woman is told at a sexual health clinic that her test for chlamydia is positive. The health adviser explains that people she has had sex with recently will need to be contacted, and offers to do this anonymously. She asks why this is necessary. What is the main purpose of this process?
UN1854.correct_answer: To ensure exposed partners are offered testing and treatment

UN1854.presentation: Gonorrhoea — who needs a test of cure
UN1854.stem: A 26-year-old man is diagnosed with gonorrhoea at a sexual health clinic. NAATs (nucleic acid amplification tests) are positive on his urine and on a pharyngeal swab. Cultures are taken from both sites and he is given intramuscular ceftriaxone. His urethral discharge settles within a few days and partner notification is under way. What is the most appropriate follow-up testing?
UN1854.correct_answer: Test of cure by NAAT, as the pharynx was infected

UN1854.stem: A man has a purulent urethral discharge and dysuria, and a swab confirms Neisseria gonorrhoeae. What is the most appropriate treatment, alongside partner notification?
A patient has painless, fleshy, cauliflower-like lumps in the genital area. What is the most likely cause and an appropriate management approach?
UN1854.correct_answer: Anogenital warts (HPV) — topical therapy or cryotherapy/ablation, plus sexual-health review

UN1854.presentation: STI Screening in an Asymptomatic Patient
UN1854.stem: A 27-year-old woman who has recently started a new sexual relationship asks whether she should have a sexual health screen even though she has no symptoms. What is the most appropriate response?
UN1854.correct_answer: Discuss appropriate testing according to sexual history and risk

UN1854.stem: A 23-year-old woman attends a sexual health clinic with 3 days of painful genital ulcers and dysuria. Examination shows several shallow, tender ulcers on the labia with tender inguinal lymph nodes. Genital herpes is suspected. Which test is most appropriate to confirm the diagnosis?
UN1854.correct_answer: Swab of an ulcer base for HSV NAAT

UN1855.stem: A man has a purulent urethral discharge and dysuria, and a swab confirms Neisseria gonorrhoeae. What is the most appropriate treatment, alongside partner notification?
A 25-year-old man has dysuria and a profuse purulent urethral discharge. A NAAT and culture confirm Neisseria gonorrhoeae. What is the most appropriate first-line treatment?

A 31-year-old man attends a sexual health clinic worried about an infection because his right testis feels heavier than the left. He has no pain, urethral discharge or dysuria. On examination there is a firm, irregular, non-tender area that cannot be separated from the body of the right testis. The epididymis feels normal, and a torch held against the scrotum does not light up the swelling. What is the most appropriate next investigation?

UN1855.presentation: Gonorrhoea — who needs a test of cure
UN1855.stem: A 26-year-old man is diagnosed with gonorrhoea at a sexual health clinic. NAATs (nucleic acid amplification tests) are positive on his urine and on a pharyngeal swab. Cultures are taken from both sites and he is given intramuscular ceftriaxone. His urethral discharge settles within a few days and partner notification is under way. What is the most appropriate follow-up testing?
UN1855.correct_answer: Test of cure by NAAT, as the pharynx was infected

UN1855.presentation: Gradual Scrotal Pain With Urethral Symptoms
UN1855.stem: A sexually active 25-year-old man develops scrotal swelling and discomfort on the right side that has worsened steadily over three days, along with pain on passing urine and a clear urethral discharge. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN1855.presentation: Epididymo-orchitis with gonococcal infection — antibiotic choice
UN1855.stem:
A 23-year-old man attends a sexual health clinic with 4 days of right scrotal pain and swelling and a urethral discharge. He had condomless sex with a new partner 2 weeks ago. The epididymis is tender and swollen, the testis lies normally, and torsion is considered unlikely. Microscopy of a urethral smear shows Gram-negative intracellular diplococci. He has no drug allergies.

Which treatment is most appropriate?

UN1855.presentation: Epididymo-orchitis in a young man — microbiological testing
UN1855.stem: A 24-year-old man presents with 3 days of gradually worsening right scrotal pain and swelling, dysuria and a scant urethral discharge. He has had a new female sexual partner in the past month. The right epididymis is tender and swollen, the testis lies normally, and the cremasteric reflex is present. Torsion is considered unlikely. Before starting antibiotics, which investigation is most important?

UN1855.presentation: Reactive arthritis — identifying the triggering infection
UN1855.stem: A 24-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a swollen right knee and a painful left heel for 5 days. Three weeks ago he had dysuria and a urethral discharge that settled without treatment; he has had a new sexual partner recently. He has no diarrhoea. Knee aspirate shows no crystals and Gram stain is negative, with culture pending. Reactive arthritis is suspected. Which investigation is most appropriate to identify the triggering infection?
UN1855.correct_answer: First-void urine nucleic acid amplification test

UN1984.presentation: Acute Flu-Like Illness in an Outbreak
UN1984.stem: During a confirmed local flu outbreak, a 27-year-old man comes down abruptly with a high temperature, a dry hacking cough, a pounding headache and aching all over his body. Which infection is most likely?

UN1984.presentation: Mild Jaundice In A Well Newborn
UN1984.stem: Mild jaundice develops in an otherwise well 4-day-old infant, with blood tests showing mostly unconjugated bilirubin. What is the most likely explanation?

A previously well 25-year-old develops chest pain and breathlessness a week after a flu-like illness. He has a raised troponin and ECG changes, but coronary angiography shows normal coronary arteries, and an echocardiogram reveals impaired left ventricular function. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A term boy who was small for his dates is examined on his second day of life. He has a rash of pinpoint purple spots, a palpable liver and spleen, and a small head circumference. He has failed the newborn hearing screen in both ears. His mother recalls a mild flu-like illness in the middle of the pregnancy.

Which congenital infection is the most likely cause?

UN1984.presentation: Troponin as a marker of myocardial injury
UN1984.stem: A 46-year-old man comes to the emergency department with sharp central chest pain that started three days after a flu-like illness. The pain eases when he leans forward. His troponin is raised, and a junior colleague says this proves he has had a heart attack. Which statement about troponin is correct?
UN1984.correct_answer: A raised level shows myocardial injury but does not by itself identify the cause

UN1984.stem:
A 23-year-old man has central chest pain and breathlessness 10 days after a flu-like illness. His ECG shows widespread ST-segment changes and his troponin is raised. CT coronary angiography shows normal coronary arteries. Echocardiography shows mildly reduced left ventricular function. He is haemodynamically stable.

Which investigation is most appropriate next?
A heavy drinker develops jaundice, fever and a tender, enlarged liver. What should be considered?

A 29-year-old woman attends the emergency department with two days of central chest discomfort and palpitations. Ten days earlier she had a flu-like illness with aching muscles and a temperature. She is tachycardic with normal oxygen saturation. The ECG shows sinus tachycardia with widespread T-wave inversion, troponin is raised, and echocardiography shows global reduction in left ventricular contraction. Urgent coronary angiography reveals no stenosis, occlusion or dissection. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN1987.presentation: STI Screening in an Asymptomatic Patient
UN1987.stem: A 27-year-old woman who has recently started a new sexual relationship asks whether she should have a sexual health screen even though she has no symptoms. What is the most appropriate response?
UN1987.correct_answer: Discuss appropriate testing according to sexual history and risk

UN1987.stem: A 26-year-old woman has a positive HIV test at a sexual health clinic during routine screening. She feels well and has no symptoms. Her CD4 count is within the normal range and her viral load is moderately raised. She asks whether she can wait a few years before taking any medication. What is the most appropriate advice?
UN1987.correct_answer: Offer antiretroviral therapy now, whatever her CD4 count

UN1987.stem:
A 29-year-old woman has a reactive fourth-generation HIV test confirmed at the sexual health clinic. Before discussing treatment and the need for prophylaxis against opportunistic infections, the team wants to know how far her immune system has been damaged.

Which blood test gives this information?

A 28-year-old man presents with a 10-day history of fever, myalgia, sore throat, and a maculopapular rash. He is otherwise well. He had unprotected sexual intercourse with a new partner 4 weeks ago. He is concerned about HIV. You perform a 4th-generation HIV test (antigen/antibody combination). The test comes back negative. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN1987.correct_answer: Order an HIV viral load (PCR) test now

UN1987.presentation: Early syphilis with penicillin anaphylaxis — alternative antibiotic
UN1987.stem: A 34-year-old man is diagnosed with secondary syphilis in a sexual health clinic. He has a documented history of anaphylaxis to amoxicillin. He has no neurological, eye or ear symptoms and his HIV test is negative. Which antibiotic is the most appropriate alternative to penicillin?

UN1987.presentation: Rationale for Partner Notification in Gonorrhoea
UN1987.stem: A patient is diagnosed with gonorrhoea, and the sexual health clinic asks whether their recent partners can be contacted and offered testing. Why is partner notification important?
UN1987.correct_answer: To identify and treat contacts and reduce onward transmission

UN1987.presentation: Communicating the limitations of a negative test
UN1987.stem:
A 62-year-old man returns a home faecal immunochemical test through the bowel cancer screening programme and receives a normal result. He has no bowel symptoms. At a GP appointment for another problem, he asks whether this means he definitely cannot have bowel cancer.

What is the best response?
UN1987.correct_answer: Explain it lowers but does not exclude the risk of cancer, and say which symptoms to report

UN1987.stem: A public health doctor is comparing the same rapid chlamydia test used in two settings: a sexual health clinic, where the infection is common among people tested, and a community screening programme, where it is much less common. The test's sensitivity and specificity are the same in both settings. Compared with the community programme, how does the probability that a positive result is a true positive differ in the sexual health clinic?

UN2068.stem: A woman has a thin, grey-white vaginal discharge with a fishy odour but no itch or soreness. The vaginal pH is raised (>4.5) and 'clue cells' are seen on microscopy. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN2068.presentation: Vulvovaginal candidiasis in pregnancy — treatment choice
UN2068.stem: A 27-year-old woman who is 24 weeks pregnant presents to her GP with vulval itching and a thick white vaginal discharge. Examination shows vulval erythema and typical curd-like discharge, and vulvovaginal candidiasis is diagnosed. She has no other symptoms. Which treatment is most appropriate?
A woman presents with pain on passing urine, frequent voiding and suprapubic discomfort, with no vaginal discharge and no fever. What is the likely diagnosis?
Ten days after a vaginal delivery, a woman presents with heavy, offensive-smelling vaginal bleeding, lower abdominal pain, fever and a tender uterus. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A 27-year-old woman complains of an itchy vulva and a bubbly, yellow-green discharge, and testing her vaginal secretions shows an unusually high pH. Which diagnosis best fits?

A 29-year-old woman who is 38 weeks pregnant has an intrauterine fetal death confirmed on ultrasound. For the past day she has noticed a foul-smelling, watery vaginal discharge. Her temperature is 38.9°C, heart rate 122 beats per minute and blood pressure 100/62 mmHg.

What is the most appropriate management?
UN2068.correct_answer: Give intravenous broad-spectrum antibiotics and expedite birth on the labour ward

UN2068.stem:
A 27-year-old woman has a 1-week history of a thin, grey vaginal discharge with a fishy smell, worse after intercourse. She is not pregnant and has no itch or soreness. Vaginal pH is 5.5 and microscopy shows clue cells. Chlamydia and gonorrhoea tests are negative. She would like treatment.

Which treatment is most appropriate?

A 61-year-old woman sees her GP with burning and itching around the vaginal entrance and pain during sex for the past year. She has had no vaginal bleeding or discharge. On examination the vaginal walls are pale, smooth and dry, with loss of the normal folds, and the vulval skin is of normal colour without white patches. What is the most likely diagnosis and appropriate treatment?
UN2068.correct_answer: Atrophic vaginitis — vaginal oestrogen with moisturisers and lubricants

UN2317.stem: A pregnant woman is exposed to a confirmed case of rubella. Why does this matter clinically?
UN2317.correct_answer: Maternal infection can cause congenital rubella syndrome in the baby

UN2317.stem: A 29-year-old woman who is 20 weeks pregnant was exposed to a child with a rash illness. Her blood tests show no evidence of current or past rubella infection, and she has no record of ever receiving MMR vaccine. She is well and asks how she can be protected against rubella in future. Which is the most appropriate plan for her vaccination?

A 27-year-old woman who is 10 weeks pregnant sees her GP. She is well. She has a pet cat and has read that cats can spread an infection that harms the baby. She asks for a blood test to check whether she is infected.

What is the most appropriate advice?
UN2317.correct_answer: Avoid cat litter and eat only well-cooked meat

UN2317.presentation: Lower urinary tract infection in pregnancy
UN2317.stem:
A 24-year-old woman who is 14 weeks pregnant attends her GP with two days of stinging when she passes urine and a need to go every hour or so. She has no temperature, loin pain or vaginal discharge and is otherwise well.

What is the most appropriate management?
UN2317.correct_answer: Send a midstream urine culture and start a suitable antibiotic immediately

UN2317.stem: A 24-year-old woman attends her GP the day after returning from a trip to rural India. Three days ago a stray cat scratched her forearm hard enough to draw blood. She washed the wound with bottled water, and the cat ran off. She feels well and the scratch is healing without signs of infection. Which is the best management?
UN2317.correct_answer: Urgent risk assessment for rabies post-exposure prophylaxis

UN2317.presentation: Aspirin Avoidance in Childhood Viral Illness
UN2317.stem: A worried parent asks why the pharmacist refused to sell aspirin for her 7-year-old son's chickenpox-related fever and recommended paracetamol instead. What is the pharmacist most likely concerned about?

A 35-year-old lorry driver is diagnosed with epilepsy following a first seizure. He states he will not inform the DVLA and will continue driving. The doctor is concerned about public safety. What is the most appropriate action?
UN2317.correct_answer: Explain his legal duty to tell the DVLA; if he continues to drive, inform the DVLA

UN2317.presentation: Antimicrobial resistance as a public-health concern
UN2317.stem: At a practice meeting, the prescribing data for a GP surgery show far more antibiotic prescriptions than neighbouring practices, mostly for coughs and sore throats. A new receptionist asks why the integrated care board is so concerned about this. What is the main public-health reason for limiting unnecessary antibiotic use?
UN2317.correct_answer: Antibiotic exposure selects for resistant bacteria that then spread in the community

UN2318.stem: A pregnant woman is exposed to a confirmed case of rubella. Why does this matter clinically?
UN2318.correct_answer: Maternal infection can cause congenital rubella syndrome in the baby

UN2318.stem:
A term boy who was small for his dates is examined on his second day of life. He has a rash of pinpoint purple spots, a palpable liver and spleen, and a small head circumference. He has failed the newborn hearing screen in both ears. His mother recalls a mild flu-like illness in the middle of the pregnancy.

Which congenital infection is the most likely cause?

UN2318.presentation: Unilateral Foul Nasal Discharge in a Child
UN2318.stem: A 3-year-old is brought in because of a persistent, foul-smelling discharge coming from only one nostril. What should be considered first?

UN2318.presentation: Recurrent Facial Pain With Nasal Discharge
UN2318.stem: A 39-year-old woman has recurring bouts of facial pain, a blocked nose and thick nasal discharge lasting several days whenever she catches a cold. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-month-old boy who was born in another country is seen by the paediatric team. He failed his hearing tests, has a heart murmur from a patent ductus arteriosus and has bilateral cataracts. His mother remembers having a rash and swollen neck glands in the first weeks of pregnancy.

Which maternal infection is the most likely cause?

A term baby boy is 12 hours old on the postnatal ward. During labour his mother developed a fever and was given intravenous antibiotics for suspected infection of the membranes and amniotic fluid. The midwife is now concerned because he is grunting, feeding poorly and his temperature has been unstable. His capillary blood glucose is normal.

Which condition must be assumed until proven otherwise?

A 40-year-old woman has had nasal blockage, facial pressure and a reduced sense of smell continuously for the past four months, with no clear improvement. Which diagnosis is most consistent with this presentation?
A 28-year-old otherwise healthy woman develops facial pressure, nasal blockage and thick nasal discharge for three days, along with mild fatigue. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN2323.stem: A patient attends with a deep, dirty puncture wound from a garden fork. Their tetanus immunisation history is uncertain/incomplete. What is the most appropriate management regarding tetanus?
UN2323.correct_answer: Tetanus-containing vaccine and tetanus immunoglobulin, with wound care

UN2323.presentation: Dirty Wound with Uncertain Tetanus History
UN2323.stem: A man attends after standing on a rusty nail. He completed his childhood vaccination schedule but cannot recall whether he has had any tetanus boosters as an adult. What is the key principle guiding tetanus prophylaxis decisions?
UN2323.correct_answer: Both the nature of the wound and the patient's vaccination history determine the appropriate management

UN2323.stem: A patient attends a few hours after a cat bite to the hand, which is deep with puncture wounds. The wound is not obviously infected yet. Besides wound cleaning, what is the most appropriate management?

A 67-year-old woman presents to an urgent treatment centre after puncturing her palm on a rusty garden fork while spreading manure. The wound is deep and contaminated with soil. She grew up abroad and does not know which vaccinations she has had. Which infection should particularly guide decisions about vaccination and immunoglobulin?

A 50-year-old gardener attends a minor injuries unit after a rusty garden fork went through the sole of his boot into his foot. The puncture is deep and soil was found in it. It has now been irrigated and cleaned. Apart from wound care, what else should be assessed?
UN2323.correct_answer: Tetanus vaccination history and need for prophylaxis

UN2323.presentation: Gas gangrene after a contaminated wound
UN2323.stem:
A 46-year-old gardener drove a garden fork deep into his right thigh while turning a manure heap. The puncture wound was cleaned and closed with sutures at an urgent treatment centre. Thirty-six hours later he is brought to the emergency department with severe thigh pain that seems far worse than the wound looks. The thigh is tense and swollen, the skin is bronze and purple with dark fluid-filled blisters, and thin, foul-smelling fluid is leaking between the sutures. Crackling can be felt under the skin. His temperature is 39.1°C, heart rate 132 bpm and blood pressure 88/50 mmHg. An X-ray shows gas tracking through the muscles.

What is the most appropriate management?
UN2323.correct_answer: IV antibiotics and emergency surgical debridement

UN2323.presentation: Valproate and conception planning in bipolar disorder
UN2323.stem: At a psychiatry outpatient clinic, a 28-year-old woman whose bipolar disorder is well controlled on valproate says that she and her husband would like to try for a baby next year. She uses contraception at present. What is the key issue to discuss with her?
UN2323.correct_answer: Valproate carries a high risk of birth defects and developmental disorders in the child

UN2323.stem: A 20-year-old woman phones her GP surgery for advice. She has norovirus and vomited about an hour after taking her combined contraceptive pill this morning. She has been taking the pill correctly for a year and had unprotected sex two days ago. What is the key issue with today's pill?
UN2323.correct_answer: The pill may not have been absorbed, so contraceptive cover may be reduced

UN2422.stem: A patient with a persistent cough, weight loss and night sweats is being investigated for possible active pulmonary tuberculosis. Which investigation is especially important for microbiological confirmation?
A patient is diagnosed with active pulmonary tuberculosis. What is the most appropriate standard initial drug regimen?
UN2422.correct_answer: Rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol, with pyridoxine

UN2422.stem: A 46-year-old man living in a homeless hostel sees the visiting GP. For two months he has had a productive cough, occasionally with streaks of blood, and he wakes drenched in sweat most nights. His trousers have become loose. Another resident of the hostel was recently started on a long course of treatment for a chest infection. Which diagnosis is most likely?

A 52-year-old man living in a homeless hostel attends a walk-in centre with two months of cough, occasionally bringing up streaks of blood. He wakes drenched in sweat most nights, feels feverish in the evenings and his trousers have become loose. A fellow resident was admitted to hospital with tuberculosis last month. He smokes 15 cigarettes a day. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old man who works as a bus driver is diagnosed with sputum smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis after months of cough and weight loss. His wife, who shares his bedroom, is referred to the TB service for contact screening.

By which route is she most likely to have been exposed?
UN2422.correct_answer: Inhaling droplet nuclei released when he coughs

UN2422.presentation: Infection control for suspected C. difficile
UN2422.stem: A 76-year-old man in a four-bed bay on an orthopaedic ward has developed three episodes of unexplained loose stool overnight after recent antibiotics. A stool sample has been sent for C. difficile testing. The nurse in charge asks what infection-control measures are needed now. What is the most appropriate advice?
UN2422.correct_answer: Side-room isolation, gloves and apron, and handwashing with soap and water

UN2422.stem: A 33-year-old nurse who works on a neonatal unit is diagnosed with sputum smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis after investigation of two months of cough and weight loss. The respiratory team is about to start treatment. Apart from starting treatment, what is the most appropriate action for the diagnosing doctor?
UN2422.correct_answer: Notify the local health protection team so contact tracing can begin

UN2422.presentation: Infection Control in Suspected Meningococcal Disease
UN2422.stem: A 4-year-old boy is brought to the paediatric emergency department with a high fever, lethargy and a spreading non-blanching purpuric rash on his legs. Intravenous ceftriaxone is given immediately and he is to be admitted. A nurse asks which infection control precautions staff should use while caring for him. What is the most appropriate answer?
UN2422.correct_answer: Droplet precautions in a single room

UN2487.stem: What is the usual mode of transmission for hepatitis A?

A traveller returns from a region with poor sanitation and develops malaise, nausea, jaundice and right-upper-quadrant discomfort. Hepatitis A is confirmed. What is the most appropriate description and management?
A patient with acute hepatitis has the following serology: HBsAg POSITIVE, anti-HBc IgM POSITIVE, anti-HBs NEGATIVE. How is this best interpreted?
Through which route can hepatitis B be transmitted?
UN2487.correct_answer: Exposure to infected blood or body fluids

UN2487.stem:
Twenty pupils and two teachers fall ill with vomiting and watery diarrhoea during a school camping trip. The toilet block had no soap, and the same tap was used for drinking and washing up. The environmental health officer asks the visiting doctor how the infection most likely spread.

Which route is most likely?
A heavy drinker develops jaundice, fever and a tender, enlarged liver. What should be considered?
Which of the following is a recognised and important route by which hepatitis B virus spreads between people?
UN2487.correct_answer: Exposure to infected blood or sexual contact

UN2487.presentation: Mild Jaundice In A Well Newborn
UN2487.stem: Mild jaundice develops in an otherwise well 4-day-old infant, with blood tests showing mostly unconjugated bilirubin. What is the most likely explanation?

UN2488.stem: A traveller preparing for a trip to a country where hepatitis A is endemic has never been vaccinated against it. What is the main reason to offer hepatitis A vaccination before departure?
UN2488.correct_answer: It reduces the risk of acquiring hepatitis A infection

UN2488.stem: A patient with acute hepatitis has the following serology: HBsAg POSITIVE, anti-HBc IgM POSITIVE, anti-HBs NEGATIVE. How is this best interpreted?
A heavy drinker develops jaundice, fever and a tender, enlarged liver. What should be considered?
Long-term infection that slowly progresses towards fibrosis and cirrhosis is a recognised feature of which hepatitis virus?
What is the usual mode of transmission for hepatitis A?
Through which route can hepatitis B be transmitted?
UN2488.correct_answer: Exposure to infected blood or body fluids

UN2488.stem: A 45-year-old woman presents with fatigue and jaundice. Her ALT is 350, she has a positive antinuclear antibody and anti-smooth-muscle antibody, and a raised IgG. Viral hepatitis serology is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A traveller returns from a region with poor sanitation and develops malaise, nausea, jaundice and right-upper-quadrant discomfort. Hepatitis A is confirmed. What is the most appropriate description and management?

UN2702.presentation: Fever without a source — blood cultures before antibiotics
UN2702.stem: A 63-year-old man is admitted with 3 weeks of intermittent fevers, night sweats and fatigue. He had a dental extraction 6 weeks ago. Temperature is 38.6°C, blood pressure 128/76 mmHg and he is alert. There is a new soft pansystolic murmur at the apex. Urinalysis shows microscopic haematuria. Chest X-ray is normal. He has not received any antibiotics. Which is the most appropriate next investigation?
UN2702.correct_answer: Three blood culture sets from separate sites

UN2702.stem: You are about to treat someone for probable infective endocarditis, and they are not acutely unwell. Which test should be organised before the first dose of antibiotics goes in?
UN2702.correct_answer: Taking multiple sets of blood cultures

UN2702.presentation: Suspected septic olecranon bursitis — key investigation
UN2702.stem: A 50-year-old roofer attends the emergency department with a 2-day history of a hot, red, very tender swelling over the tip of his right elbow after grazing it at work. His temperature is 38.1°C. He can fully flex and extend the elbow with only mild discomfort at the extremes of movement. Septic olecranon bursitis is suspected. Which investigation is most important before antibiotics are started?
UN2702.correct_answer: Bursal aspiration for Gram stain, culture and crystals

UN2702.stem: A 68-year-old woman who had a mechanical aortic valve replacement four years ago is admitted with three weeks of intermittent fevers, sweats, fatigue and weight loss. There is a new early diastolic murmur, small haemorrhages under the conjunctivae, and her urine dipstick shows blood. She is alert, with a blood pressure of 128/74 mmHg and no signs of sepsis or heart failure. What is the most important initial investigation?
UN2702.correct_answer: At least three sets of blood cultures from separate venepunctures before antibiotics

UN2702.stem: A 50-year-old man with a native aortic valve has definite infective endocarditis. Blood cultures grow Streptococcus viridans (penicillin-sensitive). He is haemodynamically stable with no complications. What is the most appropriate antibiotic regimen?
UN2702.correct_answer: IV benzylpenicillin or IV amoxicillin for 4 weeks

UN2702.stem: Which patient carries the highest risk of infective endocarditis?
UN2702.correct_answer: A patient with a prosthetic heart valve

UN2702.stem: A 50-year-old man with infective endocarditis on appropriate IV antibiotics develops worsening breathlessness with new severe mitral regurgitation and signs of heart failure. Echocardiography shows a large vegetation and valve destruction. What is the most appropriate next step?
