A 54-year-old man with a mechanical aortic valve is referred to the acute medical unit by his GP after ten days of fevers, aches and fatigue. On arrival he is alert, his observations are stable and there is no obvious source of infection. The team suspects prosthetic valve endocarditis. Which investigation should be done before any antibiotic is given?
UN2702.correct_answer: Three sets of blood cultures from separate venepunctures

UN2766.stem: A healthcare worker sustains a needlestick injury from a needle used on a patient with known untreated HIV. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
UN2766.correct_answer: Wash, risk-assess and start HIV PEP as soon as possible

UN2766.stem:
A theatre nurse attends the occupational health department two days after blood from an HIV-positive patient splashed into her eye during an emergency laparotomy. She rinsed her eye at the time but did not report the incident until today. The source patient had recently stopped antiretroviral therapy and his viral load is detectable.

What should be offered now?
UN2766.correct_answer: A 28-day course of HIV post-exposure prophylaxis started as soon as possible today

UN2766.presentation: Deciding Post-Exposure Management After Hepatitis B Exposure
UN2766.stem: A healthcare assistant is splashed with blood from a patient known to carry hepatitis B. What mainly determines whether post-exposure treatment is required?
UN2766.correct_answer: The assistant's hepatitis B immunity and the type of exposure

UN2766.presentation: Hepatitis B Exposure in an Immune Worker
UN2766.stem: A healthcare worker has a needlestick exposure to blood from a patient with chronic hepatitis B. The worker previously completed the hepatitis B vaccination course and has documented immunity on blood testing. How should this exposure be interpreted?
UN2766.correct_answer: The risk of transmission is substantially reduced by her documented immunity

UN2766.presentation: Measles exposure in pregnancy — post-exposure prophylaxis
UN2766.stem: A 27-year-old woman who is 20 weeks pregnant was in the same room as a child with confirmed measles 3 days ago. She was never vaccinated and has never had measles. She is well. Her measles IgG antibody test is negative. Which is the most appropriate post-exposure prophylaxis?
A woman at 30 weeks' gestation, with no history of chickenpox, has significant household exposure to a child with chickenpox. Her varicella IgG is negative. What is the most appropriate management?

A 24-year-old woman attends her GP the day after returning from a trip to rural India. Three days ago a stray cat scratched her forearm hard enough to draw blood. She washed the wound with bottled water, and the cat ran off. She feels well and the scratch is healing without signs of infection. Which is the best management?
UN2766.correct_answer: Urgent risk assessment for rabies post-exposure prophylaxis

UN2766.stem: A new healthcare worker has no documented evidence of hepatitis B vaccination and is about to begin a role involving regular exposure to blood and body fluids. What is the appropriate approach?
UN2766.correct_answer: Hepatitis B vaccination should be offered based on the individual's occupational risk

UN2815.stem: A 24-year-old woman attends her GP the day after returning from a trip to rural India. Three days ago a stray cat scratched her forearm hard enough to draw blood. She washed the wound with bottled water, and the cat ran off. She feels well and the scratch is healing without signs of infection. Which is the best management?
UN2815.correct_answer: Urgent risk assessment for rabies post-exposure prophylaxis

UN2815.presentation: Measles exposure in pregnancy — post-exposure prophylaxis
UN2815.stem: A 27-year-old woman who is 20 weeks pregnant was in the same room as a child with confirmed measles 3 days ago. She was never vaccinated and has never had measles. She is well. Her measles IgG antibody test is negative. Which is the most appropriate post-exposure prophylaxis?

A patient attends a few hours after a cat bite to the hand, which is deep with puncture wounds. The wound is not obviously infected yet. Besides wound cleaning, what is the most appropriate management?
A woman at 30 weeks' gestation, with no history of chickenpox, has significant household exposure to a child with chickenpox. Her varicella IgG is negative. What is the most appropriate management?

UN2815.presentation: Management of a Knocked-Out Permanent Tooth
UN2815.stem: During a rugby match, a 14-year-old boy is struck in the face and his upper permanent incisor is knocked completely out of its socket. What is the key management principle?

A theatre nurse attends the occupational health department two days after blood from an HIV-positive patient splashed into her eye during an emergency laparotomy. She rinsed her eye at the time but did not report the incident until today. The source patient had recently stopped antiretroviral therapy and his viral load is detectable.

What should be offered now?
UN2815.correct_answer: A 28-day course of HIV post-exposure prophylaxis started as soon as possible today

UN2815.stem: A 27-year-old backpacker is bitten on the hand by a stray dog in a region where rabies is endemic. The wound is contaminated with the animal's saliva. Before any medical assessment can take place, what is the single most important first-aid step?
UN2815.correct_answer: Irrigate and scrub the wound thoroughly with soap and water

UN2815.presentation: Deciding Post-Exposure Management After Hepatitis B Exposure
UN2815.stem: A healthcare assistant is splashed with blood from a patient known to carry hepatitis B. What mainly determines whether post-exposure treatment is required?
UN2815.correct_answer: The assistant's hepatitis B immunity and the type of exposure

UN2873.stem: A woman has a thin, grey-white vaginal discharge with a fishy odour but no itch or soreness. The vaginal pH is raised (>4.5) and 'clue cells' are seen on microscopy. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN2873.presentation: Persistent conjunctivitis in a sexually active adult — investigation
UN2873.stem:
A 23-year-old woman sees her GP with 4 weeks of a red, sticky right eye. A week of chloramphenicol eye drops has not helped. Vision is normal and there is no pain or photophobia. There are follicles on the lower lid conjunctiva and a tender lymph node in front of the right ear. She started a new sexual relationship 3 months ago and has noticed increased vaginal discharge.

Which investigation is most appropriate?
UN2873.correct_answer: Conjunctival swab for chlamydia nucleic acid testing

UN2873.stem: A woman presents with pain on passing urine, frequent voiding and suprapubic discomfort, with no vaginal discharge and no fever. What is the likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old woman has a 1-week history of a thin, grey vaginal discharge with a fishy smell, worse after intercourse. She is not pregnant and has no itch or soreness. Vaginal pH is 5.5 and microscopy shows clue cells. Chlamydia and gonorrhoea tests are negative. She would like treatment.

Which treatment is most appropriate?

UN2873.presentation: Vulvovaginal candidiasis in pregnancy — treatment choice
UN2873.stem: A 27-year-old woman who is 24 weeks pregnant presents to her GP with vulval itching and a thick white vaginal discharge. Examination shows vulval erythema and typical curd-like discharge, and vulvovaginal candidiasis is diagnosed. She has no other symptoms. Which treatment is most appropriate?

UN2873.presentation: Chlamydia testing in women — specimen of choice
UN2873.stem: A 22-year-old woman with no symptoms asks her GP practice for a chlamydia test after starting a relationship with a new partner. She has had vaginal sex only. Which specimen is most appropriate for a chlamydia nucleic acid amplification test?

A 22-year-old woman sees her GP for the third time in four months with burning on passing urine and frequency. Urine samples sent at her last two visits showed white cells but grew no organisms, and her symptoms did not settle with antibiotics for cystitis. She now also mentions a change in vaginal discharge and some bleeding after sex. She has had a new partner in the last six months and they do not use condoms. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN2873.presentation: Gradual Scrotal Pain With Urethral Symptoms
UN2873.stem: A sexually active 25-year-old man develops scrotal swelling and discomfort on the right side that has worsened steadily over three days, along with pain on passing urine and a clear urethral discharge. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN2940.stem: A teenage boy develops a painful, swollen testis several days after his parotid glands swelled up. What complication is this?
Which clinical feature points more towards testicular torsion than epididymo-orchitis?
UN2940.correct_answer: Abrupt onset of intense scrotal pain

UN2940.presentation: Acute Scrotal Pain In A Boy
UN2940.stem: A 12-year-old boy develops sudden, severe scrotal pain and swelling during a football match. On examination the affected testis sits higher than the other side and is extremely tender to touch. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN2940.presentation: Gradual Scrotal Pain With Urethral Symptoms
UN2940.stem: A sexually active 25-year-old man develops scrotal swelling and discomfort on the right side that has worsened steadily over three days, along with pain on passing urine and a clear urethral discharge. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A 17-year-old has acute scrotal pain. Which single feature most favours testicular torsion over epididymo-orchitis and mandates urgent exploration?
UN2940.correct_answer: Absent cremasteric reflex with a high-riding testis and sudden onset

UN2940.stem: On examining a teenage boy with acute testicular pain, which finding would most support a diagnosis of testicular torsion?

A 10-year-old boy presents with acute right-sided scrotal pain for 12 hours. He is systemically well. Examination shows a normal testicular lie, an intact cremasteric reflex, and a small tender blue-black nodule visible through the scrotal skin at the upper pole of the testis. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old university student who was never vaccinated attends an urgent treatment centre. A week ago he had fever and painful swelling below both ears that made chewing difficult. Since yesterday his right testis has become progressively painful and swollen and his temperature has risen again. The testis is enlarged and tender, it lies in a normal position and the cremasteric reflex is present. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

UN2946.stem: A hiker develops a slowly enlarging, painless red patch on the thigh ten days after walking through woodland, where she recalls removing an embedded tick. The lesion is not itchy. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN2946.presentation: Expanding Rash After a Tick Bite
UN2946.stem: A 34-year-old man notices a slowly enlarging red ring-shaped rash on his calf about ten days after a camping trip, during which he recalls pulling off an attached tick. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A walker in a tick-endemic area develops a slowly expanding, red, ring-shaped rash with central clearing (erythema migrans) at the site of a tick bite, with mild flu-like symptoms. What is the most appropriate management?
UN2946.correct_answer: Treat clinically with oral doxycycline (no need to await serology)

UN2946.presentation: Lyme disease facial palsy — antibiotic choice
UN2946.stem: A 38-year-old man has a left lower motor neurone facial palsy that developed 5 weeks after a tick bite in the New Forest. Lyme ELISA and immunoblot are both positive. He has no headache, neck stiffness, confusion, limb weakness or palpitations, and his ECG is normal. He is not allergic to any medicines. Which antibiotic treatment is most appropriate?

UN2946.presentation: Suspected Lyme disease without erythema migrans — first test
UN2946.stem: A 47-year-old woman sees her GP with 3 weeks of fatigue, headache, low-grade fevers and aches that move between different joints. Five weeks ago she removed a tick after a walking holiday in the Scottish Highlands. She has not noticed any rash, and examination shows no rash, no joint swelling and no neurological signs. The GP suspects Lyme disease. Which investigation is most appropriate first?

UN2946.presentation: Crusted Skin Lesion Spreading Among Classmates
UN2946.stem: A child develops a red, swollen, painful skin lesion with golden-coloured surface crusting. Several of his classmates have developed similar lesions recently. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 47-year-old woman went walking in a heathland national park two weeks ago. She now has a red, ring-shaped patch on her thigh that has slowly enlarged over several days, with a paler centre. It is not itchy or scaly. She feels achy and tired. She does not remember being bitten by anything. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 52-year-old woman is seen at her GP surgery. Three weeks ago she went hill walking in the Scottish Highlands and afterwards removed a small tick from her thigh. Over the past week a red patch has slowly spread outwards from the bite site to about the size of her palm, with a paler centre. She feels a little tired but has no neurological or cardiac symptoms. She is not pregnant and has no allergies. What is the most appropriate management?

UN3089.stem:
A 24-year-old man comes to the emergency department on a Sunday morning with a small cut over the knuckle of his right middle finger. He admits he hit someone in the face outside a nightclub the night before. The finger is mildly swollen and painful to bend.

Which injury does this most likely represent?
UN3089.correct_answer: Human bite wound over the knuckle

UN3089.stem: A patient attends a few hours after a cat bite to the hand, which is deep with puncture wounds. The wound is not obviously infected yet. Besides wound cleaning, what is the most appropriate management?

A 19-year-old man is punched on the jaw during a fight. He has pain on chewing and says his teeth no longer meet properly. There is bruising under the tongue and tenderness along the lower jaw.

Which injury should be suspected?
A patient recently diagnosed with Barrett's oesophagus asks why ongoing surveillance endoscopies are recommended. What is the main reason this condition is clinically important?
UN3089.correct_answer: It increases the risk of oesophageal adenocarcinoma

UN3089.presentation: Significance of Erectile Dysfunction as a Vascular Marker
UN3089.stem: A 58-year-old man with multiple cardiovascular risk factors is found to have erectile dysfunction. Why might this symptom be clinically important beyond its effect on sexual function?
UN3089.correct_answer: It may reflect underlying vascular disease

UN3089.stem:
A 9-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department 45 minutes after a neighbour's dog bit his forearm. There are several ragged puncture marks with saliva and bits of grass in them. The bleeding has stopped and he can move his fingers normally.

What is the most important initial step in managing the wound?
UN3089.correct_answer: Explore, irrigate and clean the wound thoroughly

UN3089.presentation: Cervical screening — persistent high-risk HPV with negative cytology
UN3089.stem: A 38-year-old woman's cervical screening sample is positive for high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) with negative cytology. This is her third consecutive screening test, each 12 months apart, to show high-risk HPV with negative cytology. She has no symptoms and her cervix looked normal when the sample was taken. What is the most appropriate next step?

UN3089.presentation: Antibiotic Request for a Viral Infection
UN3089.stem: A patient with a straightforward viral upper respiratory tract infection, and no features suggesting bacterial infection, asks their doctor for antibiotics. What is the most appropriate response?
UN3089.correct_answer: Explain why antibiotics are unlikely to help; give symptomatic advice and safety-netting

UN3090.stem: A patient attends a few hours after a cat bite to the hand, which is deep with puncture wounds. The wound is not obviously infected yet. Besides wound cleaning, what is the most appropriate management?
A patient attends with a deep, dirty puncture wound from a garden fork. Their tetanus immunisation history is uncertain/incomplete. What is the most appropriate management regarding tetanus?
UN3090.correct_answer: Tetanus-containing vaccine and tetanus immunoglobulin, with wound care

UN3090.stem: A 50-year-old gardener attends a minor injuries unit after a rusty garden fork went through the sole of his boot into his foot. The puncture is deep and soil was found in it. It has now been irrigated and cleaned. Apart from wound care, what else should be assessed?
UN3090.correct_answer: Tetanus vaccination history and need for prophylaxis

UN3090.stem:
A 9-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department 45 minutes after a neighbour's dog bit his forearm. There are several ragged puncture marks with saliva and bits of grass in them. The bleeding has stopped and he can move his fingers normally.

What is the most important initial step in managing the wound?
UN3090.correct_answer: Explore, irrigate and clean the wound thoroughly

UN3090.stem:
A 33-year-old railway engineer touched a high-voltage overhead cable. He has a small charred wound on his right palm and another on the sole of his right foot, with little visible skin damage in between. His right forearm is becoming tense and painful, and his urine is dark.

Why is his injury likely to be far worse than the skin wounds suggest?
UN3090.correct_answer: Current travels through deep tissues along its path

UN3090.stem: A 47-year-old woman went walking in a heathland national park two weeks ago. She now has a red, ring-shaped patch on her thigh that has slowly enlarged over several days, with a paler centre. It is not itchy or scaly. She feels achy and tired. She does not remember being bitten by anything. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3090.presentation: Gas gangrene after a contaminated wound
UN3090.stem:
A 46-year-old gardener drove a garden fork deep into his right thigh while turning a manure heap. The puncture wound was cleaned and closed with sutures at an urgent treatment centre. Thirty-six hours later he is brought to the emergency department with severe thigh pain that seems far worse than the wound looks. The thigh is tense and swollen, the skin is bronze and purple with dark fluid-filled blisters, and thin, foul-smelling fluid is leaking between the sutures. Crackling can be felt under the skin. His temperature is 39.1°C, heart rate 132 bpm and blood pressure 88/50 mmHg. An X-ray shows gas tracking through the muscles.

What is the most appropriate management?
UN3090.correct_answer: IV antibiotics and emergency surgical debridement

UN3090.stem: A patient develops a firm, raised scar after ear piercing that continues to grow well beyond the original puncture site. What is this type of scar called?

UN3220.stem: A traveller returns from a region with poor sanitation and develops malaise, nausea, jaundice and right-upper-quadrant discomfort. Hepatitis A is confirmed. What is the most appropriate description and management?
Through which route can hepatitis B be transmitted?
UN3220.correct_answer: Exposure to infected blood or body fluids

UN3220.stem: What is the usual mode of transmission for hepatitis A?
Which of the following is a recognised and important route by which hepatitis B virus spreads between people?
UN3220.correct_answer: Exposure to infected blood or sexual contact

UN3220.stem: A heavy drinker develops jaundice, fever and a tender, enlarged liver. What should be considered?
Long-term infection that slowly progresses towards fibrosis and cirrhosis is a recognised feature of which hepatitis virus?
Minutes after eating a snack containing nuts, a 9-year-old girl develops a widespread itchy rash, swollen lips and audible wheeze. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3220.presentation: Mild Jaundice In A Well Newborn
UN3220.stem: Mild jaundice develops in an otherwise well 4-day-old infant, with blood tests showing mostly unconjugated bilirubin. What is the most likely explanation?

UN3224.stem: A 23-year-old woman sees her GP with 5 days of bilateral lower abdominal pain, deep dyspareunia and an abnormal vaginal discharge. She uses condoms inconsistently and her periods are irregular. Her temperature is 37.6°C and she is otherwise well. Bimanual examination shows cervical motion tenderness and bilateral adnexal tenderness. The GP suspects pelvic inflammatory disease. Which investigation should be performed first?

A 22-year-old woman presents with bilateral lower abdominal pain, deep dyspareunia, and a mucopurulent vaginal discharge. Bimanual examination reveals cervical motion tenderness and bilateral adnexal tenderness. She is afebrile. What is the most appropriate management?
UN3224.correct_answer: Outpatient antibiotics — IM ceftriaxone plus oral doxycycline and metronidazole

UN3224.stem: A woman presents with pain on passing urine, frequent voiding and suprapubic discomfort, with no vaginal discharge and no fever. What is the likely diagnosis?

A woman has a thin, grey-white vaginal discharge with a fishy odour but no itch or soreness. The vaginal pH is raised (>4.5) and 'clue cells' are seen on microscopy. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old woman attends a sexual health clinic with a week of bilateral lower abdominal pain, pain deep inside during intercourse and bleeding after sex. She has a new sexual partner and they do not use condoms. Her temperature is 37.9°C. On bimanual examination there is tenderness in both adnexa and pain on moving the cervix. A pregnancy test is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3224.presentation: Pelvic inflammatory disease with an intrauterine device
UN3224.stem: A 31-year-old woman has had a copper intrauterine device (IUD) for 3 years. She presents to a sexual health clinic with lower abdominal pain, abnormal discharge and cervical motion tenderness. She is afebrile and systemically well, her pregnancy test is negative and she is diagnosed with mild to moderate pelvic inflammatory disease. Swabs are taken and outpatient antibiotics are started. She wishes to keep the IUD as her contraception. What is the most appropriate management of the IUD?
UN3224.correct_answer: Leave it in place and review her response early

UN3224.presentation: Persistent conjunctivitis in a sexually active adult — investigation
UN3224.stem:
A 23-year-old woman sees her GP with 4 weeks of a red, sticky right eye. A week of chloramphenicol eye drops has not helped. Vision is normal and there is no pain or photophobia. There are follicles on the lower lid conjunctiva and a tender lymph node in front of the right ear. She started a new sexual relationship 3 months ago and has noticed increased vaginal discharge.

Which investigation is most appropriate?
UN3224.correct_answer: Conjunctival swab for chlamydia nucleic acid testing

UN3224.stem: A 24-year-old woman has lower abdominal pain, deep dyspareunia, abnormal discharge and cervical motion tenderness, with a mild fever. What is the most appropriate management?
UN3224.correct_answer: Start empirical antibiotics for PID without waiting for swab results

UN3334.presentation: Crossed Cranial Nerve And Limb Signs
UN3334.stem: A 59-year-old woman suddenly develops double vision, difficulty swallowing and weakness of her right arm and leg together. Which anatomical site could explain this combination of cranial nerve and limb findings?

A 26-year-old woman develops progressive difficulty walking upstairs over several days, two weeks after an episode of diarrhoea. On examination she has symmetrical weakness in both legs with absent reflexes. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3334.presentation: Myasthenia gravis — next test when acetylcholine receptor antibodies are negative
UN3334.stem: A 34-year-old woman is seen in the neurology clinic with a 3-month history of drooping eyelids, double vision and difficulty swallowing, all worse towards the end of the day. She also has fatigable neck weakness. Pupils, reflexes and sensation are normal. Serum acetylcholine receptor antibodies are negative. Which blood test should be requested next?

UN3334.presentation: Progressive Swallowing Difficulty in an Older Smoker
UN3334.stem: A 68-year-old man with a 40-pack-year smoking history and regular heavy alcohol intake reports three months of worsening difficulty swallowing solid food and unintentional weight loss of 6 kg. What serious diagnosis must be excluded?

UN3334.presentation: Dysphagia — alarm feature for oesophageal cancer
UN3334.stem: A 70-year-old man presents with progressive difficulty swallowing solids over 4 months. He now struggles with soft food. He has lost 8 kg. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 71-year-old woman has sudden left-sided weakness together with an upper motor neurone pattern of facial weakness on the right. Which cranial nerve is responsible for producing the facial weakness itself?

UN3334.presentation: Acute urticaria after food without anaphylaxis
UN3334.stem: A 16-year-old girl is brought to a walk-in centre by her friend about an hour after eating prawns at a birthday party. Itchy, raised, pale welts have appeared on her neck, arms and trunk. She is talking in full sentences, has no wheeze, no swelling of her lips or tongue, no difficulty swallowing, no abdominal pain and does not feel faint. Her observations are normal. Which diagnosis is most likely?

A 29-year-old woman develops progressively worsening weakness that starts in her feet and spreads upward, with loss of reflexes, about two weeks after a bout of diarrhoeal illness. Which diagnosis is most likely?

UN3343.stem: A 19-year-old student presents to the GP surgery with a 5-hour history of fever, severe headache, photophobia and neck stiffness, and now a non-blanching petechial rash. She is alert with a blood pressure of 112/70. What is the most appropriate immediate action?
UN3343.correct_answer: Immediate IV (or IM) benzylpenicillin/ceftriaxone and urgent transfer

UN3343.stem:
In late summer, a 22-year-old woman attends the GP surgery with a three-day history of fever, a frontal headache and discomfort looking at light. Her younger brother had a similar illness last week. She is alert, has no rash and no focal signs, and is later confirmed to have viral meningitis.

Which group of viruses is the most common cause in the UK?

A 26-year-old man is reviewed on the acute medical unit with two days of headache, dislike of bright light and pain on bending his neck forward. He is orientated, his blood pressure and heart rate are normal, and there are no focal signs. A lumbar puncture is performed. The CSF is clear, with a raised white cell count made up mainly of lymphocytes, a normal glucose ratio and a mildly raised protein.

Which diagnosis best fits these findings?

UN3343.presentation: Fever, Neck Stiffness and Non-Blanching Rash
UN3343.stem: A university student presents with fever, a severe headache, neck stiffness and a rash that does not fade under pressure. She is becoming increasingly drowsy. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old woman has fever, severe headache, neck stiffness and photophobia, and is becoming drowsy. She has a non-blanching purpuric rash. Suspected meningococcal meningitis with septicaemia. What is the most appropriate immediate management?

A man with advanced HIV (CD4 count 50 cells/µL) and poor treatment adherence presents with headache, fever and a focal neurological deficit. Contrast CT of the brain shows multiple RING-ENHANCING lesions. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 38-year-old woman who stopped her antiretroviral therapy two years ago is brought in by her sister. For the past three weeks she has had a slowly worsening headache, low-grade fevers and, more recently, episodes of confusion. Her last CD4 count was very low. There is minimal neck stiffness and no focal weakness.

Which opportunistic infection should be considered first?

A 14-year-old boy who has not received any MMR vaccines is brought to the emergency department. A week ago he developed painful swelling of both parotid glands, and over the last day he has had a worsening headache, has vomited several times and finds bright light uncomfortable. He is alert, his neck is stiff on flexion and there is no rash.

Which complication is most likely?

UN3344.stem: A 29-year-old woman with no past medical history comes in febrile, with a pounding headache, increasingly muddled, and has had several fits affecting one side of her body. Which diagnosis needs to be high on the list?

A 59-year-old man is brought in by his wife because of a two-year change in personality. He has become disinhibited, makes socially inappropriate comments, shows little empathy, and is increasingly apathetic. His memory for recent events is relatively well preserved. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A young adult has a movement disorder (tremor and dystonia), personality change and deranged liver function. Slit-lamp examination shows brown rings at the corneal margin. What is the most appropriate diagnostic test?

A 19-year-old student presents with fever, confusion and hypotension. There is a rapidly spreading non-blanching purpuric rash. Neck stiffness is absent. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
UN3344.correct_answer: Immediate IV ceftriaxone (do not delay for investigations)

UN3344.stem: A young adult has fever, headache, confusion and a witnessed seizure, with altered behaviour but no purpuric rash. What is the most appropriate immediate treatment while investigations proceed?

A previously well young woman has fever, confusion, a falling platelet count, anaemia with red cell fragments (schistocytes) on the film, and a rising creatinine. Her clotting screen is normal. What is the most appropriate urgent treatment?

A 38-year-old man sees his GP. His father, now 58, was recently diagnosed with Huntington disease after developing involuntary jerky movements and personality change. The man has two young children and wants to understand how the condition is passed on in families. Which statement about its inheritance is accurate?
UN3344.correct_answer: It is autosomal dominant, so a child of an affected parent has a 1 in 2 chance of inheriting it

UN3344.stem: A 74-year-old woman has insidious, gradually progressive memory loss over 2 years. She forgets recent conversations, repeats questions, misplaces items and has word-finding difficulty. There is no stepwise deterioration, no early visual hallucinations or parkinsonism, no prominent early personality change, and no gait disturbance. Neurological examination is normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3490.presentation: Return to Contact Sport After Glandular Fever
UN3490.stem: A 20-year-old rugby player has just been diagnosed with infectious mononucleosis and wants to know why he should avoid contact sport while he recovers. What is the main risk being avoided?
A 17-year-old footballer recovering from confirmed glandular fever asks his doctor when he can safely return to training and matches. Why is he advised to avoid contact sport for several weeks?

A 17-year-old girl who plays rugby for her school has a week of fever, a very sore throat and swollen glands at the back of her neck. A heterophile antibody (Monospot) test is positive. She feels a little better and asks her GP whether she can play in a match next weekend. What is the main reason to advise her against this?
A 19-year-old has a sore throat, fever, marked cervical lymphadenopathy and lethargy, with atypical lymphocytes on the blood film. Which is the most appropriate advice?
UN3490.correct_answer: Avoid amoxicillin and contact sports (risk of rash and splenic rupture)

UN3490.stem: A 16-year-old boy has infectious mononucleosis confirmed on a blood test. He has a sore throat and marked tiredness but is eating and drinking, and he has no breathing difficulty or abdominal pain. His mother asks when he can go back to school. What is the most appropriate advice?
UN3490.correct_answer: Return to school as soon as he feels well enough

UN3490.stem: A 19-year-old develops fever, marked exudative tonsillitis, cervical lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly. After being given amoxicillin by another clinician, a florid widespread maculopapular rash appears. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3490.presentation: Sudden Posterior Ankle Pain During Sport
UN3490.stem: During a sprint at a 5-a-side football match, a 35-year-old feels a sudden sharp pain at the back of his ankle, as though someone had struck him there, and finds he cannot push off with that foot afterwards. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old man who plays football for a semi-professional team is about to be discharged after a 4-day admission with myocarditis following a viral illness. His chest pain has settled, troponin is falling and he has had no arrhythmias. He asks whether he can return to full training next week.

What is the most appropriate advice?
UN3490.correct_answer: Avoid competitive sport until cardiology review

UN3587.stem: A 68-year-old man develops a painful cluster of blistering lesions across the left side of his forehead and upper eyelid, sparing the tip of his nose. Which complication is particularly important to consider?

UN3587.presentation: Crusted Skin Lesion Spreading Among Classmates
UN3587.stem: A child develops a red, swollen, painful skin lesion with golden-coloured surface crusting. Several of his classmates have developed similar lesions recently. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3587.presentation: Recurrent Painful Vesicles Around the Mouth
UN3587.stem: A patient reports that every time they are run down with a cold or under stress, they develop a cluster of small painful blisters at the corner of the mouth, which then crust over and heal. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3587.presentation: Painful Band of Vesicles on the Trunk
UN3587.stem: A 74-year-old reports several days of burning pain over the right side of the chest, and now has a cluster of blisters confined to a single band following that side. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3587.presentation: Hepatitis B Exposure in an Immune Worker
UN3587.stem: A healthcare worker has a needlestick exposure to blood from a patient with chronic hepatitis B. The worker previously completed the hepatitis B vaccination course and has documented immunity on blood testing. How should this exposure be interpreted?
UN3587.correct_answer: The risk of transmission is substantially reduced by her documented immunity

UN3587.presentation: Contact Lens Wearer with Painful Eye
UN3587.stem: A 24-year-old woman who wears soft contact lenses develops a painful, photophobic eye with a visible white opacity on the cornea. What diagnosis must be urgently considered?
A patient with skin psoriasis develops a painful, swollen finger that is diffusely swollen ('sausage digit', dactylitis), with nail pitting and onycholysis. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3587.presentation: Painful Swelling at the Nail Fold
UN3587.stem: A regular nail-biter develops a painful, red, swollen area at the side of the nail on their index finger over the past two days. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3588.stem: A 70-year-old man is on a medical ward being treated for pneumonia, which caused high fevers for the first two days. He tells the doctor that his upper lip began tingling and burning yesterday, and now a crop of small, painful vesicles has appeared at the same spot, where he says 'fever blisters' have come up occasionally over the years. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A primary school teacher aged 26 rings her surgery's nurse triage line, back from a week of skiing at altitude. On Saturday a prickling, burning sensation began on the right side of her upper lip, where the red margin meets the skin; by Monday a crop of pinhead blisters filled with clear fluid had erupted there and is sore. This has occurred in the same place two or three times a year since her teens, often during busy school terms or after a cold. Which diagnosis is most likely?

UN3588.presentation: Recurrent Painful Vesicles Around the Mouth
UN3588.stem: A patient reports that every time they are run down with a cold or under stress, they develop a cluster of small painful blisters at the corner of the mouth, which then crust over and heal. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 31-year-old woman tells her GP that a few times a year she feels tingling and burning at the edge of her upper lip, and within a day a small cluster of tense, painful blisters appears in the same place. They crust over and heal in about ten days. Episodes tend to follow skiing holidays and sometimes come before her period. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old woman with recurrent cold sores attends at the onset of a familiar tingling sensation on her lip, before any vesicles have appeared. She wants treatment to shorten the episode. She is otherwise well and not immunocompromised. What is the most appropriate treatment?
UN3588.correct_answer: Topical aciclovir 5% cream 5 times daily for 5 days

UN3588.presentation: Crusted Skin Lesion Spreading Among Classmates
UN3588.stem: A child develops a red, swollen, painful skin lesion with golden-coloured surface crusting. Several of his classmates have developed similar lesions recently. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old man comes back from a week of skiing and books a GP appointment. Two days ago a sore, stinging patch appeared on the edge of his lower lip, and it has turned into a cluster of small clear blisters sitting on a red base. He has had similar spots after sunny holidays before. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 38-year-old woman asks a community pharmacist for advice about a sore spot near the corner of her upper lip. It appears most months in the days before her period, starts as a few small clustered blisters that weep and crust, and clears on its own within about a week. Today the blisters are on a red, tender base. Which diagnosis is most likely?

UN3739.stem: A 19-year-old woman attends her GP three days after being given amoxicillin at a walk-in centre for a sore throat. She has a week of fever, marked fatigue and tender swollen glands at the back of her neck, and a palpable spleen tip. Since yesterday she has had a widespread itchy, flat and slightly raised red (maculopapular) rash on her trunk and limbs, with no wheals. Her lips, mouth and eyes are unaffected and she has no breathing difficulty. What is the most likely explanation for the rash?
UN3739.correct_answer: Aminopenicillin rash in Epstein–Barr virus infection

UN3739.stem: A 19-year-old has a sore throat, fever, marked cervical lymphadenopathy and lethargy, with atypical lymphocytes on the blood film. Which is the most appropriate advice?
UN3739.correct_answer: Avoid amoxicillin and contact sports (risk of rash and splenic rupture)

UN3739.stem: A patient presents with a sore throat, fever, tonsillar exudate and tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy, and reports no cough. According to NICE guidance (NG84), which scoring systems should be used to estimate the likelihood of bacterial infection and guide antibiotic prescribing?

A 19-year-old develops fever, marked exudative tonsillitis, cervical lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly. After being given amoxicillin by another clinician, a florid widespread maculopapular rash appears. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old man with treatment-resistant schizophrenia is started on clozapine. Four weeks later he develops a fever and sore throat. Full blood count shows neutrophils 0.4 × 10⁹/L. What is the most appropriate action?
UN3739.correct_answer: Stop clozapine immediately and refer to haematology

UN3739.presentation: Tender Shin Nodules After Sore Throat
UN3739.stem: A 29-year-old woman develops several tender, red, raised nodules on both shins about two weeks after a streptococcal sore throat. The lesions are firm swellings rather than open sores. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3739.presentation: Sore throat while taking carbimazole — immediate action
UN3739.stem: A 34-year-old woman phones her GP surgery with a 2-day history of sore throat, fever and mouth ulcers. She started carbimazole for Graves disease 6 weeks ago. She sounds unwell but is not short of breath. What is the most appropriate action?
UN3739.correct_answer: Stop carbimazole and check a full blood count today

UN3739.presentation: Haematuria With Hypertension After a Throat Infection
UN3739.stem: Two weeks after a streptococcal sore throat, a 7-year-old develops visibly dark urine, a blood pressure above the normal range for his age, and a rising creatinine. Which syndrome best describes this presentation?

UN3754.stem: A 34-year-old man who has sex with men attends a sexual health clinic with four weeks of a non-itchy, copper-coloured rash over his trunk that also affects the soles of his feet. He has felt feverish, has patchy hair loss and has grey patches inside his mouth. About two months ago he noticed a painless sore near his anus, which healed without treatment. Which infection best explains his presentation?

UN3754.presentation: Early syphilis with penicillin anaphylaxis — alternative antibiotic
UN3754.stem: A 34-year-old man is diagnosed with secondary syphilis in a sexual health clinic. He has a documented history of anaphylaxis to amoxicillin. He has no neurological, eye or ear symptoms and his HIV test is negative. Which antibiotic is the most appropriate alternative to penicillin?
Ten days after starting a new anticonvulsant, a patient develops a widespread rash with areas of skin blistering and painful ulceration of the lips and mouth. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN3754.correct_answer: Stop the suspected drug and refer urgently for specialist assessment

UN3754.presentation: Syphilis serology after previous treatment — interpretation
UN3754.stem: A 52-year-old man has a routine screen at a sexual health clinic. Seven years ago he was treated in the same clinic for secondary syphilis with benzathine penicillin, and his records show that his rapid plasma reagin (RPR) titre fell to negative within a year. He has been in a mutually monogamous relationship for 6 years and has no symptoms. Today the treponemal antibody test is positive and the RPR is negative. Which is the most appropriate interpretation of these results?
UN3754.correct_answer: Past treated syphilis with no evidence of reinfection

UN3754.stem: A 3-year-old boy develops a fever, refuses to eat because of painful mouth ulcers, and his parents notice small blisters on his palms and soles. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A woman at 35 weeks gestation presents with a 2-week history of generalised itching that is worst on the palms and soles of her feet. She has no rash. Liver function tests show ALT 80 IU/L and serum bile acids 45 µmol/L (reference range below 19 µmol/L). What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3754.presentation: Asymptomatic sexual contact of early syphilis
UN3754.stem: A 34-year-old man attends a sexual health clinic because his regular male partner was diagnosed with primary syphilis last week. They last had sex 10 days ago. He has no symptoms, and examination of the genitals, mouth, skin and lymph nodes is normal. He has no drug allergies. Blood is taken for syphilis serology. What is the most appropriate management?
UN3754.correct_answer: Offer epidemiological treatment for syphilis today

UN3754.presentation: Delayed Fever and Rash With Organ Involvement
UN3754.stem: Four weeks after starting a new anticonvulsant, a patient develops fever, a widespread rash, marked facial swelling and is found to have eosinophilia and deranged liver function tests. What severe drug reaction should be suspected?

UN3756.stem: A man has a purulent urethral discharge and dysuria, and a swab confirms Neisseria gonorrhoeae. What is the most appropriate treatment, alongside partner notification?
A 25-year-old man has dysuria and a profuse purulent urethral discharge. A NAAT and culture confirm Neisseria gonorrhoeae. What is the most appropriate first-line treatment?

UN3756.presentation: Gradual Scrotal Pain With Urethral Symptoms
UN3756.stem: A sexually active 25-year-old man develops scrotal swelling and discomfort on the right side that has worsened steadily over three days, along with pain on passing urine and a clear urethral discharge. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3756.presentation: Epididymo-orchitis in a young man — microbiological testing
UN3756.stem: A 24-year-old man presents with 3 days of gradually worsening right scrotal pain and swelling, dysuria and a scant urethral discharge. He has had a new female sexual partner in the past month. The right epididymis is tender and swollen, the testis lies normally, and the cremasteric reflex is present. Torsion is considered unlikely. Before starting antibiotics, which investigation is most important?

A 22-year-old woman has post-coital bleeding and a mucopurulent cervical discharge. A nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT) is positive for Chlamydia trachomatis. What is the most appropriate management?
UN3756.correct_answer: Doxycycline, plus partner notification and testing

UN3756.presentation: Reactive arthritis — identifying the triggering infection
UN3756.stem: A 24-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a swollen right knee and a painful left heel for 5 days. Three weeks ago he had dysuria and a urethral discharge that settled without treatment; he has had a new sexual partner recently. He has no diarrhoea. Knee aspirate shows no crystals and Gram stain is negative, with culture pending. Reactive arthritis is suspected. Which investigation is most appropriate to identify the triggering infection?
UN3756.correct_answer: First-void urine nucleic acid amplification test

UN3756.presentation: Gonorrhoea — who needs a test of cure
UN3756.stem: A 26-year-old man is diagnosed with gonorrhoea at a sexual health clinic. NAATs (nucleic acid amplification tests) are positive on his urine and on a pharyngeal swab. Cultures are taken from both sites and he is given intramuscular ceftriaxone. His urethral discharge settles within a few days and partner notification is under way. What is the most appropriate follow-up testing?
UN3756.correct_answer: Test of cure by NAAT, as the pharynx was infected

UN3756.stem: A 31-year-old man attends a sexual health clinic worried about an infection because his right testis feels heavier than the left. He has no pain, urethral discharge or dysuria. On examination there is a firm, irregular, non-tender area that cannot be separated from the body of the right testis. The epididymis feels normal, and a torch held against the scrotum does not light up the swelling. What is the most appropriate next investigation?

UN3765.stem: Which of the following is a recognised and important route by which hepatitis B virus spreads between people?
UN3765.correct_answer: Exposure to infected blood or sexual contact

UN3765.stem: Long-term infection that slowly progresses towards fibrosis and cirrhosis is a recognised feature of which hepatitis virus?
What is the usual mode of transmission for hepatitis A?
Through which route can hepatitis B be transmitted?
UN3765.correct_answer: Exposure to infected blood or body fluids

UN3765.stem:
A 30-year-old man attends a sexual health clinic after condomless sex with a new partner. While his screening samples are taken, he asks whether any of the infections being tested for can be prevented by a vaccine. He is particularly worried about one that can be passed on through blood as well as through sex.

Which infection on the list can he be vaccinated against?
A pathogen that can persist for years, eventually predisposing to liver cancer, is being discussed on the ward round. Which organism fits?

UN3765.presentation: Hepatitis B Exposure in an Immune Worker
UN3765.stem: A healthcare worker has a needlestick exposure to blood from a patient with chronic hepatitis B. The worker previously completed the hepatitis B vaccination course and has documented immunity on blood testing. How should this exposure be interpreted?
UN3765.correct_answer: The risk of transmission is substantially reduced by her documented immunity

UN3765.stem:
At a drug and alcohol service, a 44-year-old woman who injected heroin in her twenties asks to be checked for blood-borne infections. She has never been tested before and is currently well. Her keyworker arranges a blood sample.

Which test should be sent first to find out whether she has ever been infected with hepatitis C?

UN3766.stem: Which of the following is a recognised and important route by which hepatitis B virus spreads between people?
UN3766.correct_answer: Exposure to infected blood or sexual contact

UN3766.stem: Long-term infection that slowly progresses towards fibrosis and cirrhosis is a recognised feature of which hepatitis virus?
Through which route can hepatitis B be transmitted?
UN3766.correct_answer: Exposure to infected blood or body fluids

UN3766.stem: A traveller returns from a region with poor sanitation and develops malaise, nausea, jaundice and right-upper-quadrant discomfort. Hepatitis A is confirmed. What is the most appropriate description and management?
What is the usual mode of transmission for hepatitis A?
A patient with acute hepatitis has the following serology: HBsAg POSITIVE, anti-HBc IgM POSITIVE, anti-HBs NEGATIVE. How is this best interpreted?
A pathogen that can persist for years, eventually predisposing to liver cancer, is being discussed on the ward round. Which organism fits?
A heavy drinker develops jaundice, fever and a tender, enlarged liver. What should be considered?

UN3767.presentation: Tingling and Spasms After Neck Surgery
UN3767.stem: A day after undergoing a total thyroidectomy for a large multinodular goitre, a patient develops tingling around her mouth and fingers along with involuntary muscle spasms. Blood tests show a low serum calcium. What is the most likely cause?
A patient attends with a deep, dirty puncture wound from a garden fork. Their tetanus immunisation history is uncertain/incomplete. What is the most appropriate management regarding tetanus?
UN3767.correct_answer: Tetanus-containing vaccine and tetanus immunoglobulin, with wound care

UN3767.stem: A 67-year-old woman presents to an urgent treatment centre after puncturing her palm on a rusty garden fork while spreading manure. The wound is deep and contaminated with soil. She grew up abroad and does not know which vaccinations she has had. Which infection should particularly guide decisions about vaccination and immunoglobulin?

A 62-year-old gardener attends the emergency department because he cannot open his mouth properly. Ten days ago he cut his hand while clearing brambles and soil, and did not seek treatment. He grew up abroad and has no record of any vaccinations. His jaw and neck feel rigid, and sudden noises trigger painful spasms of his back and limbs. He is fully alert and his temperature is 37.4°C. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3767.presentation: Gas gangrene after a contaminated wound
UN3767.stem:
A 46-year-old gardener drove a garden fork deep into his right thigh while turning a manure heap. The puncture wound was cleaned and closed with sutures at an urgent treatment centre. Thirty-six hours later he is brought to the emergency department with severe thigh pain that seems far worse than the wound looks. The thigh is tense and swollen, the skin is bronze and purple with dark fluid-filled blisters, and thin, foul-smelling fluid is leaking between the sutures. Crackling can be felt under the skin. His temperature is 39.1°C, heart rate 132 bpm and blood pressure 88/50 mmHg. An X-ray shows gas tracking through the muscles.

What is the most appropriate management?
UN3767.correct_answer: IV antibiotics and emergency surgical debridement

UN3767.presentation: Dirty Wound with Uncertain Tetanus History
UN3767.stem: A man attends after standing on a rusty nail. He completed his childhood vaccination schedule but cannot recall whether he has had any tetanus boosters as an adult. What is the key principle guiding tetanus prophylaxis decisions?
UN3767.correct_answer: Both the nature of the wound and the patient's vaccination history determine the appropriate management

UN3767.presentation: Spasticity in multiple sclerosis — first-line drug
UN3767.stem: A 46-year-old man with secondary progressive multiple sclerosis reports painful leg stiffness and spasms that are disturbing his sleep and making transfers difficult. His pressure areas are intact, he has no urinary symptoms, his constipation is controlled and his seating and posture have been reviewed by the physiotherapist. After discussing the possible benefits and harms, he wants a medicine to ease the spasms. He takes no regular medicines. Which medicine is most appropriate to start first?

A 50-year-old gardener attends a minor injuries unit after a rusty garden fork went through the sole of his boot into his foot. The puncture is deep and soil was found in it. It has now been irrigated and cleaned. Apart from wound care, what else should be assessed?
UN3767.correct_answer: Tetanus vaccination history and need for prophylaxis

UN3768.stem:
A 40-year-old man who recently returned from a stay in a region with an ongoing diphtheria outbreak develops a sore throat, low-grade fever and a grey membrane over the tonsils. Public health staff begin tracing the people he has been near.

By what route is this infection most likely to have spread to him?
UN3768.correct_answer: Respiratory droplets from an infected person

UN3768.presentation: Tender Shin Nodules After Sore Throat
UN3768.stem: A 29-year-old woman develops several tender, red, raised nodules on both shins about two weeks after a streptococcal sore throat. The lesions are firm swellings rather than open sores. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3768.presentation: Sore throat in pregnancy with penicillin allergy — antibiotic choice
UN3768.stem: A 29-year-old woman who is 20 weeks pregnant sees her GP with 2 days of a severe sore throat. Her temperature is 38.3°C and she has purulent tonsils and no cough or coryza; her FeverPAIN score is 4. She is systemically well, with no signs of quinsy. She had anaphylaxis to amoxicillin as a child. After discussion, an immediate antibiotic is to be prescribed. Which antibiotic is most appropriate?

A 7-year-old child develops cola-coloured urine, periorbital oedema and hypertension about 2 weeks after a sore throat. Investigations show a low C3 complement and a raised anti-streptolysin O (ASO) titre. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3768.presentation: Sore throat while taking carbimazole — immediate action
UN3768.stem: A 34-year-old woman phones her GP surgery with a 2-day history of sore throat, fever and mouth ulcers. She started carbimazole for Graves disease 6 weeks ago. She sounds unwell but is not short of breath. What is the most appropriate action?
UN3768.correct_answer: Stop carbimazole and check a full blood count today

UN3768.presentation: Haematuria With Hypertension After a Throat Infection
UN3768.stem: Two weeks after a streptococcal sore throat, a 7-year-old develops visibly dark urine, a blood pressure above the normal range for his age, and a rising creatinine. Which syndrome best describes this presentation?

A 27-year-old woman has a video consultation with her GP about a sore throat that started three days ago. She feels feverish, and on camera her tonsils look swollen with some white spots. She has no cough or runny nose. She asks whether she needs antibiotics. What is the most appropriate way to make this decision?
UN3768.correct_answer: Apply a clinical score such as FeverPAIN or Centor

UN3768.stem: A patient presents with a sore throat, fever, tonsillar exudate and tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy, and reports no cough. According to NICE guidance (NG84), which scoring systems should be used to estimate the likelihood of bacterial infection and guide antibiotic prescribing?

UN3769.stem: A patient with a persistent cough, weight loss and night sweats is being investigated for possible active pulmonary tuberculosis. Which investigation is especially important for microbiological confirmation?

A patient has weeks of cough, haemoptysis, night sweats, weight loss and fever, with upper-lobe changes on chest X-ray. Sputum is positive for acid-fast bacilli. What is the standard initial treatment regimen?
UN3769.correct_answer: RIPE for 2 months, then rifampicin and isoniazid

UN3769.stem: A 34-year-old woman recently recruited from a country with a high incidence of tuberculosis attends occupational health before starting work as a nurse on a UK ward. She feels well, with no cough, fever, night sweats or weight loss. An interferon-gamma release assay is positive and her chest X-ray is normal. HIV test and liver function tests are normal. What is the most appropriate management?
UN3769.correct_answer: Three months of isoniazid (with pyridoxine) and rifampicin

UN3769.stem: A 55-year-old man who has never smoked has a telephone consultation with his GP. He developed a cold in the spring and has had a dry, tickly cough ever since, now four months later. He feels otherwise well, has no breathlessness and has not coughed up blood. How should his cough be classified?

UN3769.presentation: Silicosis with new cavitation — investigation for tuberculosis
UN3769.stem:
A 62-year-old man who worked for 30 years as a stonemason has known silicosis. He sees his GP with 6 weeks of productive cough, night sweats and 5 kg weight loss. His temperature is 37.9°C. A chest X-ray shows a new cavitating lesion in the right upper lobe on a background of nodular upper-lobe changes.

Which investigation is most appropriate next?
UN3769.correct_answer: Sputum for acid-fast bacilli microscopy and culture

UN3769.stem: A 71-year-old woman has blood tests at her GP surgery before starting a new antihypertensive. Her full blood count shows a raised lymphocyte count, with normal haemoglobin and platelet count. She feels well and denies weight loss, night sweats or frequent infections. There is no palpable lymphadenopathy, hepatomegaly or splenomegaly. Haematology confirm a clonal B-cell population with immunophenotyping typical of chronic lymphocytic leukaemia. What is the most appropriate management?
UN3769.correct_answer: Active monitoring with regular blood counts and clinical review

UN3769.stem:
A 58-year-old man who moved to the UK from Pakistan two years ago is admitted with a month of night sweats, drenching fevers and marked weight loss. He takes methotrexate for rheumatoid arthritis. His chest X-ray shows countless tiny nodules scattered evenly through both lungs, liver enzymes are raised and fundoscopy reveals small pale choroidal lesions.

Which form of disease best accounts for this picture?
An older patient describes progressive difficulty swallowing — first solids, then liquids — over weeks, with weight loss. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN3769.correct_answer: Urgent upper GI endoscopy (suspected cancer pathway) for oesophageal cancer

UN3773.presentation: Influenza in a previously healthy adult — management and safety-netting
UN3773.stem: A 28-year-old man has had fever, headache, muscle aches and a dry cough for 24 hours during a week when influenza is known to be circulating. He has no medical conditions, takes no regular medicines and is not immunosuppressed. His observations are normal and his chest is clear. What is the most appropriate management?

A 65-year-old man develops fever, cough and diarrhoea several days after returning from a hotel stay. The hotel reports that a handful of other guests have become unwell with similar symptoms around the same time. Which organism is the most likely cause?
An otherwise healthy adult has acute diarrhoea and vomiting after a meal, with no severe dehydration and no significant comorbidity. What is the most appropriate general management?
UN3773.correct_answer: Oral rehydration and supportive care, generally avoiding routine antibiotics

UN3773.stem: A 70-year-old man has fever, productive cough and right-sided pleuritic pain. He is confused, with a respiratory rate of 32, blood pressure 88/56, and urea 8 mmol/L. What does his CURB-65 assessment indicate?
UN3773.correct_answer: High severity — admit and treat as severe pneumonia

UN3773.stem: A patient with a recent stroke and impaired swallowing develops a pneumonia, with consolidation seen in the right lower lobe. What is the most likely type of pneumonia and an important management consideration?
UN3773.correct_answer: Aspiration pneumonia — antibiotics and a swallow assessment

UN3773.stem: An 81-year-old woman is admitted from her care home with three days of cough productive of green sputum, and a chest X-ray shows right lower lobe consolidation. Staff say that until yesterday she was fully orientated, but she now does not know where she is or what day it is. She has bronchial breathing at the right base and a raised white cell count. Which feature most clearly indicates more severe pneumonia?
A 68-year-old with pneumonia has new confusion, a urea of 8 mmol/L, a respiratory rate of 32, and a blood pressure of 88/56. What does the CURB-65 score indicate about his management?
UN3773.correct_answer: High score — admit and manage as high-severity pneumonia

UN3773.presentation: New Fluctuating Confusion After a Medication Change
UN3773.stem: A 75-year-old man becomes agitated and confused shortly after starting a new medication. He has no focal neurological signs, and his level of confusion seems to come and go throughout the day. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3775.stem: A 51-year-old woman develops fever, a productive cough and increasing breathlessness over two days. A chest X-ray demonstrates a new area of focal consolidation. What is the most appropriate treatment?
UN3775.correct_answer: Antibiotics guided by CURB-65 and local guidance

UN3775.stem: A 70-year-old man has fever, productive cough and right-sided pleuritic pain. He is confused, with a respiratory rate of 32, blood pressure 88/56, and urea 8 mmol/L. What does his CURB-65 assessment indicate?
UN3775.correct_answer: High severity — admit and treat as severe pneumonia

UN3775.stem: A 65-year-old man has fever, productive cough, and right-sided pleuritic chest pain. CXR shows opacification of the right lower zone with air bronchograms visible within the opacity. There is no volume loss. What is the diagnosis?

A 71-year-old woman is seen on a GP home visit. For three days she has had shivering attacks, a cough bringing up rust-coloured sputum and a sharp pain in her right side when she breathes in. Her temperature is 38.6°C and she is mildly tachypnoeic but fully oriented. There is dullness to percussion at the right base with bronchial breathing and coarse crackles over the same area. Which diagnosis best fits?

UN3775.presentation: Fever, cough and fast breathing in a child
UN3775.stem:
A 6-year-old girl has had three days of fever and cough. She is breathing faster than expected for her age and has a sharp pain on the right side of her chest when she breathes in deeply. On examination, air entry is reduced and there are coarse crackles at the right base. The rest of the chest is clear and there is no wheeze.

What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old man attends his GP with a productive cough and fever, and community-acquired pneumonia is suspected. Before an antibiotic is chosen, he mentions that about ten years ago, within an hour of taking a penicillin tablet, he came out in itchy raised welts all over his body and his lips and eyelids swelled up. How should this history be interpreted?
UN3775.correct_answer: As a probable immediate, IgE-mediated allergy to penicillin

UN3775.stem: A 72-year-old man with community-acquired pneumonia has a new-onset confusion, urea 12 mmol/L, respiratory rate 30 breaths/min, and blood pressure 100/70 mmHg. What is his CURB-65 score?
A 68-year-old with pneumonia has new confusion, a urea of 8 mmol/L, a respiratory rate of 32, and a blood pressure of 88/56. What does the CURB-65 score indicate about his management?
UN3775.correct_answer: High score — admit and manage as high-severity pneumonia

UN3776.presentation: Expanding Rash After a Tick Bite
UN3776.stem: A 34-year-old man notices a slowly enlarging red ring-shaped rash on his calf about ten days after a camping trip, during which he recalls pulling off an attached tick. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A hiker develops a slowly enlarging, painless red patch on the thigh ten days after walking through woodland, where she recalls removing an embedded tick. The lesion is not itchy. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A walker in a tick-endemic area develops a slowly expanding, red, ring-shaped rash with central clearing (erythema migrans) at the site of a tick bite, with mild flu-like symptoms. What is the most appropriate management?
UN3776.correct_answer: Treat clinically with oral doxycycline (no need to await serology)

UN3776.presentation: Lyme disease facial palsy — antibiotic choice
UN3776.stem: A 38-year-old man has a left lower motor neurone facial palsy that developed 5 weeks after a tick bite in the New Forest. Lyme ELISA and immunoblot are both positive. He has no headache, neck stiffness, confusion, limb weakness or palpitations, and his ECG is normal. He is not allergic to any medicines. Which antibiotic treatment is most appropriate?

UN3776.presentation: Suspected Lyme disease without erythema migrans — first test
UN3776.stem: A 47-year-old woman sees her GP with 3 weeks of fatigue, headache, low-grade fevers and aches that move between different joints. Five weeks ago she removed a tick after a walking holiday in the Scottish Highlands. She has not noticed any rash, and examination shows no rash, no joint swelling and no neurological signs. The GP suspects Lyme disease. Which investigation is most appropriate first?

A 52-year-old woman is seen at her GP surgery. Three weeks ago she went hill walking in the Scottish Highlands and afterwards removed a small tick from her thigh. Over the past week a red patch has slowly spread outwards from the bite site to about the size of her palm, with a paler centre. She feels a little tired but has no neurological or cardiac symptoms. She is not pregnant and has no allergies. What is the most appropriate management?

A 47-year-old woman went walking in a heathland national park two weeks ago. She now has a red, ring-shaped patch on her thigh that has slowly enlarged over several days, with a paler centre. It is not itchy or scaly. She feels achy and tired. She does not remember being bitten by anything. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old boy develops an expanding red rash on his thigh a week after a family camping trip in the New Forest, and the GP diagnoses erythema migrans. His mother had doxycycline for the same problem last year and asks why her son is being given amoxicillin instead. What is the main reason tetracyclines are generally avoided at his age?
UN3776.correct_answer: They are deposited in developing teeth, causing permanent staining and enamel hypoplasia

UN3777.stem: A 71-year-old woman has sudden left-sided weakness together with an upper motor neurone pattern of facial weakness on the right. Which cranial nerve is responsible for producing the facial weakness itself?

UN3777.presentation: Facial Weakness Affecting the Whole Side of the Face
UN3777.stem: A patient develops sudden weakness of the entire left side of the face, including the inability to raise the left eyebrow or fully close the left eye. What type of facial nerve lesion does this represent?
UN3777.correct_answer: Lower motor neurone facial nerve palsy

UN3777.presentation: Lyme disease facial palsy — antibiotic choice
UN3777.stem: A 38-year-old man has a left lower motor neurone facial palsy that developed 5 weeks after a tick bite in the New Forest. Lyme ELISA and immunoblot are both positive. He has no headache, neck stiffness, confusion, limb weakness or palpitations, and his ECG is normal. He is not allergic to any medicines. Which antibiotic treatment is most appropriate?

A 38-year-old woman develops weakness affecting the entire left side of her face, including being unable to close her left eye and losing movement of her forehead on that side. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3777.presentation: Unilateral Facial Weakness Including the Forehead
UN3777.stem: A patient wakes with weakness of the left side of the face, unable to raise the left eyebrow or fully close the left eye, while the rest of their neurological examination is normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3777.presentation: Facial nerve palsy — feature that needs urgent specialist referral
UN3777.stem:
A 52-year-old man sees his GP with weakness of the right side of his face, including his forehead. He cannot fully close his right eye. There are no limb symptoms, the ear canal and eardrum look normal, and there is no rash. The GP is considering a diagnosis of Bell palsy.

Which additional feature should most prompt specialist referral rather than treatment as Bell palsy in primary care?
UN3777.correct_answer: Weakness worsening slowly over three weeks

UN3777.stem: A 67-year-old man develops sudden left-sided facial droop. On examination he can wrinkle his forehead symmetrically, but the lower half of the left face is weak. He also has mild left arm weakness. What is the most appropriate immediate action?
Which of these symptoms most specifically points to involvement of the dominant cerebral hemisphere, in a patient with sudden facial weakness, arm weakness and difficulty speaking?

UN3782.stem: A 27-year-old backpacker is bitten on the hand by a stray dog in a region where rabies is endemic. The wound is contaminated with the animal's saliva. Before any medical assessment can take place, what is the single most important first-aid step?
UN3782.correct_answer: Irrigate and scrub the wound thoroughly with soap and water

UN3782.stem: A 24-year-old woman attends her GP the day after returning from a trip to rural India. Three days ago a stray cat scratched her forearm hard enough to draw blood. She washed the wound with bottled water, and the cat ran off. She feels well and the scratch is healing without signs of infection. Which is the best management?
UN3782.correct_answer: Urgent risk assessment for rabies post-exposure prophylaxis

UN3782.stem: A patient attends a few hours after a cat bite to the hand, which is deep with puncture wounds. The wound is not obviously infected yet. Besides wound cleaning, what is the most appropriate management?

UN3782.presentation: Measles exposure in pregnancy — post-exposure prophylaxis
UN3782.stem: A 27-year-old woman who is 20 weeks pregnant was in the same room as a child with confirmed measles 3 days ago. She was never vaccinated and has never had measles. She is well. Her measles IgG antibody test is negative. Which is the most appropriate post-exposure prophylaxis?
A woman at 30 weeks' gestation, with no history of chickenpox, has significant household exposure to a child with chickenpox. Her varicella IgG is negative. What is the most appropriate management?

A theatre nurse attends the occupational health department two days after blood from an HIV-positive patient splashed into her eye during an emergency laparotomy. She rinsed her eye at the time but did not report the incident until today. The source patient had recently stopped antiretroviral therapy and his viral load is detectable.

What should be offered now?
UN3782.correct_answer: A 28-day course of HIV post-exposure prophylaxis started as soon as possible today

UN3782.stem:
A 31-year-old man is seen in a medical admissions unit with two days of fever, extreme anxiety and episodes of throat spasm when he tries to drink water. Seven weeks ago, while volunteering in rural India, he was bitten on the hand by a stray dog and did not seek treatment. He now becomes agitated when a fan blows air at his face.

What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3782.presentation: Deciding Post-Exposure Management After Hepatitis B Exposure
UN3782.stem: A healthcare assistant is splashed with blood from a patient known to carry hepatitis B. What mainly determines whether post-exposure treatment is required?
UN3782.correct_answer: The assistant's hepatitis B immunity and the type of exposure

UN3783.stem:
A 74-year-old man is seen in the haematology clinic. Over several months he has noticed painless lumps in his right axilla and left groin, and examination also finds an enlarged node in the neck, with no involvement of the areas in between. He feels generally well.

Which diagnosis best explains this pattern of lymph node enlargement?

A 23-year-old man sees his GP with a painless lump in his neck that has grown over six weeks. He has generalised itching, drenching night sweats and unintentional weight loss. There is a firm, rubbery, non-tender lymph node in the left supraclavicular fossa and smaller nodes in the neck. A chest X-ray shows mediastinal widening. He is referred urgently to haematology. Which investigation is most appropriate to establish the diagnosis and its subtype?
UN3783.correct_answer: Excision biopsy of a lymph node

UN3783.stem: A 25-year-old man presents with painless right-sided cervical lymphadenopathy for 3 months, drenching night sweats, and 10 kg weight loss. CXR shows mediastinal widening. Lymph node biopsy shows Reed-Sternberg cells (large binucleate cells with prominent owl-eye nucleoli). What is the most likely diagnosis?
A child develops a high fever with cough, a runny nose and red eyes, followed a few days later by a blotchy rash that starts on the face and spreads down the body. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old has had a high fever for 6 days with bilateral non-purulent conjunctivitis, a strawberry tongue with cracked lips, a polymorphous rash, swollen red hands and feet, and a large cervical lymph node. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A patient over 55 has new, persistent dyspepsia with unintentional weight loss and early satiety. Examination reveals an enlarged left supraclavicular lymph node. What is the most appropriate action?
UN3783.correct_answer: Urgent upper GI endoscopy to investigate for gastric cancer

UN3783.stem: A patient attends a few hours after a cat bite to the hand, which is deep with puncture wounds. The wound is not obviously infected yet. Besides wound cleaning, what is the most appropriate management?

UN3783.presentation: Rough Papule Interrupting Normal Skin Lines
UN3783.stem: An 8-year-old has a rough, firm papule on the back of her hand. On close inspection, the normal skin lines across the lesion appear interrupted. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3820.stem: A 19-year-old develops fever, marked exudative tonsillitis, cervical lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly. After being given amoxicillin by another clinician, a florid widespread maculopapular rash appears. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A 19-year-old has a sore throat, fever, marked cervical lymphadenopathy and lethargy, with atypical lymphocytes on the blood film. Which is the most appropriate advice?
UN3820.correct_answer: Avoid amoxicillin and contact sports (risk of rash and splenic rupture)

UN3820.stem: A 16-year-old boy has infectious mononucleosis confirmed on a blood test. He has a sore throat and marked tiredness but is eating and drinking, and he has no breathing difficulty or abdominal pain. His mother asks when he can go back to school. What is the most appropriate advice?
UN3820.correct_answer: Return to school as soon as he feels well enough

UN3820.stem: A 25-year-old man presents with painless right-sided cervical lymphadenopathy for 3 months, drenching night sweats, and 10 kg weight loss. CXR shows mediastinal widening. Lymph node biopsy shows Reed-Sternberg cells (large binucleate cells with prominent owl-eye nucleoli). What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old man sees his GP with a painless lump in his neck that has grown over six weeks. He has generalised itching, drenching night sweats and unintentional weight loss. There is a firm, rubbery, non-tender lymph node in the left supraclavicular fossa and smaller nodes in the neck. A chest X-ray shows mediastinal widening. He is referred urgently to haematology. Which investigation is most appropriate to establish the diagnosis and its subtype?
UN3820.correct_answer: Excision biopsy of a lymph node

UN3820.stem:
A 74-year-old man is seen in the haematology clinic. Over several months he has noticed painless lumps in his right axilla and left groin, and examination also finds an enlarged node in the neck, with no involvement of the areas in between. He feels generally well.

Which diagnosis best explains this pattern of lymph node enlargement?

A 24-year-old woman has fever, sore throat and enlarged neck glands, followed by severe tiredness and an enlarged liver and spleen. Blood film shows atypical lymphocytes. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3820.presentation: Characteristic Symptom of Gastric Outlet Obstruction
UN3820.stem: An older man with known gastric cancer develops progressive weight loss and worsening nausea. Which symptom is particularly characteristic of the gastric outlet obstruction that can complicate this condition?

UN3825.stem: A patient attends with a deep, dirty puncture wound from a garden fork. Their tetanus immunisation history is uncertain/incomplete. What is the most appropriate management regarding tetanus?
UN3825.correct_answer: Tetanus-containing vaccine and tetanus immunoglobulin, with wound care

UN3825.stem: A 67-year-old woman presents to an urgent treatment centre after puncturing her palm on a rusty garden fork while spreading manure. The wound is deep and contaminated with soil. She grew up abroad and does not know which vaccinations she has had. Which infection should particularly guide decisions about vaccination and immunoglobulin?

A 50-year-old gardener attends a minor injuries unit after a rusty garden fork went through the sole of his boot into his foot. The puncture is deep and soil was found in it. It has now been irrigated and cleaned. Apart from wound care, what else should be assessed?
UN3825.correct_answer: Tetanus vaccination history and need for prophylaxis

UN3825.stem: A patient attends a few hours after a cat bite to the hand, which is deep with puncture wounds. The wound is not obviously infected yet. Besides wound cleaning, what is the most appropriate management?

UN3825.presentation: Dirty Wound with Uncertain Tetanus History
UN3825.stem: A man attends after standing on a rusty nail. He completed his childhood vaccination schedule but cannot recall whether he has had any tetanus boosters as an adult. What is the key principle guiding tetanus prophylaxis decisions?
UN3825.correct_answer: Both the nature of the wound and the patient's vaccination history determine the appropriate management

UN3825.presentation: Gas gangrene after a contaminated wound
UN3825.stem:
A 46-year-old gardener drove a garden fork deep into his right thigh while turning a manure heap. The puncture wound was cleaned and closed with sutures at an urgent treatment centre.
