Thirty-six hours later he is brought to the emergency department with severe thigh pain that seems far worse than the wound looks. The thigh is tense and swollen, the skin is bronze and purple with dark fluid-filled blisters, and thin, foul-smelling fluid is leaking between the sutures. Crackling can be felt under the skin. His temperature is 39.1°C, heart rate 132 bpm and blood pressure 88/50 mmHg. An X-ray shows gas tracking through the muscles.

What is the most appropriate management?
UN3825.correct_answer: IV antibiotics and emergency surgical debridement

UN3825.stem: On day 6 after an abdominal laparotomy, a patient notices pink serous fluid soaking through the dressing, and on inspection the wound edges have partially separated. What is the most likely complication?

A 27-year-old backpacker is bitten on the hand by a stray dog in a region where rabies is endemic. The wound is contaminated with the animal's saliva. Before any medical assessment can take place, what is the single most important first-aid step?
UN3825.correct_answer: Irrigate and scrub the wound thoroughly with soap and water

UN3827.stem: A patient develops a PAINFUL, tender swelling of the thyroid with transient hyperthyroid symptoms a few weeks after a viral illness. ESR is raised, and radioiodine uptake is LOW. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 38-year-old woman attends the infectious diseases clinic. She was found to have HIV two years ago but stopped antiretroviral therapy last year, and her CD4 count is now very low. Sputum culture has grown Mycobacterium tuberculosis. The registrar explains to the foundation doctor why this pairing of infections matters.

Which statement is most accurate?
UN3827.correct_answer: HIV-related immunosuppression greatly increases progression from latent to active tuberculosis

UN3827.presentation: Subacute Combined Degeneration of the Cord
UN3827.stem: A patient with low vitamin B12 develops a progressive unsteady gait, loss of vibration sense and proprioception in the feet, and weakness. Examination shows ABSENT ankle jerks but EXTENSOR (upgoing) plantar responses. What is the most likely diagnosis?
UN3827.correct_answer: Subacute combined degeneration of the cord

UN3827.stem: A 30-year-old woman develops a painful, tender swelling in the front of her neck following a viral upper respiratory illness, with transient symptoms of thyrotoxicosis. Her ESR is raised, and a radioiodine uptake scan shows low uptake. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 66-year-old man with stable angina returns to his GP two weeks after being given a glyceryl trinitrate spray. He says it relieves his chest tightness within minutes, but each time he uses it he gets a throbbing headache and feels flushed. He has no other neurological symptoms and is otherwise well. What is the most likely explanation for the headache?

A patient describes shimmering zig-zag lines across their vision lasting about 25 minutes, which resolve just before a throbbing one-sided headache develops with associated nausea. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A patient with Wilson disease develops worsening neurological symptoms after starting penicillamine. What is the most appropriate alternative treatment?
A 28-year-old woman recovering from a streptococcal throat infection develops several painful, tender red lumps over both shins. Which diagnosis is most likely?

UN3997.stem: A 19-year-old has a sore throat, fever, marked cervical lymphadenopathy and lethargy, with atypical lymphocytes on the blood film. Which is the most appropriate advice?
UN3997.correct_answer: Avoid amoxicillin and contact sports (risk of rash and splenic rupture)

UN3997.stem: A 19-year-old develops fever, marked exudative tonsillitis, cervical lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly. After being given amoxicillin by another clinician, a florid widespread maculopapular rash appears. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3997.presentation: Return to Contact Sport After Glandular Fever
UN3997.stem: A 20-year-old rugby player has just been diagnosed with infectious mononucleosis and wants to know why he should avoid contact sport while he recovers. What is the main risk being avoided?
A 17-year-old footballer recovering from confirmed glandular fever asks his doctor when he can safely return to training and matches. Why is he advised to avoid contact sport for several weeks?

A 24-year-old woman has fever, sore throat and enlarged neck glands, followed by severe tiredness and an enlarged liver and spleen. Blood film shows atypical lymphocytes. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 16-year-old boy has infectious mononucleosis confirmed on a blood test. He has a sore throat and marked tiredness but is eating and drinking, and he has no breathing difficulty or abdominal pain. His mother asks when he can go back to school. What is the most appropriate advice?
UN3997.correct_answer: Return to school as soon as he feels well enough

UN3997.stem: A 19-year-old woman attends her GP three days after being given amoxicillin at a walk-in centre for a sore throat. She has a week of fever, marked fatigue and tender swollen glands at the back of her neck, and a palpable spleen tip. Since yesterday she has had a widespread itchy, flat and slightly raised red (maculopapular) rash on her trunk and limbs, with no wheals. Her lips, mouth and eyes are unaffected and she has no breathing difficulty. What is the most likely explanation for the rash?
UN3997.correct_answer: Aminopenicillin rash in Epstein–Barr virus infection

UN3997.presentation: Infectious mononucleosis — airway compromise red flag
UN3997.stem: A 19-year-old woman who was diagnosed with glandular fever 4 days ago phones her GP surgery. Her throat has become much more swollen, she cannot swallow her own saliva and she is finding it hard to breathe. She is speaking in short phrases. What is the most appropriate action?
UN3997.correct_answer: Arrange immediate transfer to hospital by ambulance

UN4133.stem: A 22-year-old woman has post-coital bleeding and a mucopurulent cervical discharge. A nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT) is positive for Chlamydia trachomatis. What is the most appropriate management?
UN4133.correct_answer: Doxycycline, plus partner notification and testing

UN4133.stem: A 22-year-old woman sees her GP for the third time in four months with burning on passing urine and frequency. Urine samples sent at her last two visits showed white cells but grew no organisms, and her symptoms did not settle with antibiotics for cystitis. She now also mentions a change in vaginal discharge and some bleeding after sex. She has had a new partner in the last six months and they do not use condoms. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN4133.presentation: Epididymo-orchitis in a young man — microbiological testing
UN4133.stem: A 24-year-old man presents with 3 days of gradually worsening right scrotal pain and swelling, dysuria and a scant urethral discharge. He has had a new female sexual partner in the past month. The right epididymis is tender and swollen, the testis lies normally, and the cremasteric reflex is present. Torsion is considered unlikely. Before starting antibiotics, which investigation is most important?

A 22-year-old woman presents with bilateral lower abdominal pain, deep dyspareunia, and a mucopurulent vaginal discharge. Bimanual examination reveals cervical motion tenderness and bilateral adnexal tenderness. She is afebrile. What is the most appropriate management?
UN4133.correct_answer: Outpatient antibiotics — IM ceftriaxone plus oral doxycycline and metronidazole

UN4133.stem: A woman has a thin, grey-white vaginal discharge with a fishy odour but no itch or soreness. The vaginal pH is raised (>4.5) and 'clue cells' are seen on microscopy. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN4133.presentation: Reactive arthritis — identifying the triggering infection
UN4133.stem: A 24-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a swollen right knee and a painful left heel for 5 days. Three weeks ago he had dysuria and a urethral discharge that settled without treatment; he has had a new sexual partner recently. He has no diarrhoea. Knee aspirate shows no crystals and Gram stain is negative, with culture pending. Reactive arthritis is suspected. Which investigation is most appropriate to identify the triggering infection?
UN4133.correct_answer: First-void urine nucleic acid amplification test

UN4133.stem: A 24-year-old woman who is 28 weeks pregnant has a positive nucleic acid amplification test for Chlamydia trachomatis from a vulvovaginal swab taken at her antenatal booking review. She has no symptoms and no drug allergies. Which antibiotic is most appropriate?

A 28-year-old woman who is 30 weeks pregnant mentions at her antenatal appointment that she has had intense vulval itching and soreness for five days. She recently finished a course of antibiotics for a chest infection. There is a thick, white, curd-like discharge with no unpleasant smell. The vulva is red with small superficial fissures. She has no new sexual partner. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN4134.stem: A man has a purulent urethral discharge and dysuria, and a swab confirms Neisseria gonorrhoeae. What is the most appropriate treatment, alongside partner notification?
A 25-year-old man has dysuria and a profuse purulent urethral discharge. A NAAT and culture confirm Neisseria gonorrhoeae. What is the most appropriate first-line treatment?

A 22-year-old man develops cramping abdominal pain and bloody diarrhoea three days after eating an undercooked beef burger at a barbecue. Which organism is particularly associated with this presentation?

UN4134.presentation: Epididymo-orchitis in a young man — microbiological testing
UN4134.stem: A 24-year-old man presents with 3 days of gradually worsening right scrotal pain and swelling, dysuria and a scant urethral discharge. He has had a new female sexual partner in the past month. The right epididymis is tender and swollen, the testis lies normally, and the cremasteric reflex is present. Torsion is considered unlikely. Before starting antibiotics, which investigation is most important?

A 31-year-old man attends a sexual health clinic worried about an infection because his right testis feels heavier than the left. He has no pain, urethral discharge or dysuria. On examination there is a firm, irregular, non-tender area that cannot be separated from the body of the right testis. The epididymis feels normal, and a torch held against the scrotum does not light up the swelling. What is the most appropriate next investigation?

UN4134.presentation: Reactive arthritis — identifying the triggering infection
UN4134.stem: A 24-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a swollen right knee and a painful left heel for 5 days. Three weeks ago he had dysuria and a urethral discharge that settled without treatment; he has had a new sexual partner recently. He has no diarrhoea. Knee aspirate shows no crystals and Gram stain is negative, with culture pending. Reactive arthritis is suspected. Which investigation is most appropriate to identify the triggering infection?
UN4134.correct_answer: First-void urine nucleic acid amplification test

UN4134.stem:
Two weeks after returning from a holiday in the Caribbean, a 38-year-old man sees his GP with five days of fever, a widespread itchy red rash and severe pain and swelling in his wrists, fingers and ankles on both sides. He recalls many mosquito bites. He has had no diarrhoea, urethral discharge or new sexual partners, and no joint is hot and red.

Which diagnosis is most likely?

UN4134.presentation: Gonorrhoea — who needs a test of cure
UN4134.stem: A 26-year-old man is diagnosed with gonorrhoea at a sexual health clinic. NAATs (nucleic acid amplification tests) are positive on his urine and on a pharyngeal swab. Cultures are taken from both sites and he is given intramuscular ceftriaxone. His urethral discharge settles within a few days and partner notification is under way. What is the most appropriate follow-up testing?
UN4134.correct_answer: Test of cure by NAAT, as the pharynx was infected

UN4217.stem: A teenage boy develops a painful, swollen testis several days after his parotid glands swelled up. What complication is this?

A 14-year-old boy who has not received any MMR vaccines is brought to the emergency department. A week ago he developed painful swelling of both parotid glands, and over the last day he has had a worsening headache, has vomited several times and finds bright light uncomfortable. He is alert, his neck is stiff on flexion and there is no rash.

Which complication is most likely?

A 19-year-old university student is seen in general practice with 2 days of fever and painful swelling of both parotid glands. He has not had the MMR vaccine. He is well enough to manage at home, and the GP has notified the health protection team and arranged an oral fluid test. Which new symptom should he be told to seek urgent medical review for?

UN4217.presentation: Painful Bilateral Swelling Below the Ears
UN4217.stem: A child presents with fever and tender swelling below both ears, with the parotid glands clearly enlarged and painful to touch. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old girl is seen by her GP with fever and tender swelling of both parotid glands. She has had no MMR vaccines. The GP is confident clinically that this is mumps and has advised rest, fluids and paracetamol. No laboratory test has yet been done.

What is the most appropriate action regarding public health?
UN4217.correct_answer: Notify the health protection team now

UN4217.stem: A 52-year-old man notices painful swelling of the side of his face near the ear that worsens noticeably whenever he eats. Between meals, the swelling partially settles. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old man develops a painful cluster of blistering lesions across the left side of his forehead and upper eyelid, sparing the tip of his nose. Which complication is particularly important to consider?

UN4217.presentation: Painful Swelling at the Nail Fold
UN4217.stem: A regular nail-biter develops a painful, red, swollen area at the side of the nail on their index finger over the past two days. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN4409.stem: A man with advanced HIV (CD4 count 50 cells/µL) and poor treatment adherence presents with headache, fever and a focal neurological deficit. Contrast CT of the brain shows multiple RING-ENHANCING lesions. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN4409.presentation: Cerebral toxoplasmosis in advanced HIV — first-line treatment
UN4409.stem:
A 38-year-old man with newly diagnosed advanced HIV and a very low CD4 count presents with headache, fever and right-sided weakness. MRI of the brain shows multiple ring-enhancing lesions in the basal ganglia, and Toxoplasma IgG is positive. The HIV team diagnose presumed cerebral toxoplasmosis and start empirical treatment.

Which is the preferred first-line treatment?

A 38-year-old woman who stopped her antiretroviral therapy two years ago is brought in by her sister. For the past three weeks she has had a slowly worsening headache, low-grade fevers and, more recently, episodes of confusion. Her last CD4 count was very low. There is minimal neck stiffness and no focal weakness.

Which opportunistic infection should be considered first?

A man with newly diagnosed HIV has a CD4 count of 150 cells/mm3. Alongside starting antiretroviral therapy, which prophylaxis is most important to prevent the commonest serious opportunistic infection at this count?

UN4409.presentation: Papilloedema with suspected IIH — image before lumbar puncture
UN4409.stem:
A 30-year-old woman is referred to the acute medical unit by her optometrist, who saw swelling of both optic discs at a routine eye test. For a month she has had a daily headache that is worse when she lies down and when she coughs. She has gained weight over the past year and is otherwise well, with no fever, neck stiffness or focal neurological signs. The medical registrar suspects idiopathic intracranial hypertension (raised brain pressure with no identifiable cause) and suggests a lumbar puncture this afternoon to measure the opening pressure. No brain imaging has been done.

What should be the next investigation?

A 23-year-old man describes recurrent episodes beginning with a rising sensation in the stomach and a feeling of déjà vu, followed by lip-smacking and plucking at his clothes, for which he is amnesic, lasting about a minute with brief postictal confusion. What is the most likely diagnosis?
UN4409.correct_answer: Focal seizures of temporal lobe origin

UN4409.presentation: New Confusion in Chronic Liver Disease
UN4409.stem: A man with known alcohol-related cirrhosis is brought to hospital by his family because he has become increasingly muddled and is behaving out of character over the past two days. Neurological examination reveals no focal deficit. Which complication of his liver disease should be considered?

A 52-year-old woman has a 1-week history of headache, fever and confusion following a severe sinus infection. Contrast-enhanced MRI shows a single 2 cm ring-enhancing lesion in the left frontal lobe with surrounding oedema. Blood cultures have been taken and the neurosurgical team will review her today. She has no drug allergies. Which empirical antibiotic regimen is most appropriate?

UN4411.stem: A 54-year-old man with a mechanical aortic valve is referred to the acute medical unit by his GP after ten days of fevers, aches and fatigue. On arrival he is alert, his observations are stable and there is no obvious source of infection. The team suspects prosthetic valve endocarditis. Which investigation should be done before any antibiotic is given?
UN4411.correct_answer: Three sets of blood cultures from separate venepunctures

UN4411.stem: A 45-year-old intravenous drug user has two weeks of fever, malaise and night sweats. Examination reveals a new heart murmur, splinter haemorrhages and painful nodules on the finger pulps. What is the most important initial investigation pair?

A 50-year-old man with a native aortic valve has definite infective endocarditis. Blood cultures grow Streptococcus viridans (penicillin-sensitive). He is haemodynamically stable with no complications. What is the most appropriate antibiotic regimen?
UN4411.correct_answer: IV benzylpenicillin or IV amoxicillin for 4 weeks

UN4411.stem: You are about to treat someone for probable infective endocarditis, and they are not acutely unwell. Which test should be organised before the first dose of antibiotics goes in?
UN4411.correct_answer: Taking multiple sets of blood cultures

UN4411.stem: A 34-year-old man who injects drugs is admitted with fever and a new heart murmur, and blood cultures grow Staphylococcus aureus. On examination there are flat, non-tender, red-purple macules on the soles of his feet and the thenar eminences of his hands. What are these lesions called?

A 66-year-old woman receiving chemotherapy for ovarian cancer is admitted with rigors and a fever, and neutropenic sepsis is suspected. Intravenous antibiotics are being prepared. Which investigation should be taken first, as long as it does not delay the antibiotics?

A 35-year-old intravenous drug user presents with 3 weeks of fever, night sweats, and weight loss. He has a new pansystolic murmur at the lower left sternal edge worsening on inspiration. Blood cultures grow Staphylococcus aureus. Echocardiogram shows a vegetation on the tricuspid valve. What is the most likely diagnosis using the Duke criteria?

A 68-year-old woman who had a mechanical aortic valve replacement four years ago is admitted with three weeks of intermittent fevers, sweats, fatigue and weight loss. There is a new early diastolic murmur, small haemorrhages under the conjunctivae, and her urine dipstick shows blood. She is alert, with a blood pressure of 128/74 mmHg and no signs of sepsis or heart failure. What is the most important initial investigation?
UN4411.correct_answer: At least three sets of blood cultures from separate venepunctures before antibiotics

UN4416.stem: A patient attends a few hours after a cat bite to the hand, which is deep with puncture wounds. The wound is not obviously infected yet. Besides wound cleaning, what is the most appropriate management?
A patient with Wilson disease develops worsening neurological symptoms after starting penicillamine. What is the most appropriate alternative treatment?

A 27-year-old backpacker is bitten on the hand by a stray dog in a region where rabies is endemic. The wound is contaminated with the animal's saliva. Before any medical assessment can take place, what is the single most important first-aid step?
UN4416.correct_answer: Irrigate and scrub the wound thoroughly with soap and water

UN4416.stem: A father brings his 6-year-old daughter to a community pharmacy. She is on day three of co-amoxiclav prescribed for a skin infection after an animal bite, and since yesterday she has had softer, more frequent stools. She is playing normally, drinking well and has no fever, abdominal pain or blood in her stools. What is the most likely explanation for her bowel change?

A 66-year-old man with stable angina returns to his GP two weeks after being given a glyceryl trinitrate spray. He says it relieves his chest tightness within minutes, but each time he uses it he gets a throbbing headache and feels flushed. He has no other neurological symptoms and is otherwise well. What is the most likely explanation for the headache?

UN4416.presentation: Symptoms After A Road Traffic Collision
UN4416.stem: Four months after being involved in a frightening car crash, a 28-year-old man continues to have unwanted flashbacks, avoids driving altogether and becomes intensely distressed whenever he hears a car horn. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 47-year-old woman went walking in a heathland national park two weeks ago. She now has a red, ring-shaped patch on her thigh that has slowly enlarged over several days, with a paler centre. It is not itchy or scaly. She feels achy and tired. She does not remember being bitten by anything. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 31-year-old man is seen in a medical admissions unit with two days of fever, extreme anxiety and episodes of throat spasm when he tries to drink water. Seven weeks ago, while volunteering in rural India, he was bitten on the hand by a stray dog and did not seek treatment. He now becomes agitated when a fan blows air at his face.

What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN4419.presentation: Long-Term Risk of Chronic Hepatitis C
UN4419.stem: A patient is newly diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C infection. Over the following years, which complication represents the most significant long-term risk?
Long-term infection that slowly progresses towards fibrosis and cirrhosis is a recognised feature of which hepatitis virus?
A pathogen that can persist for years, eventually predisposing to liver cancer, is being discussed on the ward round. Which organism fits?

A 30-year-old man attends a sexual health clinic after condomless sex with a new partner. While his screening samples are taken, he asks whether any of the infections being tested for can be prevented by a vaccine. He is particularly worried about one that can be passed on through blood as well as through sex.

Which infection on the list can he be vaccinated against?

A 68-year-old man with Child-Pugh A cirrhosis secondary to chronic hepatitis B infection attends for routine outpatient review. He is asymptomatic with stable liver function. His most recent abdominal ultrasound, performed 8 months ago, was unremarkable. What is the recommended HCC surveillance strategy?
UN4419.correct_answer: Ultrasound and serum AFP every 6 months

UN4419.stem: A 23-year-old woman comes in with lower abdominal discomfort and an unusual discharge, and moving her cervix on examination causes marked tenderness. If her pelvic infection goes untreated, which long-term complication is she at risk of?

A 9-year-old boy recently arrived from West Africa is seen in the paediatric clinic three weeks after a sore throat. He has had painful joints that flit from knees to ankles, a faint rash of pink rings on his trunk and a few small, firm, painless nodules over his elbows. Which long-term cardiac problem is he at greatest risk of developing?
UN4419.correct_answer: Chronic rheumatic valve disease, mainly of the mitral valve

UN4419.stem: Which of the following is a recognised and important route by which hepatitis B virus spreads between people?
UN4419.correct_answer: Exposure to infected blood or sexual contact

UN4420.stem: A new healthcare worker has no documented evidence of hepatitis B vaccination and is about to begin a role involving regular exposure to blood and body fluids. What is the appropriate approach?
UN4420.correct_answer: Hepatitis B vaccination should be offered based on the individual's occupational risk

UN4420.stem:
A newly qualified healthcare assistant attends occupational health to start her hepatitis B vaccine course. She asks whether she can also be vaccinated against hepatitis C at the same appointment, since she will be handling blood samples.

What is the correct response?
UN4420.correct_answer: No, there is no licensed vaccine that prevents hepatitis C

UN4420.stem: A traveller preparing for a trip to a country where hepatitis A is endemic has never been vaccinated against it. What is the main reason to offer hepatitis A vaccination before departure?
UN4420.correct_answer: It reduces the risk of acquiring hepatitis A infection

UN4420.presentation: Hepatitis B Exposure in an Immune Worker
UN4420.stem: A healthcare worker has a needlestick exposure to blood from a patient with chronic hepatitis B. The worker previously completed the hepatitis B vaccination course and has documented immunity on blood testing. How should this exposure be interpreted?
UN4420.correct_answer: The risk of transmission is substantially reduced by her documented immunity

UN4420.presentation: Needlestick with Known Hepatitis B Immunity
UN4420.stem: A 38-year-old paramedic sustains a needlestick injury from a patient known to be hepatitis B surface-antigen positive. She completed her hepatitis B vaccination course 6 years ago and has documented immunity. What is generally required in this situation?
UN4420.correct_answer: A hepatitis B vaccine booster dose

UN4420.stem: A factory worker notices that his cough and wheeze are consistently worse during his shifts and improve markedly over weekends and while on annual leave. What is the most likely explanation?

UN4420.presentation: Hepatitis B serology — inactive carrier state
UN4420.stem: A 35-year-old healthcare worker undergoes occupational health screening. Blood tests: HBsAg positive, anti-HBc total positive, HBeAg negative, anti-HBe positive, HBV DNA <2,000 IU/mL, ALT normal. What is the correct interpretation?

A mass vaccination campaign reduces how easily an infection spreads through a community, which in turn protects some unvaccinated individuals who have not personally received the vaccine. What term describes this indirect, population-level protection?

UN4421.stem: Several days after completing a course of a broad-spectrum antibiotic, a patient develops profuse watery diarrhoea and crampy abdominal pain. Which diagnosis must be considered?

An inpatient on recent broad-spectrum antibiotics develops profuse watery diarrhoea, abdominal pain and a raised white cell count. Stool tests positive for Clostridioides difficile toxin. What is the most appropriate management?
UN4421.correct_answer: Stop the offending antibiotic, start oral vancomycin and isolate

UN4421.presentation: Risk Factor for a Severe Diarrhoeal Illness
UN4421.stem: A patient develops profuse, foul-smelling diarrhoea two weeks after a course of co-amoxiclav for a chest infection, and stool testing confirms *Clostridioides difficile* infection. What is the most important risk factor for this infection?
A 25-year-old backpacker develops sudden, frequent watery stools two days after arriving in India. There is no blood in the stool and only mild cramping. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN4421.presentation: C. difficile relapse within 12 weeks — antibiotic choice
UN4421.stem: A 76-year-old woman had a first episode of Clostridioides difficile infection treated with a course of oral vancomycin, and her diarrhoea settled. Three weeks after her symptoms resolved, she develops watery diarrhoea again, and a stool sample is positive for C. difficile toxin. She is not severely unwell. Which treatment is most appropriate?

An 81-year-old woman on a care of the elderly ward has been receiving co-amoxiclav and clarithromycin for a chest infection, which is now improving clinically. On day six she develops frequent watery stools, and a stool test is positive for Clostridioides difficile toxin. Alongside starting specific treatment, which further step matters most?
UN4421.correct_answer: Review and stop any antibiotics that are no longer essential

UN4421.stem: A 78-year-old woman in a nursing home develops profuse watery diarrhoea and abdominal cramps 5 days after completing co-amoxiclav for a chest infection. She is afebrile. What is the most likely causative organism?

A 78-year-old woman develops profuse watery diarrhoea 6 days into a course of co-amoxiclav for a chest infection. Stool tests are positive for Clostridioides difficile toxin. She is systemically well. What is the most appropriate first-line treatment?

UN4422.presentation: Infection control for suspected C. difficile
UN4422.stem: A 76-year-old man in a four-bed bay on an orthopaedic ward has developed three episodes of unexplained loose stool overnight after recent antibiotics. A stool sample has been sent for C. difficile testing. The nurse in charge asks what infection-control measures are needed now. What is the most appropriate advice?
UN4422.correct_answer: Side-room isolation, gloves and apron, and handwashing with soap and water

UN4422.presentation: Infection Control in Suspected Meningococcal Disease
UN4422.stem: A 4-year-old boy is brought to the paediatric emergency department with a high fever, lethargy and a spreading non-blanching purpuric rash on his legs. Intravenous ceftriaxone is given immediately and he is to be admitted. A nurse asks which infection control precautions staff should use while caring for him. What is the most appropriate answer?
UN4422.correct_answer: Droplet precautions in a single room

UN4422.stem:
A newly qualified nurse in a general practice treatment room tells a colleague that she only uses gloves, aprons and careful sharps disposal for patients known to have an infection such as hepatitis or HIV. Her colleague explains how standard infection control precautions should be applied.

Which statement is correct?
UN4422.correct_answer: They apply to every patient in every setting, at all times

UN4422.stem: A 79-year-old man is admitted to hospital with a urinary tract infection. His son explains that his father was managing well at home until yesterday, when he suddenly became confused and disorientated. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN4422.presentation: Suspected infectious diarrhoea on a ward
UN4422.stem: You are the doctor on a medical ward. A 66-year-old man in a six-bed bay is on day four of intravenous co-amoxiclav for pneumonia and has developed frequent, foul-smelling watery diarrhoea. A stool sample has been sent, but the result will not be back until tomorrow. What is the most appropriate immediate action?
UN4422.correct_answer: Move him to a side room now with contact precautions, gloves, apron and soap-and-water hand washing

UN4422.stem: A 78-year-old woman in a nursing home develops profuse watery diarrhoea and abdominal cramps 5 days after completing co-amoxiclav for a chest infection. She is afebrile. What is the most likely causative organism?

A 78-year-old woman develops profuse watery diarrhoea 6 days into a course of co-amoxiclav for a chest infection. Stool tests are positive for Clostridioides difficile toxin. She is systemically well. What is the most appropriate first-line treatment?

UN4422.presentation: Risk Factor for a Severe Diarrhoeal Illness
UN4422.stem: A patient develops profuse, foul-smelling diarrhoea two weeks after a course of co-amoxiclav for a chest infection, and stool testing confirms *Clostridioides difficile* infection. What is the most important risk factor for this infection?

UN4425.stem: A 68-year-old man develops a painful cluster of blistering lesions across the left side of his forehead and upper eyelid, sparing the tip of his nose. Which complication is particularly important to consider?

A 74-year-old man sees the out-of-hours GP. Three days ago he felt burning pain over his left forehead, and now clusters of fluid-filled blisters cover the left forehead and upper eyelid, stopping sharply at the midline. There is a vesicle on the tip of his nose and his left eye is red and watering. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN4425.presentation: Herpes zoster ophthalmicus in an immunocompromised patient
UN4425.stem: A 67-year-old man is receiving chemotherapy for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, with his last cycle 9 days ago. He presents with a two-day history of a painful vesicular rash over the right side of his forehead, upper eyelid and the tip of his nose, preceded by burning pain in the same area. His right eye feels gritty and slightly blurred. Temperature is 37.4°C and he is otherwise stable. Neutrophil count is 0.6 x 10^9/L. Right visual acuity is 6/9 and the conjunctiva is injected. What is the most appropriate management?
UN4425.correct_answer: Admit for IV aciclovir and same-day eye review

UN4425.stem: A 66-year-old man sees his GP with two days of burning pain followed by clusters of blisters on the left side of his forehead and scalp. On examination there are also vesicles on the side of the tip of his nose. His visual acuity is currently normal. Which complication is this distribution particularly associated with?
UN4425.correct_answer: Ocular involvement such as keratitis or uveitis

UN4425.stem: A 66-year-old man has had 3 days of burning pain followed by clustered vesicles over the right side of his forehead and upper eyelid. Today he has noticed new vesicles on the tip of his nose. His right eye is currently white and comfortable, with normal vision, and he is otherwise well. Which complication is he at particular risk of?

UN4425.presentation: Shingles — when to treat and refer
UN4425.stem: A 70-year-old presents within 48 hours of a painful vesicular rash in a single dermatome, with vesicles on the tip and side of the nose. What is the most appropriate management?
UN4425.correct_answer: Oral antiviral and urgent eye review

UN4425.stem: A patient has an acute facial (lower motor neurone) weakness on one side, together with a painful vesicular rash in and around the ear and ear canal on the same side, with some altered taste and hearing. What is the most likely diagnosis?
UN4425.correct_answer: Ramsay Hunt syndrome (geniculate ganglion herpes zoster)

UN4425.stem: A 74-year-old woman is seen as an urgent same-day appointment at her GP surgery. Two days ago she developed burning pain over the left side of her forehead, and she now has a band of blisters across the left forehead extending onto the side of her nose. Her left eye is watery and sore. What is the most appropriate management?
UN4425.correct_answer: Oral aciclovir and same-day ophthalmology assessment

UN4687.stem: A patient's urine dipstick is positive for nitrites and leucocyte esterase. In a patient with urinary symptoms, what does this most suggest?
A woman has fever with rigors, loin pain and tenderness, and dysuria with urinary frequency. Urine dipstick is positive for nitrites and leucocytes. What is the most appropriate management?
UN4687.correct_answer: Send a urine culture and start empirical antibiotics per local guidance

UN4687.stem: A 3-year-old girl presents with fever, vomiting, and abdominal pain. She has no urinary symptoms. Urine dipstick is positive for leucocytes and nitrites. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN4687.correct_answer: Send urine for culture and start empirical oral antibiotics

UN4687.stem: A 30-year-old woman has fever with rigors, loin pain and tenderness in the renal angle, with dysuria and urinary frequency. Urine dipstick is positive for nitrites and leucocytes. She is able to tolerate oral fluids and is haemodynamically stable. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A new urine dipstick test for UTI has a sensitivity of 85% and a specificity of 75%. In a population where the prevalence of UTI is 20%, a patient tests positive. Which statement is correct about the interpretation?
UN4687.correct_answer: Specificity 75% means 25% of people without UTI will test positive (false positive rate)

UN4687.stem: A 19-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by his flatmate with a few hours of fever, headache, vomiting and aching legs. He is drowsy but rousable. Which examination finding would most strongly suggest meningococcal septicaemia?
UN4687.correct_answer: Non-blanching petechiae on the trunk and legs

UN4687.stem: Ten days after a right total knee replacement, a 58-year-old woman sees her GP with a dull ache in her right calf. She is otherwise well. Which examination finding would most strongly suggest a deep vein thrombosis?
UN4687.correct_answer: Swelling of the right calf, which is clearly wider than the left

UN4687.stem: A new blood test for a disease is reported to have a sensitivity of 90%. What does this figure actually tell you?
UN4687.correct_answer: 90% of people with the disease will test positive

UN4721.stem: A mass vaccination campaign reduces how easily an infection spreads through a community, which in turn protects some unvaccinated individuals who have not personally received the vaccine. What term describes this indirect, population-level protection?
What is the usual mode of transmission for hepatitis A?

UN4721.presentation: Hepatitis B Exposure in an Immune Worker
UN4721.stem: A healthcare worker has a needlestick exposure to blood from a patient with chronic hepatitis B. The worker previously completed the hepatitis B vaccination course and has documented immunity on blood testing. How should this exposure be interpreted?
UN4721.correct_answer: The risk of transmission is substantially reduced by her documented immunity

UN4721.stem: A doctor diagnoses a patient with a notifiable infectious disease. The patient asks the doctor to keep it confidential and not tell anyone. What is the doctor's obligation?
UN4721.correct_answer: Notify the relevant public health authority, as required by law

UN4721.stem: A 70-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation has had a stable INR on warfarin for two years. At her anticoagulation clinic appointment she says that she is about to start a new healthy-eating plan with a large green smoothie of kale and spinach every day. What effect could this change have on her anticoagulation?
UN4721.correct_answer: Warfarin's anticoagulant effect may be reduced

UN4721.presentation: Effect of Low Prevalence on a Screening Test
UN4721.stem: A new screening test is rolled out across a population where the condition being tested for is rare. Even though the test's sensitivity and specificity remain unchanged, which property of the test is most affected by this low prevalence?
Through which route can hepatitis B be transmitted?
UN4721.correct_answer: Exposure to infected blood or body fluids

UN4721.presentation: Common Anatomical Position of the Appendix
UN4721.stem: If you had to pick the single most frequent anatomical position of the vermiform appendix in the general population, which site would you choose?

UN4850.stem: A healthcare worker sustains a needlestick injury from a needle used on a patient with known untreated HIV. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
UN4850.correct_answer: Wash, risk-assess and start HIV PEP as soon as possible

UN4850.stem:
A theatre nurse attends the occupational health department two days after blood from an HIV-positive patient splashed into her eye during an emergency laparotomy. She rinsed her eye at the time but did not report the incident until today. The source patient had recently stopped antiretroviral therapy and his viral load is detectable.

What should be offered now?
UN4850.correct_answer: A 28-day course of HIV post-exposure prophylaxis started as soon as possible today

UN4850.presentation: Deciding Post-Exposure Management After Hepatitis B Exposure
UN4850.stem: A healthcare assistant is splashed with blood from a patient known to carry hepatitis B. What mainly determines whether post-exposure treatment is required?
UN4850.correct_answer: The assistant's hepatitis B immunity and the type of exposure

UN4850.presentation: Measles exposure in pregnancy — post-exposure prophylaxis
UN4850.stem: A 27-year-old woman who is 20 weeks pregnant was in the same room as a child with confirmed measles 3 days ago. She was never vaccinated and has never had measles. She is well. Her measles IgG antibody test is negative. Which is the most appropriate post-exposure prophylaxis?
A woman at 30 weeks' gestation, with no history of chickenpox, has significant household exposure to a child with chickenpox. Her varicella IgG is negative. What is the most appropriate management?

A 24-year-old woman attends her GP the day after returning from a trip to rural India. Three days ago a stray cat scratched her forearm hard enough to draw blood. She washed the wound with bottled water, and the cat ran off. She feels well and the scratch is healing without signs of infection. Which is the best management?
UN4850.correct_answer: Urgent risk assessment for rabies post-exposure prophylaxis

UN4850.presentation: Hepatitis B Exposure in an Immune Worker
UN4850.stem: A healthcare worker has a needlestick exposure to blood from a patient with chronic hepatitis B. The worker previously completed the hepatitis B vaccination course and has documented immunity on blood testing. How should this exposure be interpreted?
UN4850.correct_answer: The risk of transmission is substantially reduced by her documented immunity

UN4850.stem: After first aid for a needlestick, the source patient is found to be hepatitis B surface-antigen positive. The exposed healthcare worker was fully vaccinated and is a documented responder (adequate anti-HBs). What is the most appropriate action regarding hepatitis B?
UN4850.correct_answer: A hepatitis B vaccine booster dose

UN4851.presentation: Needlestick with Known Hepatitis B Immunity
UN4851.stem: A 38-year-old paramedic sustains a needlestick injury from a patient known to be hepatitis B surface-antigen positive. She completed her hepatitis B vaccination course 6 years ago and has documented immunity. What is generally required in this situation?
UN4851.correct_answer: A hepatitis B vaccine booster dose

UN4851.stem: A healthcare worker sustains a needlestick injury from a needle used on a patient with known untreated HIV. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
UN4851.correct_answer: Wash, risk-assess and start HIV PEP as soon as possible

UN4851.stem:
A newly qualified healthcare assistant attends occupational health to start her hepatitis B vaccine course. She asks whether she can also be vaccinated against hepatitis C at the same appointment, since she will be handling blood samples.

What is the correct response?
UN4851.correct_answer: No, there is no licensed vaccine that prevents hepatitis C

UN4851.correct_answer: Hepatitis B vaccination should be offered based on the individual's occupational risk

UN4851.correct_answer: The risk of transmission is substantially reduced by her documented immunity

UN4851.stem: After first aid for a needlestick, the source patient is found to be hepatitis B surface-antigen positive. The exposed healthcare worker was fully vaccinated and is a documented responder (adequate anti-HBs). What is the most appropriate action regarding hepatitis B?
UN4851.correct_answer: A hepatitis B vaccine booster dose

UN4851.stem: A 29-year-old nurse sustains a needlestick injury from a used needle while caring for a patient whose bloodborne virus status is unknown. What should she do first?
UN4851.correct_answer: Wash the affected area immediately with soap and running water

UN4851.stem:
A 26-year-old newly qualified midwife sustains a deep needlestick while suturing a perineal tear. The woman she was caring for is known to be hepatitis B surface antigen positive. The midwife washes the wound but cannot remember whether she completed her hepatitis B vaccine course.

What is the most appropriate next step?
UN4851.correct_answer: Urgent same-day assessment for hepatitis B prophylaxis

UN4854.stem:
A 29-year-old woman has a reactive fourth-generation HIV test confirmed at the sexual health clinic. Before discussing treatment and the need for prophylaxis against opportunistic infections, the team wants to know how far her immune system has been damaged.

Which blood test gives this information?

A 26-year-old woman has a positive HIV test at a sexual health clinic during routine screening. She feels well and has no symptoms. Her CD4 count is within the normal range and her viral load is moderately raised. She asks whether she can wait a few years before taking any medication. What is the most appropriate advice?
UN4854.correct_answer: Offer antiretroviral therapy now, whatever her CD4 count

UN4854.presentation: Early syphilis with penicillin anaphylaxis — alternative antibiotic
UN4854.stem: A 34-year-old man is diagnosed with secondary syphilis in a sexual health clinic. He has a documented history of anaphylaxis to amoxicillin. He has no neurological, eye or ear symptoms and his HIV test is negative. Which antibiotic is the most appropriate alternative to penicillin?

A 28-year-old man presents with a 10-day history of fever, myalgia, sore throat, and a maculopapular rash. He is otherwise well. He had unprotected sexual intercourse with a new partner 4 weeks ago. He is concerned about HIV. You perform a 4th-generation HIV test (antigen/antibody combination). The test comes back negative. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN4854.correct_answer: Order an HIV viral load (PCR) test now

UN4854.presentation: STI Screening in an Asymptomatic Patient
UN4854.stem: A 27-year-old woman who has recently started a new sexual relationship asks whether she should have a sexual health screen even though she has no symptoms. What is the most appropriate response?
UN4854.correct_answer: Discuss appropriate testing according to sexual history and risk

UN4854.presentation: NAAT-positive gonorrhoea — sample needed before treatment
UN4854.stem: A 23-year-old woman attends a sexual health clinic after a self-taken vulvovaginal swab from an online testing service was positive for Neisseria gonorrhoeae on a nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT). She has no symptoms. Pharyngeal and rectal NAAT swabs have just been taken, and blood has been sent for HIV and syphilis testing. Which additional test should be taken before she is given antibiotics?

A 27-year-old woman is told at a sexual health clinic that her test for chlamydia is positive. The health adviser explains that people she has had sex with recently will need to be contacted, and offers to do this anonymously. She asks why this is necessary. What is the main purpose of this process?
UN4854.correct_answer: To ensure exposed partners are offered testing and treatment

UN4854.presentation: Chlamydia testing in women — specimen of choice
UN4854.stem: A 22-year-old woman with no symptoms asks her GP practice for a chlamydia test after starting a relationship with a new partner. She has had vaginal sex only. Which specimen is most appropriate for a chlamydia nucleic acid amplification test?

UN4855.presentation: Infection Control in Suspected Meningococcal Disease
UN4855.stem: A 4-year-old boy is brought to the paediatric emergency department with a high fever, lethargy and a spreading non-blanching purpuric rash on his legs. Intravenous ceftriaxone is given immediately and he is to be admitted. A nurse asks which infection control precautions staff should use while caring for him. What is the most appropriate answer?
UN4855.correct_answer: Droplet precautions in a single room

Which statement is correct?
UN4855.correct_answer: They apply to every patient in every setting, at all times

UN4855.stem: A patient with a persistent cough, weight loss and night sweats is being investigated for possible active pulmonary tuberculosis. Which investigation is especially important for microbiological confirmation?
