UN4855.stem: A 76-year-old man in a four-bed bay on an orthopaedic ward has developed three episodes of unexplained loose stool overnight after recent antibiotics. A stool sample has been sent for C. difficile testing. The nurse in charge asks what infection-control measures are needed now. What is the most appropriate advice?
UN4855.correct_answer: Side-room isolation, gloves and apron, and handwashing with soap and water

UN4855.stem: A patient is diagnosed with active pulmonary tuberculosis. What is the most appropriate standard initial drug regimen?
UN4855.correct_answer: Rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol, with pyridoxine

UN4855.stem: A 46-year-old man living in a homeless hostel sees the visiting GP. For two months he has had a productive cough, occasionally with streaks of blood, and he wakes drenched in sweat most nights. His trousers have become loose. Another resident of the hostel was recently started on a long course of treatment for a chest infection. Which diagnosis is most likely?

A 52-year-old man living in a homeless hostel attends a walk-in centre with two months of cough, occasionally bringing up streaks of blood. He wakes drenched in sweat most nights, feels feverish in the evenings and his trousers have become loose. A fellow resident was admitted to hospital with tuberculosis last month. He smokes 15 cigarettes a day. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old man who works as a bus driver is diagnosed with sputum smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis after months of cough and weight loss. His wife, who shares his bedroom, is referred to the TB service for contact screening.

By which route is she most likely to have been exposed?
UN4855.correct_answer: Inhaling droplet nuclei released when he coughs

UN4861.presentation: Lymphoma after chemotherapy — live vaccine contraindicated
UN4861.stem: A 31-year-old woman completed chemotherapy for classical Hodgkin lymphoma 3 months ago and is in complete remission. She plans to visit relatives in rural Ghana in 6 weeks and attends her GP practice for travel vaccines. She has no other medical history and takes no regular medicines. Which vaccine is contraindicated for her at present?

In the emergency department, a patient thought to be having an acute coronary event has no history of aspirin sensitivity or any other reason to avoid it. Which drug should be given straight away for its antiplatelet effect?

UN4861.presentation: Child on high-dose prednisolone for nephrotic relapse — live vaccine
UN4861.stem: A 4-year-old boy weighing 16 kg has steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome. Ten days ago he started a course of high-dose daily prednisolone for a relapse. He has not yet had his pre-school dose of measles, mumps, rubella and varicella (MMRV) vaccine, and his mother asks the practice nurse to give it at today's appointment. He is well apart from mild ankle oedema. What is the most appropriate advice?
UN4861.correct_answer: Defer MMRV until 3 months after high-dose steroids stop

UN4861.stem:
A 28-year-old woman who is in the second trimester of her first pregnancy attends her antenatal appointment in October. She is otherwise well and has no long-term conditions. The midwife offers the seasonal flu vaccine, but she says a friend warned her that the injection could give her flu and harm the baby, so she would rather wait until after the birth.

Which is the most appropriate advice?
UN4861.correct_answer: Have the inactivated vaccine now, as it protects her and gives her baby early protection

UN4861.presentation: Needlestick with Known Hepatitis B Immunity
UN4861.stem: A 38-year-old paramedic sustains a needlestick injury from a patient known to be hepatitis B surface-antigen positive. She completed her hepatitis B vaccination course 6 years ago and has documented immunity. What is generally required in this situation?
UN4861.correct_answer: A hepatitis B vaccine booster dose

UN4861.stem: A patient attends with a deep, dirty puncture wound from a garden fork. Their tetanus immunisation history is uncertain/incomplete. What is the most appropriate management regarding tetanus?
UN4861.correct_answer: Tetanus-containing vaccine and tetanus immunoglobulin, with wound care

UN4861.stem:
A health visitor is seeing an 8-month-old girl, born in the UK in early 2026, for a routine developmental review. Her father says she has had all her vaccines so far, and he asks at what age she will receive her first vaccine against measles under the routine UK schedule. She is well and has no medical problems.

What is the correct answer?
UN4861.correct_answer: At 12 months, on or after her first birthday

UN4861.presentation: Anaphylaxis to a previous vaccine dose
UN4861.stem:
The mother of a 4-month-old girl brings her for the next dose of a routine vaccine. The records show that minutes after the previous dose of the same vaccine the baby developed widespread hives, wheeze and floppiness, and was treated with intramuscular adrenaline in the surgery.

What is the most appropriate plan?
UN4861.correct_answer: Withhold further doses until specialist advice is obtained

UN4900.stem: A 39-year-old man returns from three weeks in rural sub-Saharan Africa and develops fever, headache and a diffuse maculopapular rash. He admits he did not take any malaria chemoprophylaxis. Which investigation is particularly important to perform urgently?
A traveller returning from sub-Saharan Africa has a fever, rigors, headache and myalgia. A blood film shows Plasmodium falciparum parasites. What is the most important immediate consideration?
UN4900.correct_answer: Assess for severe/complicated malaria and treat urgently (can be rapidly fatal)

UN4900.stem: A traveller returning from sub-Saharan Africa has fever, and a blood film confirms Plasmodium falciparum with a parasitaemia of 6%, plus impaired consciousness and acidosis. How should this be classified and managed?
UN4900.correct_answer: Severe/complicated malaria — admit and give IV artesunate

UN4900.stem: A 52-year-old man attends the emergency department ten days after returning from visiting relatives in Nigeria. He did not take antimalarial tablets. He has had three days of fever with drenching sweats, aching muscles and headache. He looks mildly jaundiced, and his blood tests show a low platelet count. Which diagnosis is the priority to exclude today?
A 40-year-old man presents with fevers, rigors and headache ten days after returning from a work trip to Nigeria. Which investigation should be performed as a priority?
UN4900.correct_answer: Thick and thin blood films for malaria parasites

UN4900.stem: A 27-year-old woman attends the emergency department 10 days after returning from visiting family in Nigeria. She has had fevers, headache and muscle aches for three days. She is alert, eating and drinking normally and has no vomiting. A pregnancy test is negative. Blood films show Plasmodium falciparum at low parasitaemia, and her renal function, glucose and haemoglobin are normal. What is the most appropriate treatment?

A GP reviews a 39-year-old man with a high temperature, sweats and headache for two days. He works for an engineering firm and has made several work trips overseas this year, some of them to tropical countries. The GP is considering malaria.

Which part of the history is most important to establish?
UN4900.correct_answer: Exactly where and when he travelled

UN4900.stem: A man develops a painful, swollen calf shortly after returning from a 12-hour long-haul flight. Which physiological factor from prolonged sitting is most responsible for his increased risk of venous thrombosis?
UN4900.correct_answer: Venous stasis caused by prolonged immobility

UN4903.stem: A 31-year-old woman develops diarrhoea after returning from travel abroad. She looks clinically well and there is no blood in her stool. What is the most appropriate initial advice?
A 25-year-old backpacker develops sudden, frequent watery stools two days after arriving in India. There is no blood in the stool and only mild cramping. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old woman telephones her GP surgery two days after getting back from a fortnight in Thailand. Since yesterday she has opened her bowels about six times a day with loose, watery stool. There has been no blood or mucus, she feels mildly warm but not unwell, and she is managing to drink and is passing urine normally. What should be the first priority in her care?
UN4903.correct_answer: Oral rehydration with fluids and oral rehydration salts

UN4903.stem: Several days after completing a course of a broad-spectrum antibiotic, a patient develops profuse watery diarrhoea and crampy abdominal pain. Which diagnosis must be considered?

A 34-year-old man phones his GP surgery on the fourth day of a course of clarithromycin prescribed for a chest infection. His cough is improving, but he has developed loose stools a few times a day with mild cramping. He has no blood in the stool, no fever and no vomiting, and he is eating and drinking normally. He has not travelled recently. What is the most likely cause of his diarrhoea?

A 78-year-old woman develops profuse watery diarrhoea 6 days into a course of co-amoxiclav for a chest infection. Stool tests are positive for Clostridioides difficile toxin. She is systemically well. What is the most appropriate first-line treatment?

UN4903.presentation: Acute infective gastroenteritis in a traveller
UN4903.stem: Three days after returning from a fortnight in Thailand, a 30-year-old woman calls NHS 111. Since yesterday she has had several episodes of vomiting, cramping abdominal pain and frequent watery stools with no blood. She is drinking, passing urine and feels only mildly feverish. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 78-year-old woman in a nursing home develops profuse watery diarrhoea and abdominal cramps 5 days after completing co-amoxiclav for a chest infection. She is afebrile. What is the most likely causative organism?

UN4934.stem: A man has a purulent urethral discharge and dysuria, and a swab confirms Neisseria gonorrhoeae. What is the most appropriate treatment, alongside partner notification?

UN4934.presentation: Epididymo-orchitis with gonococcal infection — antibiotic choice
UN4934.stem:
A 23-year-old man attends a sexual health clinic with 4 days of right scrotal pain and swelling and a urethral discharge. He had condomless sex with a new partner 2 weeks ago. The epididymis is tender and swollen, the testis lies normally, and torsion is considered unlikely. Microscopy of a urethral smear shows Gram-negative intracellular diplococci. He has no drug allergies.

Which treatment is most appropriate?

A 22-year-old woman sees her GP for the third time in four months with burning on passing urine and frequency. Urine samples sent at her last two visits showed white cells but grew no organisms, and her symptoms did not settle with antibiotics for cystitis. She now also mentions a change in vaginal discharge and some bleeding after sex. She has had a new partner in the last six months and they do not use condoms. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old man attends a sexual health clinic. Three days after unprotected sex with a new partner he developed stinging on passing urine, and since yesterday a thick, yellow-green discharge has been staining his underwear. He has no genital ulcers, rash or fever. Which organism is most likely responsible?
A 25-year-old man has dysuria and a profuse purulent urethral discharge. A NAAT and culture confirm Neisseria gonorrhoeae. What is the most appropriate first-line treatment?

A 22-year-old woman has post-coital bleeding and a mucopurulent cervical discharge. A nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT) is positive for Chlamydia trachomatis. What is the most appropriate management?
UN4934.correct_answer: Doxycycline, plus partner notification and testing

UN4934.stem: A 29-year-old man presents with pain on passing urine and discharge from the urethra after a recent episode of unprotected sex. Which investigation is commonly used to test for chlamydia and gonorrhoea?

UN4934.presentation: Gradual Scrotal Pain With Urethral Symptoms
UN4934.stem: A sexually active 25-year-old man develops scrotal swelling and discomfort on the right side that has worsened steadily over three days, along with pain on passing urine and a clear urethral discharge. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN5030.stem: A 19-year-old woman has fever, severe headache, neck stiffness and photophobia, and is becoming drowsy. She has a non-blanching purpuric rash. Suspected meningococcal meningitis with septicaemia. What is the most appropriate immediate management?

UN5030.presentation: Fever, Neck Stiffness and Non-Blanching Rash
UN5030.stem: A university student presents with fever, a severe headache, neck stiffness and a rash that does not fade under pressure. She is becoming increasingly drowsy. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old student presents with fever, confusion and hypotension. There is a rapidly spreading non-blanching purpuric rash. Neck stiffness is absent. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
UN5030.correct_answer: Immediate IV ceftriaxone (do not delay for investigations)

UN5030.stem: A 3-year-old presents with fever, vomiting, and a widespread non-blanching purpuric rash that has spread over 2 hours. He is drowsy with a capillary refill time of 4 seconds and a heart rate of 145 bpm. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
UN5030.correct_answer: IV ceftriaxone now, without awaiting investigations

UN5030.stem: A 19-year-old student presents with a 12-hour history of fever, severe headache, neck stiffness and a non-blanching petechial rash. He is drowsy with a blood pressure of 100/60. What is the most appropriate immediate treatment?

A 22-year-old man develops cramping abdominal pain and bloody diarrhoea three days after eating an undercooked beef burger at a barbecue. Which organism is particularly associated with this presentation?

A 19-year-old university student presents to ED with a 6-hour history of fever, headache, vomiting, and myalgia. He is tachycardic (HR 110 bpm), hypotensive (BP 96/58 mmHg), and has a widespread purpuric rash that is non-blanching. He is confused. What is the single most important immediate action?
UN5030.correct_answer: IV ceftriaxone 2 g now — do not wait for investigations

UN5030.presentation: Infection Control in Suspected Meningococcal Disease
UN5030.stem: A 4-year-old boy is brought to the paediatric emergency department with a high fever, lethargy and a spreading non-blanching purpuric rash on his legs. Intravenous ceftriaxone is given immediately and he is to be admitted. A nurse asks which infection control precautions staff should use while caring for him. What is the most appropriate answer?
UN5030.correct_answer: Droplet precautions in a single room

UN5094.stem: A woman presents with pain on passing urine, frequent voiding and suprapubic discomfort, with no vaginal discharge and no fever. What is the likely diagnosis?
Which of the following urinary symptoms is classified as a 'voiding' lower urinary tract symptom, commonly associated with bladder outlet obstruction?
When urinary symptoms are grouped into categories based on the phase of the bladder cycle they affect, which option below belongs in the 'storage' group?

UN5094.presentation: Prescribing for yourself or a close family member
UN5094.stem: You are an FY2 doctor. Your mother telephones you at home. She has had two days of dysuria and urinary frequency, is otherwise well, and asks you to write her a prescription for trimethoprim so that she does not have to wait for a GP appointment. You are confident this is an uncomplicated urinary tract infection. What is the most appropriate action?
UN5094.correct_answer: Decline, and advise her to contact her own GP or out-of-hours service

UN5094.presentation: Lower urinary tract infection in pregnancy
UN5094.stem:
A 24-year-old woman who is 14 weeks pregnant attends her GP with two days of stinging when she passes urine and a need to go every hour or so. She has no temperature, loin pain or vaginal discharge and is otherwise well.

What is the most appropriate management?
UN5094.correct_answer: Send a midstream urine culture and start a suitable antibiotic immediately

UN5094.stem: A patient's urine dipstick is positive for nitrites and leucocyte esterase. In a patient with urinary symptoms, what does this most suggest?
A woman has fever with rigors, loin pain and tenderness, and dysuria with urinary frequency. Urine dipstick is positive for nitrites and leucocytes. What is the most appropriate management?
UN5094.correct_answer: Send a urine culture and start empirical antibiotics per local guidance

UN5094.stem: A 30-year-old woman has fever with rigors, loin pain and tenderness in the renal angle, with dysuria and urinary frequency. Urine dipstick is positive for nitrites and leucocytes. She is able to tolerate oral fluids and is haemodynamically stable. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN5105.stem: A 31-year-old woman develops diarrhoea after returning from travel abroad. She looks clinically well and there is no blood in her stool. What is the most appropriate initial advice?
Several days after completing a course of a broad-spectrum antibiotic, a patient develops profuse watery diarrhoea and crampy abdominal pain. Which diagnosis must be considered?

A 65-year-old man develops fever, cough and diarrhoea several days after returning from a hotel stay. The hotel reports that a handful of other guests have become unwell with similar symptoms around the same time. Which organism is the most likely cause?

A 27-year-old woman attends the emergency department 10 days after returning from visiting family in Nigeria. She has had fevers, headache and muscle aches for three days. She is alert, eating and drinking normally and has no vomiting. A pregnancy test is negative. Blood films show Plasmodium falciparum at low parasitaemia, and her renal function, glucose and haemoglobin are normal. What is the most appropriate treatment?
A 19-year-old backpacker develops diarrhoea after eating from a street stall abroad, and several travel companions who shared the meal are affected too. What is the most likely mechanism?

A 22-year-old man develops cramping abdominal pain and bloody diarrhoea three days after eating an undercooked beef burger at a barbecue. Which organism is particularly associated with this presentation?

A 26-year-old woman telephones her GP surgery two days after getting back from a fortnight in Thailand. Since yesterday she has opened her bowels about six times a day with loose, watery stool. There has been no blood or mucus, she feels mildly warm but not unwell, and she is managing to drink and is passing urine normally. What should be the first priority in her care?
UN5105.correct_answer: Oral rehydration with fluids and oral rehydration salts

UN5105.stem: A patient with several days of profuse watery diarrhoea is found to have a metabolic acidosis on blood gas analysis. Loss of which gastrointestinal secretion is primarily responsible for this acid-base disturbance?

UN5266.stem: A man has a single painless, indurated genital ulcer (chancre) with non-tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. Treponemal serology is positive. What is the most appropriate treatment?

UN5266.presentation: Painless genital ulcer: referral for syphilis testing
UN5266.stem:
A 44-year-old man sees his GP about a sore in the groove just behind the head of his penis, which he noticed about a week ago. It is a single ulcer with a clean base and a firm, rubbery edge, and it does not hurt. He has had several new male partners over the past three months.

Which is the most appropriate next step?
UN5266.correct_answer: Refer urgently to sexual health for syphilis testing

UN5266.stem: A 34-year-old man attends a sexual health clinic because of a sore on the shaft of his penis that appeared ten days ago. He had condomless sex with a new male partner about four weeks ago. The lesion is a single, firm, clean-based ulcer that does not hurt even when pressed. There are rubbery, non-tender enlarged nodes in both groins. He feels well. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old man sees his GP about a sore on his lower lip that appeared roughly three weeks after he began a new relationship and has been present for ten days. It has never been tender. There is a single firm, clean-based ulcer on the lip, and a non-tender, rubbery submandibular lymph node can be felt on the same side. He has no history of cold sores. What is the most likely cause?

UN5266.presentation: Asymptomatic sexual contact of early syphilis
UN5266.stem: A 34-year-old man attends a sexual health clinic because his regular male partner was diagnosed with primary syphilis last week. They last had sex 10 days ago. He has no symptoms, and examination of the genitals, mouth, skin and lymph nodes is normal. He has no drug allergies. Blood is taken for syphilis serology. What is the most appropriate management?
UN5266.correct_answer: Offer epidemiological treatment for syphilis today

UN5266.stem: A 25-year-old woman develops a single oval, scaly, salmon-coloured patch on her trunk, followed a week later by many smaller similar lesions along the skin cleavage lines in a 'fir-tree' pattern on her back. She is otherwise well. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old woman attends a sexual health clinic with 3 days of painful genital ulcers and dysuria. Examination shows several shallow, tender ulcers on the labia with tender inguinal lymph nodes. Genital herpes is suspected. Which test is most appropriate to confirm the diagnosis?
UN5266.correct_answer: Swab of an ulcer base for HSV NAAT

UN5266.stem: A patient recently started on an SGLT2 inhibitor for type 2 diabetes develops recurrent itching and discharge around the genital area. Which adverse effect is characteristically linked to this drug class?

UN5307.stem: A 50-year-old man with a native aortic valve has definite infective endocarditis. Blood cultures grow Streptococcus viridans (penicillin-sensitive). He is haemodynamically stable with no complications. What is the most appropriate antibiotic regimen?
UN5307.correct_answer: IV benzylpenicillin or IV amoxicillin for 4 weeks

UN5307.stem: You are about to treat someone for probable infective endocarditis, and they are not acutely unwell. Which test should be organised before the first dose of antibiotics goes in?
UN5307.correct_answer: Taking multiple sets of blood cultures

UN5307.stem: A 66-year-old woman receiving chemotherapy for ovarian cancer is admitted with rigors and a fever, and neutropenic sepsis is suspected. Intravenous antibiotics are being prepared. Which investigation should be taken first, as long as it does not delay the antibiotics?
Someone who had valve replacement surgery in the past now feels generally unwell with a lingering temperature, and the clinician hears a murmur that wasn't there before. What diagnosis fits?

A 45-year-old intravenous drug user has two weeks of fever, malaise and night sweats. Examination reveals a new heart murmur, splinter haemorrhages and painful nodules on the finger pulps. What is the most important initial investigation pair?

A 35-year-old intravenous drug user presents with 3 weeks of fever, night sweats, and weight loss. He has a new pansystolic murmur at the lower left sternal edge worsening on inspiration. Blood cultures grow Staphylococcus aureus. Echocardiogram shows a vegetation on the tricuspid valve. What is the most likely diagnosis using the Duke criteria?
Which patient carries the highest risk of infective endocarditis?
UN5307.correct_answer: A patient with a prosthetic heart valve

UN5307.stem: A 50-year-old man with infective endocarditis on appropriate IV antibiotics develops worsening breathlessness with new severe mitral regurgitation and signs of heart failure. Echocardiography shows a large vegetation and valve destruction. What is the most appropriate next step?

UN5385.stem: A 31-year-old woman develops diarrhoea after returning from travel abroad. She looks clinically well and there is no blood in her stool. What is the most appropriate initial advice?

A 26-year-old woman telephones her GP surgery two days after getting back from a fortnight in Thailand. Since yesterday she has opened her bowels about six times a day with loose, watery stool. There has been no blood or mucus, she feels mildly warm but not unwell, and she is managing to drink and is passing urine normally. What should be the first priority in her care?
UN5385.correct_answer: Oral rehydration with fluids and oral rehydration salts

UN5385.stem: A 38-year-old woman is admitted with three days of profuse watery diarrhoea after returning from a holiday abroad. She feels weak and her legs feel heavy. Her ECG shows flattened T waves, ST depression and a prominent extra wave after each T wave, making the QT interval appear long. Which electrolyte abnormality is most likely?
Several days after completing a course of a broad-spectrum antibiotic, a patient develops profuse watery diarrhoea and crampy abdominal pain. Which diagnosis must be considered?
A 19-year-old backpacker develops diarrhoea after eating from a street stall abroad, and several travel companions who shared the meal are affected too. What is the most likely mechanism?
A 25-year-old backpacker develops sudden, frequent watery stools two days after arriving in India. There is no blood in the stool and only mild cramping. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 78-year-old woman in a nursing home develops profuse watery diarrhoea and abdominal cramps 5 days after completing co-amoxiclav for a chest infection. She is afebrile. What is the most likely causative organism?

A 22-year-old man develops cramping abdominal pain and bloody diarrhoea three days after eating an undercooked beef burger at a barbecue. Which organism is particularly associated with this presentation?

UN5615.presentation: Painful Bilateral Swelling Below the Ears
UN5615.stem: A child presents with fever and tender swelling below both ears, with the parotid glands clearly enlarged and painful to touch. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A teenage boy develops a painful, swollen testis several days after his parotid glands swelled up. What complication is this?

A 7-year-old girl is seen by her GP with fever and tender swelling of both parotid glands. She has had no MMR vaccines. The GP is confident clinically that this is mumps and has advised rest, fluids and paracetamol. No laboratory test has yet been done.

What is the most appropriate action regarding public health?
UN5615.correct_answer: Notify the health protection team now

UN5615.stem: A 19-year-old university student is seen in general practice with 2 days of fever and painful swelling of both parotid glands. He has not had the MMR vaccine. He is well enough to manage at home, and the GP has notified the health protection team and arranged an oral fluid test. Which new symptom should he be told to seek urgent medical review for?

A 14-year-old boy who has not received any MMR vaccines is brought to the emergency department. A week ago he developed painful swelling of both parotid glands, and over the last day he has had a worsening headache, has vomited several times and finds bright light uncomfortable. He is alert, his neck is stiff on flexion and there is no rash.

Which complication is most likely?

A 19-year-old university student who was never vaccinated attends an urgent treatment centre. A week ago he had fever and painful swelling below both ears that made chewing difficult. Since yesterday his right testis has become progressively painful and swollen and his temperature has risen again. The testis is enlarged and tender, it lies in a normal position and the cremasteric reflex is present. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old university student has fever and painful swelling in front of both ears that started 2 days ago. Several students in his hall of residence have similar symptoms. He is unsure whether he had the MMR vaccine. The local health protection team asks the GP to arrange confirmation of the diagnosis.

Which sample is most appropriate?

UN5615.presentation: Painful Swelling at the Nail Fold
UN5615.stem: A regular nail-biter develops a painful, red, swollen area at the side of the nail on their index finger over the past two days. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN5687.stem: A patient with acute hepatitis has the following serology: HBsAg POSITIVE, anti-HBc IgM POSITIVE, anti-HBs NEGATIVE. How is this best interpreted?

A 28-year-old man presents with a 10-day history of fever, myalgia, sore throat, and a maculopapular rash. He is otherwise well. He had unprotected sexual intercourse with a new partner 4 weeks ago. He is concerned about HIV. You perform a 4th-generation HIV test (antigen/antibody combination). The test comes back negative. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN5687.correct_answer: Order an HIV viral load (PCR) test now

UN5687.presentation: Mild Jaundice In A Well Newborn
UN5687.stem: Mild jaundice develops in an otherwise well 4-day-old infant, with blood tests showing mostly unconjugated bilirubin. What is the most likely explanation?
A heavy drinker develops jaundice, fever and a tender, enlarged liver. What should be considered?

A 68-year-old man presents with two weeks of progressive painless jaundice, dark urine, pale stools and weight loss. Examination reveals a palpable, non-tender gallbladder. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A woman keeps getting symptomatic urinary infections. Which factor in her history is particularly worth asking about?

UN5687.presentation: Painless obstructive jaundice with suspected pancreatic cancer — imaging
UN5687.stem: A 72-year-old man presents with 2 weeks of painless jaundice, dark urine, and pale stools. He has lost 4 kg unintentionally. No abdominal pain. Examination: palpable non-tender gallbladder. What is the most appropriate imaging investigation?

UN5687.presentation: Haematuria With Hypertension After a Throat Infection
UN5687.stem: Two weeks after a streptococcal sore throat, a 7-year-old develops visibly dark urine, a blood pressure above the normal range for his age, and a rising creatinine. Which syndrome best describes this presentation?

UN5730.stem: A 19-year-old has a sore throat, fever, marked cervical lymphadenopathy and lethargy, with atypical lymphocytes on the blood film. Which is the most appropriate advice?
UN5730.correct_answer: Avoid amoxicillin and contact sports (risk of rash and splenic rupture)

UN5730.stem: A patient presents with a sore throat, fever, tonsillar exudate and tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy, and reports no cough. According to NICE guidance (NG84), which scoring systems should be used to estimate the likelihood of bacterial infection and guide antibiotic prescribing?

UN5730.presentation: Sore throat while taking carbimazole — immediate action
UN5730.stem: A 34-year-old woman phones her GP surgery with a 2-day history of sore throat, fever and mouth ulcers. She started carbimazole for Graves disease 6 weeks ago. She sounds unwell but is not short of breath. What is the most appropriate action?
UN5730.correct_answer: Stop carbimazole and check a full blood count today

UN5730.presentation: Fever, Neck Stiffness and Non-Blanching Rash
UN5730.stem: A university student presents with fever, a severe headache, neck stiffness and a rash that does not fade under pressure. She is becoming increasingly drowsy. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old woman has fever, sore throat and enlarged neck glands, followed by severe tiredness and an enlarged liver and spleen. Blood film shows atypical lymphocytes. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old university student notices visible blood in his urine on two occasions, each starting within a day or two of a sore throat. Between episodes his urine is clear and his renal function is normal. What diagnosis should be considered?

A 6-year-old child has a sore throat, fever, and a fine sandpaper-textured rash on the trunk and in the flexures. Examination shows a strawberry tongue and pallor around the mouth. What is the causative organism and first-line treatment?

UN5730.presentation: Tender Shin Nodules After Sore Throat
UN5730.stem: A 29-year-old woman develops several tender, red, raised nodules on both shins about two weeks after a streptococcal sore throat. The lesions are firm swellings rather than open sores. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN5733.stem: A man with advanced HIV (CD4 count 50 cells/µL) and poor treatment adherence presents with headache, fever and a focal neurological deficit. Contrast CT of the brain shows multiple RING-ENHANCING lesions. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN5733.presentation: Cerebral toxoplasmosis in advanced HIV — first-line treatment
UN5733.stem:
A 38-year-old man with newly diagnosed advanced HIV and a very low CD4 count presents with headache, fever and right-sided weakness. MRI of the brain shows multiple ring-enhancing lesions in the basal ganglia, and Toxoplasma IgG is positive. The HIV team diagnose presumed cerebral toxoplasmosis and start empirical treatment.

Which is the preferred first-line treatment?

A 38-year-old woman who stopped her antiretroviral therapy two years ago is brought in by her sister. For the past three weeks she has had a slowly worsening headache, low-grade fevers and, more recently, episodes of confusion. Her last CD4 count was very low. There is minimal neck stiffness and no focal weakness.

Which opportunistic infection should be considered first?

A man with newly diagnosed HIV has a CD4 count of 150 cells/mm3. Alongside starting antiretroviral therapy, which prophylaxis is most important to prevent the commonest serious opportunistic infection at this count?

UN5733.presentation: Papilloedema with suspected IIH — image before lumbar puncture
UN5733.stem:
A 30-year-old woman is referred to the acute medical unit by her optometrist, who saw swelling of both optic discs at a routine eye test. For a month she has had a daily headache that is worse when she lies down and when she coughs. She has gained weight over the past year and is otherwise well, with no fever, neck stiffness or focal neurological signs. The medical registrar suspects idiopathic intracranial hypertension (raised brain pressure with no identifiable cause) and suggests a lumbar puncture this afternoon to measure the opening pressure. No brain imaging has been done.

What should be the next investigation?

A 52-year-old woman has a 1-week history of headache, fever and confusion following a severe sinus infection. Contrast-enhanced MRI shows a single 2 cm ring-enhancing lesion in the left frontal lobe with surrounding oedema. Blood cultures have been taken and the neurosurgical team will review her today. She has no drug allergies. Which empirical antibiotic regimen is most appropriate?

An overweight young woman has headaches, transient visual obscurations and pulsatile tinnitus. Fundoscopy shows papilloedema, but neurological examination is otherwise normal and brain imaging shows no mass or hydrocephalus. Lumbar puncture shows a raised opening pressure with normal constituents. What is the diagnosis?

UN5733.presentation: Acute mastoiditis — imaging when not improving
UN5733.stem: A 6-year-old boy was admitted 24 hours ago with acute mastoiditis and started on intravenous ceftriaxone and metronidazole. He still has a fever, the post-auricular swelling is more fluctuant, and he now complains of a persistent headache. He is alert and has no neck stiffness or focal neurological signs. Which investigation is most appropriate now?
UN5733.correct_answer: Contrast-enhanced CT of the petrous bones and brain

UN5737.stem: A traveller returning from sub-Saharan Africa has a fever, rigors, headache and myalgia. A blood film shows Plasmodium falciparum parasites. What is the most important immediate consideration?
UN5737.correct_answer: Assess for severe/complicated malaria and treat urgently (can be rapidly fatal)

UN5737.stem: A traveller returning from sub-Saharan Africa has fever, and a blood film confirms Plasmodium falciparum with a parasitaemia of 6%, plus impaired consciousness and acidosis. How should this be classified and managed?
UN5737.correct_answer: Severe/complicated malaria — admit and give IV artesunate

UN5737.stem: A 39-year-old man returns from three weeks in rural sub-Saharan Africa and develops fever, headache and a diffuse maculopapular rash. He admits he did not take any malaria chemoprophylaxis. Which investigation is particularly important to perform urgently?

A 52-year-old man attends the emergency department ten days after returning from visiting relatives in Nigeria. He did not take antimalarial tablets. He has had three days of fever with drenching sweats, aching muscles and headache. He looks mildly jaundiced, and his blood tests show a low platelet count. Which diagnosis is the priority to exclude today?
A 40-year-old man presents with fevers, rigors and headache ten days after returning from a work trip to Nigeria. Which investigation should be performed as a priority?
UN5737.correct_answer: Thick and thin blood films for malaria parasites

UN5737.stem: A 27-year-old woman attends the emergency department 10 days after returning from visiting family in Nigeria. She has had fevers, headache and muscle aches for three days. She is alert, eating and drinking normally and has no vomiting. A pregnancy test is negative. Blood films show Plasmodium falciparum at low parasitaemia, and her renal function, glucose and haemoglobin are normal. What is the most appropriate treatment?

A 58-year-old woman develops sudden severe breathlessness, pleuritic chest pain, a rapid heart rate and a low blood pressure shortly after a long-haul flight. Which complication of pulmonary embolism is particularly concerning in this presentation?

A walker in a tick-endemic area develops a slowly expanding, red, ring-shaped rash with central clearing (erythema migrans) at the site of a tick bite, with mild flu-like symptoms. What is the most appropriate management?
UN5737.correct_answer: Treat clinically with oral doxycycline (no need to await serology)

UN5740.stem: A 68-year-old man presents with two weeks of progressive painless jaundice, dark urine, pale stools and weight loss. Examination reveals a palpable, non-tender gallbladder. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN5740.presentation: Painless obstructive jaundice with suspected pancreatic cancer — imaging
UN5740.stem: A 72-year-old man presents with 2 weeks of painless jaundice, dark urine, and pale stools. He has lost 4 kg unintentionally. No abdominal pain. Examination: palpable non-tender gallbladder. What is the most appropriate imaging investigation?
A heavy drinker develops jaundice, fever and a tender, enlarged liver. What should be considered?

A traveller returns from a region with poor sanitation and develops malaise, nausea, jaundice and right-upper-quadrant discomfort. Hepatitis A is confirmed. What is the most appropriate description and management?

A 50-year-old man with a remote history of injecting drug use is found to have mildly deranged liver enzymes on routine testing. He is asymptomatic. A hepatitis C antibody test is positive. What is the most appropriate next step to determine active infection?

A 45-year-old woman presents with fatigue and jaundice. Her ALT is 350, she has a positive antinuclear antibody and anti-smooth-muscle antibody, and a raised IgG. Viral hepatitis serology is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?

Twelve days after a streptococcal throat infection, an 8-year-old boy develops tea-coloured urine, puffy eyelids, reduced urine volume and a raised blood pressure. Which renal syndrome fits this presentation best?

A 49-year-old man who has been immobile for a prolonged period develops severe muscle aching and notices his urine has turned dark. His creatine kinase is markedly raised. What substance in the urine explains the colour change?

UN5747.presentation: Dirty Wound with Uncertain Tetanus History
UN5747.stem: A man attends after standing on a rusty nail. He completed his childhood vaccination schedule but cannot recall whether he has had any tetanus boosters as an adult. What is the key principle guiding tetanus prophylaxis decisions?
UN5747.correct_answer: Both the nature of the wound and the patient's vaccination history determine the appropriate management

UN5747.stem: A patient attends with a deep, dirty puncture wound from a garden fork. Their tetanus immunisation history is uncertain/incomplete. What is the most appropriate management regarding tetanus?
UN5747.correct_answer: Tetanus-containing vaccine and tetanus immunoglobulin, with wound care

UN5747.stem: A 67-year-old woman presents to an urgent treatment centre after puncturing her palm on a rusty garden fork while spreading manure. The wound is deep and contaminated with soil. She grew up abroad and does not know which vaccinations she has had. Which infection should particularly guide decisions about vaccination and immunoglobulin?

A 50-year-old gardener attends a minor injuries unit after a rusty garden fork went through the sole of his boot into his foot. The puncture is deep and soil was found in it. It has now been irrigated and cleaned. Apart from wound care, what else should be assessed?
UN5747.correct_answer: Tetanus vaccination history and need for prophylaxis

UN5747.stem: A patient attends a few hours after a cat bite to the hand, which is deep with puncture wounds. The wound is not obviously infected yet. Besides wound cleaning, what is the most appropriate management?

On day 6 after an abdominal laparotomy, a patient notices pink serous fluid soaking through the dressing, and on inspection the wound edges have partially separated. What is the most likely complication?

UN5747.presentation: Gas gangrene after a contaminated wound
UN5747.stem:
A 46-year-old gardener drove a garden fork deep into his right thigh while turning a manure heap. The puncture wound was cleaned and closed with sutures at an urgent treatment centre. Thirty-six hours later he is brought to the emergency department with severe thigh pain that seems far worse than the wound looks. The thigh is tense and swollen, the skin is bronze and purple with dark fluid-filled blisters, and thin, foul-smelling fluid is leaking between the sutures. Crackling can be felt under the skin. His temperature is 39.1°C, heart rate 132 bpm and blood pressure 88/50 mmHg. An X-ray shows gas tracking through the muscles.

What is the most appropriate management?
UN5747.correct_answer: IV antibiotics and emergency surgical debridement

UN5747.stem: A 27-year-old backpacker is bitten on the hand by a stray dog in a region where rabies is endemic. The wound is contaminated with the animal's saliva. Before any medical assessment can take place, what is the single most important first-aid step?
UN5747.correct_answer: Irrigate and scrub the wound thoroughly with soap and water

UN5905.stem: Several days after completing a course of a broad-spectrum antibiotic, a patient develops profuse watery diarrhoea and crampy abdominal pain. Which diagnosis must be considered?

A 45-year-old woman with bipolar disorder, stable on lithium for several years, attends the emergency department after four days of vomiting and watery diarrhoea. She now has a coarse tremor, slurred speech and an unsteady gait. Which mechanism best explains her current presentation?
UN5905.correct_answer: Fluid and sodium loss have reduced renal lithium clearance, raising the level

UN5905.stem: A patient with several days of profuse watery diarrhoea is found to have a metabolic acidosis on blood gas analysis. Loss of which gastrointestinal secretion is primarily responsible for this acid-base disturbance?

A 15-month-old boy has had vomiting and watery diarrhoea for 2 days. In the GP surgery he is irritable and difficult to settle, his eyes look sunken and his mother says he refuses his cup and has had only two wet nappies today. His hands and feet are warm, his pulses are normal and his capillary refill is brisk. He is not drowsy.

What is the most appropriate management?
UN5905.correct_answer: Same-day hospital care, with tube-fed ORS if needed

UN5905.stem: A 25-year-old backpacker develops sudden, frequent watery stools two days after arriving in India. There is no blood in the stool and only mild cramping. What is the most likely diagnosis?

Twenty pupils and two teachers fall ill with vomiting and watery diarrhoea during a school camping trip. The toilet block had no soap, and the same tap was used for drinking and washing up. The environmental health officer asks the visiting doctor how the infection most likely spread.

Which route is most likely?

A 46-year-old woman sees her GP to request another prescription for diazepam. It was first prescribed six months ago for a short period after her husband died, and she has continued it with repeat prescriptions. She now finds the same dose helps less, and when she missed a day she felt shaky, sweaty and unable to sleep. Which risk of this treatment is most important to discuss with her?
UN5905.correct_answer: Tolerance and physical dependence with withdrawal symptoms

UN5905.presentation: Infective gastroenteritis — return to work for a food handler
UN5905.stem: A 27-year-old man who works as a chef in a restaurant kitchen sees his GP after 36 hours of vomiting and watery, non-bloody diarrhoea. Two members of his household had a similar illness earlier in the week. He is now improving, is drinking well and his observations are normal. The GP judges that he has viral gastroenteritis and that a stool sample is not needed. He asks when he can go back to preparing food at work. What is the most appropriate advice?
UN5905.correct_answer: Return 48 hours after symptoms have stopped

UN5906.stem: A patient who underwent gastric surgery develops, shortly after eating (especially sugary meals), sweating, palpitations, light-headedness, abdominal cramps and diarrhoea. What is the most likely diagnosis and the most appropriate first-line management?

A 78-year-old woman in a nursing home develops profuse watery diarrhoea and abdominal cramps 5 days after completing co-amoxiclav for a chest infection. She is afebrile. What is the most likely causative organism?

A 22-year-old man develops cramping abdominal pain and bloody diarrhoea three days after eating an undercooked beef burger at a barbecue. Which organism is particularly associated with this presentation?

A 52-year-old man sees his GP with two days of fever, griping lower abdominal pain and frequent loose stools. Three days ago he ate a homemade dessert made with raw eggs at a family party, and his sister who ate the same dessert is also unwell.

Which bacterium is the most likely cause?
A 19-year-old backpacker develops diarrhoea after eating from a street stall abroad, and several travel companions who shared the meal are affected too. What is the most likely mechanism?
A patient develops overgrowth (hyperplasia) of the gums. Which of the following drugs is a recognised cause?

A 65-year-old man develops fever, cough and diarrhoea several days after returning from a hotel stay. The hotel reports that a handful of other guests have become unwell with similar symptoms around the same time. Which organism is the most likely cause?
A 31-year-old woman develops diarrhoea after returning from travel abroad. She looks clinically well and there is no blood in her stool. What is the most appropriate initial advice?

UN5908.stem: A 31-year-old woman develops diarrhoea after returning from travel abroad. She looks clinically well and there is no blood in her stool. What is the most appropriate initial advice?

A 34-year-old woman sees her GP three weeks after returning from a trekking holiday in Nepal, where she filled her water bottle from mountain streams. For two weeks she has had loose, pale, greasy and foul-smelling stools that are difficult to flush, with abdominal bloating and sulphurous belching. She has lost 3 kg. There is no blood in the stool and no fever. Which organism is the most likely cause?

UN5908.presentation: Risk Factor for a Severe Diarrhoeal Illness
UN5908.stem: A patient develops profuse, foul-smelling diarrhoea two weeks after a course of co-amoxiclav for a chest infection, and stool testing confirms *Clostridioides difficile* infection. What is the most important risk factor for this infection?

UN5908.presentation: Chronic diarrhoea + iron deficiency — coeliac testing
UN5908.stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with chronic diarrhoea, bloating, and fatigue. Blood tests: microcytic anaemia (Hb 102 g/L, MCV 72 fL) with low ferritin. No weight loss. What is the most appropriate next investigation?
A 19-year-old backpacker develops diarrhoea after eating from a street stall abroad, and several travel companions who shared the meal are affected too. What is the most likely mechanism?

A 22-year-old man develops cramping abdominal pain and bloody diarrhoea three days after eating an undercooked beef burger at a barbecue. Which organism is particularly associated with this presentation?

A 78-year-old woman admitted from a care home with pneumonia has been treated with co-amoxiclav for five days. She now has frequent foul-smelling loose stools, crampy lower abdominal pain and a rising white cell count. She has not eaten any unusual food and no other patients in the bay are unwell. Which organism is the most likely cause?

UN5908.presentation: Unilateral Foul Nasal Discharge in a Child
UN5908.stem: A 3-year-old is brought in because of a persistent, foul-smelling discharge coming from only one nostril. What should be considered first?

UN6145.stem: A 27-year-old woman complains of an itchy vulva and a bubbly, yellow-green discharge, and testing her vaginal secretions shows an unusually high pH. Which diagnosis best fits?

A woman has a thin, grey-white vaginal discharge with a fishy odour but no itch or soreness. The vaginal pH is raised (>4.5) and 'clue cells' are seen on microscopy. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN6145.presentation: Vulvovaginal candidiasis in pregnancy — treatment choice
UN6145.stem: A 27-year-old woman who is 24 weeks pregnant presents to her GP with vulval itching and a thick white vaginal discharge. Examination shows vulval erythema and typical curd-like discharge, and vulvovaginal candidiasis is diagnosed. She has no other symptoms. Which treatment is most appropriate?

A patient wakes to find both eyes crusted shut with a thick, yellow-green discharge, and the eyes have been red and sticky through the day. There is no pain or visual loss. What is the most likely diagnosis?
Almost two weeks in, a 38-year-old man still has pain confined to one side of his face, a blocked nostril, and thick yellow-green discharge running from his nose. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A woman presents with pain on passing urine, frequent voiding and suprapubic discomfort, with no vaginal discharge and no fever. What is the likely diagnosis?

A 44-year-old woman tells her GP about two months of bleeding after intercourse and an offensive, bloodstained vaginal discharge. She has not attended her last two cervical screening invitations. On speculum examination there is an irregular, ulcerated area on the cervix that bleeds readily on contact. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN6145.correct_answer: Make an urgent suspected cancer referral to gynaecology

UN6145.stem: A 24-year-old man attends a sexual health clinic. Three days after unprotected sex with a new partner he developed stinging on passing urine, and since yesterday a thick, yellow-green discharge has been staining his underwear. He has no genital ulcers, rash or fever. Which organism is most likely responsible?

UN6161.presentation: CSF Interpretation — Bacterial versus Viral Meningitis
UN6161.stem: A patient with suspected meningitis has a lumbar puncture. The CSF shows a high neutrophil count, high protein and LOW glucose (relative to plasma). What does this pattern indicate?
A lumbar puncture in a patient with suspected meningitis shows: markedly raised neutrophils, high protein, and low CSF glucose (low CSF:plasma glucose ratio). What does this pattern most indicate?

UN6161.presentation: CSF Interpretation — Bacterial versus Viral Meningitis
UN6161.stem: A lumbar puncture is performed for suspected meningitis. The cerebrospinal fluid shows: turbid appearance, a high white cell count with PREDOMINANTLY NEUTROPHILS, a HIGH protein and a LOW glucose (low CSF:serum glucose ratio). Which type of meningitis does this most suggest?

UN6161.presentation: Bacterial meningitis — CSF and Gram stain
UN6161.stem:
A 14-month-old boy is brought to the emergency department. His GP treated him for a painful left ear four days ago, but over the last day he has become feverish, irritable and reluctant to feed, and he cries when his legs are moved. His neck is stiff and there is no rash. After blood cultures and a first dose of intravenous ceftriaxone, a lumbar puncture is performed. The fluid is cloudy, with a very high white cell count made up mainly of neutrophils, a raised protein, and a glucose well below half of the simultaneous blood value. Gram staining shows Gram-positive cocci in pairs.

Which interpretation of these findings is most accurate?

A 2-year-old child has bacterial meningitis. CSF microscopy shows: WBC 600/µL (90% neutrophils), protein 2.0 g/L, glucose 1.2 mmol/L (simultaneous serum glucose 5.0 mmol/L). Gram stain shows Gram-positive cocci in pairs. What is the most likely causative organism?

A 26-year-old man is reviewed on the acute medical unit with two days of headache, dislike of bright light and pain on bending his neck forward. He is orientated, his blood pressure and heart rate are normal, and there are no focal signs. A lumbar puncture is performed. The CSF is clear, with a raised white cell count made up mainly of lymphocytes, a normal glucose ratio and a mildly raised protein.

Which diagnosis best fits these findings?

UN6161.presentation: Bacterial meningitis in a young infant
UN6161.stem:
A 7-week-old girl is brought to the emergency department because she has been feeding poorly since yesterday and has a high-pitched cry that her mother has not heard before. Her temperature is 38.6 degrees C, her skin is mottled and her capillary refill is prolonged. The anterior fontanelle is tense. She becomes more distressed when picked up. Blood cultures and a blood glucose have just been taken.

What is the most appropriate next step?
UN6161.correct_answer: Intravenous ceftriaxone plus amoxicillin now, with lumbar puncture once safe

UN6161.presentation: Blood cultures in suspected bacterial meningitis
UN6161.stem:
A 34-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department with a high fever, intense headache and neck stiffness that came on over the last 12 hours. Bacterial meningitis is suspected. She is conscious, her airway is safe and she has no rash.

Which investigation should be taken without delay as part of her first assessment?

UN6210.stem: What is the usual mode of transmission for hepatitis A?
Through which route can hepatitis B be transmitted?
UN6210.correct_answer: Exposure to infected blood or body fluids

UN6210.stem: A patient with acute hepatitis has the following serology: HBsAg POSITIVE, anti-HBc IgM POSITIVE, anti-HBs NEGATIVE. How is this best interpreted?

A traveller returns from a region with poor sanitation and develops malaise, nausea, jaundice and right-upper-quadrant discomfort. Hepatitis A is confirmed. What is the most appropriate description and management?
A heavy drinker develops jaundice, fever and a tender, enlarged liver. What should be considered?
Which of the following is a recognised and important route by which hepatitis B virus spreads between people?
UN6210.correct_answer: Exposure to infected blood or sexual contact

UN6210.stem:
A 34-year-old man attends a drug and alcohol service for a health check. He has injected heroin intermittently for several years and also has tattoos done professionally, plays football in a team, uses a public gym and lives with a partner who shares meals with him.

Which activity puts him at the greatest risk of acquiring hepatitis C?
UN6210.correct_answer: Sharing needles or other injecting equipment

UN6210.presentation: Hepatitis B Exposure in an Immune Worker
UN6210.stem: A healthcare worker has a needlestick exposure to blood from a patient with chronic hepatitis B. The worker previously completed the hepatitis B vaccination course and has documented immunity on blood testing. How should this exposure be interpreted?
UN6210.correct_answer: The risk of transmission is substantially reduced by her documented immunity

UN6298.stem: A 55-year-old has several weeks of headaches that are worse in the early morning and on lying down, coughing or straining, with associated vomiting. Fundoscopy reveals papilloedema, and there is a new subtle focal neurological deficit. What is the most appropriate next investigation?

UN6298.presentation: Papilloedema with suspected IIH — image before lumbar puncture
UN6298.stem:
A 30-year-old woman is referred to the acute medical unit by her optometrist, who saw swelling of both optic discs at a routine eye test. For a month she has had a daily headache that is worse when she lies down and when she coughs. She has gained weight over the past year and is otherwise well, with no fever, neck stiffness or focal neurological signs. The medical registrar suspects idiopathic intracranial hypertension (raised brain pressure with no identifiable cause) and suggests a lumbar puncture this afternoon to measure the opening pressure. No brain imaging has been done.

What should be the next investigation?
A lumbar puncture in a patient with suspected meningitis shows: markedly raised neutrophils, high protein, and low CSF glucose (low CSF:plasma glucose ratio). What does this pattern most indicate?

UN6298.presentation: CSF Interpretation — Bacterial versus Viral Meningitis
UN6298.stem: A patient with suspected meningitis has a lumbar puncture. The CSF shows a high neutrophil count, high protein and LOW glucose (relative to plasma). What does this pattern indicate?

An overweight young woman has headaches, transient visual obscurations and pulsatile tinnitus. Fundoscopy shows papilloedema, but neurological examination is otherwise normal and brain imaging shows no mass or hydrocephalus. Lumbar puncture shows a raised opening pressure with normal constituents. What is the diagnosis?

A 27-year-old woman in the emergency department has fever, neck stiffness and photophobia. She is alert, orientated and asking sensible questions. The registrar plans an urgent diagnostic lumbar puncture, and a junior doctor is asked to prepare her.

What must happen before the needle is inserted?
UN6298.correct_answer: Explain its purpose, what it involves, its risks and alternatives, then get her consent

UN6298.stem: A 26-year-old obese woman presents with a 6-week history of daily headache worse on lying down and on coughing, with transient visual obscurations. Fundoscopy shows bilateral papilloedema. CT head is normal. What is the most appropriate next investigation?
UN6298.correct_answer: Lumbar puncture with measurement of opening pressure

UN6298.presentation: CSF Interpretation — Bacterial versus Viral Meningitis
UN6298.stem: A lumbar puncture is performed for suspected meningitis. The cerebrospinal fluid shows: turbid appearance, a high white cell count with PREDOMINANTLY NEUTROPHILS, a HIGH protein and a LOW glucose (low CSF:serum glucose ratio). Which type of meningitis does this most suggest?

UN6300.stem: Having just been told she has shingles affecting the left flank, a 59-year-old woman wants to know if her young grandchild, who visits often, could catch shingles from her. How should this be explained to her?
UN6300.correct_answer: She can pass varicella-zoster virus to non-immune people through contact with blister fluid

UN6300.presentation: Shingles — when to treat and refer
UN6300.stem: A 70-year-old presents within 48 hours of a painful vesicular rash in a single dermatome, with vesicles on the tip and side of the nose. What is the most appropriate management?
UN6300.correct_answer: Oral antiviral and urgent eye review

UN6300.stem: Shortly after reporting burning discomfort along one flank, a 70-year-old woman is found to have grouped blisters following a strip of skin on the right side of her trunk; crucially, none of the lesions cross over to the left side. Which diagnosis fits best?

A patient has an acute facial (lower motor neurone) weakness on one side, together with a painful vesicular rash in and around the ear and ear canal on the same side, with some altered taste and hearing. What is the most likely diagnosis?
UN6300.correct_answer: Ramsay Hunt syndrome (geniculate ganglion herpes zoster)

UN6300.stem: A 3-year-old has a few days of mild fever, painful mouth ulcers, and a vesicular rash on the palms of the hands and soles of the feet. He is otherwise well and eating a little less. What is the most appropriate management?
UN6300.correct_answer: Supportive care (fluids, analgesia) — it is self-limiting

UN6300.stem: A baby is born to a mother who developed a chickenpox rash 3 days before delivery. The newborn is 24 hours old and has vesicular lesions on the trunk and scalp. What is the most appropriate management?
Long-term infection that slowly progresses towards fibrosis and cirrhosis is a recognised feature of which hepatitis virus?

UN6300.presentation: Herpes zoster ophthalmicus in an immunocompromised patient
UN6300.stem: A 67-year-old man is receiving chemotherapy for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, with his last cycle 9 days ago. He presents with a two-day history of a painful vesicular rash over the right side of his forehead, upper eyelid and the tip of his nose, preceded by burning pain in the same area. His right eye feels gritty and slightly blurred. Temperature is 37.4°C and he is otherwise stable. Neutrophil count is 0.6 x 10^9/L. Right visual acuity is 6/9 and the conjunctiva is injected. What is the most appropriate management?
UN6300.correct_answer: Admit for IV aciclovir and same-day eye review

UN6364.stem: Several days after completing a course of a broad-spectrum antibiotic, a patient develops profuse watery diarrhoea and crampy abdominal pain. Which diagnosis must be considered?

A 78-year-old woman in a nursing home develops profuse watery diarrhoea and abdominal cramps 5 days after completing co-amoxiclav for a chest infection. She is afebrile. What is the most likely causative organism?

An inpatient on recent broad-spectrum antibiotics develops profuse watery diarrhoea, abdominal pain and a raised white cell count. Stool tests positive for Clostridioides difficile toxin. What is the most appropriate management?
UN6364.correct_answer: Stop the offending antibiotic, start oral vancomycin and isolate

UN6364.presentation: C. difficile relapse within 12 weeks — antibiotic choice
UN6364.stem: A 76-year-old woman had a first episode of Clostridioides difficile infection treated with a course of oral vancomycin, and her diarrhoea settled. Three weeks after her symptoms resolved, she develops watery diarrhoea again, and a stool sample is positive for C. difficile toxin. She is not severely unwell. Which treatment is most appropriate?

A 78-year-old woman develops profuse watery diarrhoea 6 days into a course of co-amoxiclav for a chest infection. Stool tests are positive for Clostridioides difficile toxin. She is systemically well. What is the most appropriate first-line treatment?
A 25-year-old backpacker develops sudden, frequent watery stools two days after arriving in India. There is no blood in the stool and only mild cramping. What is the most likely diagnosis?

An 81-year-old woman on a care of the elderly ward has been receiving co-amoxiclav and clarithromycin for a chest infection, which is now improving clinically. On day six she develops frequent watery stools, and a stool test is positive for Clostridioides difficile toxin. Alongside starting specific treatment, which further step matters most?
UN6364.correct_answer: Review and stop any antibiotics that are no longer essential

UN6364.stem: A 75-year-old woman who received a 7-day course of co-amoxiclav for a urinary tract infection develops profuse watery diarrhoea (6 episodes per day), abdominal pain, and fever (38.5°C) 5 days after completing the antibiotics. Stool PCR is positive for Clostridioides difficile toxin. What is the first-line treatment for this severity of infection?

UN6367.correct_answer: Stop the offending antibiotic, start oral vancomycin and isolate

UN6367.stem: A 25-year-old backpacker develops sudden, frequent watery stools two days after arriving in India. There is no blood in the stool and only mild cramping. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 75-year-old woman who received a 7-day course of co-amoxiclav for a urinary tract infection develops profuse watery diarrhoea (6 episodes per day), abdominal pain, and fever (38.5°C) 5 days after completing the antibiotics. Stool PCR is positive for Clostridioides difficile toxin. What is the first-line treatment for this severity of infection?

A 22-year-old man develops cramping abdominal pain and bloody diarrhoea three days after eating an undercooked beef burger at a barbecue. Which organism is particularly associated with this presentation?

UN6377.stem:
A 34-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department with a high fever, intense headache and neck stiffness that came on over the last 12 hours. Bacterial meningitis is suspected. She is conscious, her airway is safe and she has no rash.

Which investigation should be taken without delay as part of her first assessment?

A 19-year-old woman has fever, severe headache, neck stiffness and photophobia, and is becoming drowsy. She has a non-blanching purpuric rash. Suspected meningococcal meningitis with septicaemia. What is the most appropriate immediate management?

UN6377.presentation: CSF Interpretation — Bacterial versus Viral Meningitis
UN6377.stem: A patient with suspected meningitis has a lumbar puncture. The CSF shows a high neutrophil count, high protein and LOW glucose (relative to plasma). What does this pattern indicate?

A young adult has fever, headache, confusion and a witnessed seizure, with altered behaviour but no purpuric rash. What is the most appropriate immediate treatment while investigations proceed?
A patient established on warfarin is prescribed a new medicine by a different clinician who is unaware of the warfarin treatment. Why is this situation particularly important to address?
UN6377.correct_answer: New medicines can alter the anticoagulant effect and increase the risk of bleeding or clotting

UN6377.stem: A 51-year-old woman develops fever, a productive cough and increasing breathlessness over two days. A chest X-ray demonstrates a new area of focal consolidation. What is the most appropriate treatment?
UN6377.correct_answer: Antibiotics guided by CURB-65 and local guidance

UN6528.stem: A patient attends with a deep, dirty puncture wound from a garden fork. Their tetanus immunisation history is uncertain/incomplete. What is the most appropriate management regarding tetanus?
UN6528.correct_answer: Tetanus-containing vaccine and tetanus immunoglobulin, with wound care
