UN8303.presentation: Blood cultures in suspected bacterial meningitis
UN8303.stem:
A 34-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department with a high fever, intense headache and neck stiffness that came on over the last 12 hours. Bacterial meningitis is suspected. She is conscious, her airway is safe and she has no rash.

Which investigation should be taken without delay as part of her first assessment?

A 19-year-old woman has fever, severe headache, neck stiffness and photophobia, and is becoming drowsy. She has a non-blanching purpuric rash. Suspected meningococcal meningitis with septicaemia. What is the most appropriate immediate management?

UN8303.presentation: Antibiotic Choice in a Patient on Warfarin
UN8303.stem: A patient taking warfarin for a mechanical heart valve requires antibiotic treatment for a chest infection. Which of the following antibiotics carries the greatest risk of significantly raising the INR?

UN8303.presentation: CSF Interpretation — Bacterial versus Viral Meningitis
UN8303.stem: A patient with suspected meningitis has a lumbar puncture. The CSF shows a high neutrophil count, high protein and LOW glucose (relative to plasma). What does this pattern indicate?
A lumbar puncture in a patient with suspected meningitis shows: markedly raised neutrophils, high protein, and low CSF glucose (low CSF:plasma glucose ratio). What does this pattern most indicate?

UN8303.presentation: CSF Interpretation — Bacterial versus Viral Meningitis
UN8303.stem: A lumbar puncture is performed for suspected meningitis. The cerebrospinal fluid shows: turbid appearance, a high white cell count with PREDOMINANTLY NEUTROPHILS, a HIGH protein and a LOW glucose (low CSF:serum glucose ratio). Which type of meningitis does this most suggest?

UN8303.presentation: Lyme disease facial palsy — antibiotic choice
UN8303.stem: A 38-year-old man has a left lower motor neurone facial palsy that developed 5 weeks after a tick bite in the New Forest. Lyme ELISA and immunoblot are both positive. He has no headache, neck stiffness, confusion, limb weakness or palpitations, and his ECG is normal. He is not allergic to any medicines. Which antibiotic treatment is most appropriate?

UN8303.presentation: Antibiotic request for a viral illness
UN8303.stem: A 30-year-old man sees a GP after three days of sore throat, cough, runny nose and a mild temperature. He is otherwise well, with no features of a bacterial infection on examination. He asks for antibiotics because they have always worked for him in the past. Which principle should most guide the GP's prescribing decision?

UN8306.stem: A 20-year-old woman shares a flat with a student who was diagnosed with mumps 2 days ago. She is well and has no symptoms. Her GP records show she has never received any MMR vaccine, and she is not pregnant. She asks whether anything can be given to protect her. Which is most appropriate to offer her?
A teenage boy develops a painful, swollen testis several days after his parotid glands swelled up. What complication is this?

A 19-year-old university student is seen in general practice with 2 days of fever and painful swelling of both parotid glands. He has not had the MMR vaccine. He is well enough to manage at home, and the GP has notified the health protection team and arranged an oral fluid test. Which new symptom should he be told to seek urgent medical review for?

A 14-year-old boy who has not received any MMR vaccines is brought to the emergency department. A week ago he developed painful swelling of both parotid glands, and over the last day he has had a worsening headache, has vomited several times and finds bright light uncomfortable. He is alert, his neck is stiff on flexion and there is no rash.

Which complication is most likely?

A 19-year-old university student has fever and painful swelling in front of both ears that started 2 days ago. Several students in his hall of residence have similar symptoms. He is unsure whether he had the MMR vaccine. The local health protection team asks the GP to arrange confirmation of the diagnosis.

Which sample is most appropriate?

A 29-year-old woman who is 20 weeks pregnant was exposed to a child with a rash illness. Her blood tests show no evidence of current or past rubella infection, and she has no record of ever receiving MMR vaccine. She is well and asks how she can be protected against rubella in future. Which is the most appropriate plan for her vaccination?
A 58-year-old woman develops a painful, swollen calf in one leg several days after major surgery. Which diagnosis must be considered?

UN8306.presentation: Painful Bilateral Swelling Below the Ears
UN8306.stem: A child presents with fever and tender swelling below both ears, with the parotid glands clearly enlarged and painful to touch. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN8310.stem: A 39-year-old man returns from three weeks in rural sub-Saharan Africa and develops fever, headache and a diffuse maculopapular rash. He admits he did not take any malaria chemoprophylaxis. Which investigation is particularly important to perform urgently?
A traveller returning from sub-Saharan Africa has a fever, rigors, headache and myalgia. A blood film shows Plasmodium falciparum parasites. What is the most important immediate consideration?
UN8310.correct_answer: Assess for severe/complicated malaria and treat urgently (can be rapidly fatal)

UN8310.stem:
A GP reviews a 39-year-old man with a high temperature, sweats and headache for two days. He works for an engineering firm and has made several work trips overseas this year, some of them to tropical countries. The GP is considering malaria.

Which part of the history is most important to establish?
UN8310.correct_answer: Exactly where and when he travelled

UN8310.stem: A 40-year-old man presents with fevers, rigors and headache ten days after returning from a work trip to Nigeria. Which investigation should be performed as a priority?
UN8310.correct_answer: Thick and thin blood films for malaria parasites

UN8310.stem: A 26-year-old returns from Southeast Asia with four days of fever that has now settled, but he develops worsening abdominal pain and repeated vomiting. Blood films for malaria are negative. What should be suspected?
UN8310.correct_answer: Dengue fever with warning signs of severe disease

UN8310.stem: A 52-year-old man attends the emergency department ten days after returning from visiting relatives in Nigeria. He did not take antimalarial tablets. He has had three days of fever with drenching sweats, aching muscles and headache. He looks mildly jaundiced, and his blood tests show a low platelet count. Which diagnosis is the priority to exclude today?

A traveller returning from sub-Saharan Africa has fever, and a blood film confirms Plasmodium falciparum with a parasitaemia of 6%, plus impaired consciousness and acidosis. How should this be classified and managed?
UN8310.correct_answer: Severe/complicated malaria — admit and give IV artesunate

UN8310.presentation: Deteriorating Patient Days After Bowel Surgery
UN8310.stem: On day six after an anterior resection for colorectal cancer, a patient develops a temperature of 38.6°C, a heart rate of 118 beats per minute, and worsening diffuse abdominal pain. Which complication should be excluded urgently?

UN8311.stem: A traveller returns from a region with poor sanitation and develops malaise, nausea, jaundice and right-upper-quadrant discomfort. Hepatitis A is confirmed. What is the most appropriate description and management?

A 68-year-old man presents with two weeks of progressive painless jaundice, dark urine, pale stools and weight loss. Examination reveals a palpable, non-tender gallbladder. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A heavy drinker develops jaundice, fever and a tender, enlarged liver. What should be considered?

UN8311.presentation: Painless obstructive jaundice with suspected pancreatic cancer — imaging
UN8311.stem: A 72-year-old man presents with 2 weeks of painless jaundice, dark urine, and pale stools. He has lost 4 kg unintentionally. No abdominal pain. Examination: palpable non-tender gallbladder. What is the most appropriate imaging investigation?

A 40-year-old woman presents with rapidly progressive anaemia (Hb 68 g/L), jaundice, and dark urine. Blood film shows spherocytes. Direct antiglobulin test (Coombs test) is positive for IgG. Reticulocyte count is elevated. What is the most appropriate first-line treatment?

A 45-year-old woman presents with fatigue and jaundice. Her ALT is 350, she has a positive antinuclear antibody and anti-smooth-muscle antibody, and a raised IgG. Viral hepatitis serology is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?

Twelve days after a streptococcal throat infection, an 8-year-old boy develops tea-coloured urine, puffy eyelids, reduced urine volume and a raised blood pressure. Which renal syndrome fits this presentation best?

A 49-year-old man who has been immobile for a prolonged period develops severe muscle aching and notices his urine has turned dark. His creatine kinase is markedly raised. What substance in the urine explains the colour change?

UN8314.stem: A healthcare worker sustains a needlestick injury from a needle used on a patient with known untreated HIV. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
UN8314.correct_answer: Wash, risk-assess and start HIV PEP as soon as possible

UN8314.stem:
A theatre nurse attends the occupational health department two days after blood from an HIV-positive patient splashed into her eye during an emergency laparotomy. She rinsed her eye at the time but did not report the incident until today. The source patient had recently stopped antiretroviral therapy and his viral load is detectable.

What should be offered now?
UN8314.correct_answer: A 28-day course of HIV post-exposure prophylaxis started as soon as possible today

UN8314.presentation: Hepatitis B Exposure in an Immune Worker
UN8314.stem: A healthcare worker has a needlestick exposure to blood from a patient with chronic hepatitis B. The worker previously completed the hepatitis B vaccination course and has documented immunity on blood testing. How should this exposure be interpreted?
UN8314.correct_answer: The risk of transmission is substantially reduced by her documented immunity

UN8314.presentation: Measles exposure in pregnancy — post-exposure prophylaxis
UN8314.stem: A 27-year-old woman who is 20 weeks pregnant was in the same room as a child with confirmed measles 3 days ago. She was never vaccinated and has never had measles. She is well. Her measles IgG antibody test is negative. Which is the most appropriate post-exposure prophylaxis?
A woman at 30 weeks' gestation, with no history of chickenpox, has significant household exposure to a child with chickenpox. Her varicella IgG is negative. What is the most appropriate management?

UN8314.presentation: Deciding Post-Exposure Management After Hepatitis B Exposure
UN8314.stem: A healthcare assistant is splashed with blood from a patient known to carry hepatitis B. What mainly determines whether post-exposure treatment is required?
UN8314.correct_answer: The assistant's hepatitis B immunity and the type of exposure

UN8314.stem: A new healthcare worker has no documented evidence of hepatitis B vaccination and is about to begin a role involving regular exposure to blood and body fluids. What is the appropriate approach?
UN8314.correct_answer: Hepatitis B vaccination should be offered based on the individual's occupational risk

UN8314.stem: A 24-year-old woman attends her GP the day after returning from a trip to rural India. Three days ago a stray cat scratched her forearm hard enough to draw blood. She washed the wound with bottled water, and the cat ran off. She feels well and the scratch is healing without signs of infection. Which is the best management?
UN8314.correct_answer: Urgent risk assessment for rabies post-exposure prophylaxis

UN8458.stem: A 23-year-old woman sees her GP with 5 days of bilateral lower abdominal pain, deep dyspareunia and an abnormal vaginal discharge. She uses condoms inconsistently and her periods are irregular. Her temperature is 37.6°C and she is otherwise well. Bimanual examination shows cervical motion tenderness and bilateral adnexal tenderness. The GP suspects pelvic inflammatory disease. Which investigation should be performed first?

A 22-year-old woman attends a sexual health clinic with a week of bilateral lower abdominal pain, pain deep inside during intercourse and bleeding after sex. She has a new sexual partner and they do not use condoms. Her temperature is 37.9°C. On bimanual examination there is tenderness in both adnexa and pain on moving the cervix. A pregnancy test is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN8458.presentation: Pelvic inflammatory disease with an intrauterine device
UN8458.stem: A 31-year-old woman has had a copper intrauterine device (IUD) for 3 years. She presents to a sexual health clinic with lower abdominal pain, abnormal discharge and cervical motion tenderness. She is afebrile and systemically well, her pregnancy test is negative and she is diagnosed with mild to moderate pelvic inflammatory disease. Swabs are taken and outpatient antibiotics are started. She wishes to keep the IUD as her contraception. What is the most appropriate management of the IUD?
UN8458.correct_answer: Leave it in place and review her response early

UN8458.stem: A 24-year-old woman has lower abdominal pain, deep dyspareunia, abnormal discharge and cervical motion tenderness, with a mild fever. What is the most appropriate management?
UN8458.correct_answer: Start empirical antibiotics for PID without waiting for swab results

UN8458.presentation: Persistent pelvic pain in a man
UN8458.stem:
A 41-year-old man has had five months of aching discomfort in the perineum and above the pubis, with urinary frequency and pain on ejaculation. He has had no fever or loin pain, his urine dipstick and culture are negative, and he is otherwise well.

Which diagnosis should be considered?

A 22-year-old woman presents with bilateral lower abdominal pain, deep dyspareunia, and a mucopurulent vaginal discharge. Bimanual examination reveals cervical motion tenderness and bilateral adnexal tenderness. She is afebrile. What is the most appropriate management?
UN8458.correct_answer: Outpatient antibiotics — IM ceftriaxone plus oral doxycycline and metronidazole

UN8458.stem: For many months, a 24-year-old woman has had pelvic pain that flares specifically around menstruation and also during sex; a urine dipstick has already ruled out infection as the cause. Which underlying condition fits best?
A woman has fever with rigors, loin pain and tenderness, and dysuria with urinary frequency. Urine dipstick is positive for nitrites and leucocytes. What is the most appropriate management?
UN8458.correct_answer: Send a urine culture and start empirical antibiotics per local guidance

UN8505.presentation: Infection control for suspected C. difficile
UN8505.stem: A 76-year-old man in a four-bed bay on an orthopaedic ward has developed three episodes of unexplained loose stool overnight after recent antibiotics. A stool sample has been sent for C. difficile testing. The nurse in charge asks what infection-control measures are needed now. What is the most appropriate advice?
UN8505.correct_answer: Side-room isolation, gloves and apron, and handwashing with soap and water

UN8505.presentation: Infection Control in Suspected Meningococcal Disease
UN8505.stem: A 4-year-old boy is brought to the paediatric emergency department with a high fever, lethargy and a spreading non-blanching purpuric rash on his legs. Which statement is correct?
UN8505.correct_answer: They apply to every patient in every setting, at all times

UN8505.stem: A foundation doctor is asked to insert a peripheral intravenous cannula in a 58-year-old woman on a medical ward who needs intravenous antibiotics. The doctor has just taken blood from the patient in the next bed. Which measure is most important to reduce the risk of a cannula-related bloodstream infection?
UN8505.correct_answer: Perform hand hygiene and use aseptic non-touch technique throughout

Which bacterium is the most likely cause?

UN8618.correct_answer: Oral rehydration and supportive care, generally avoiding routine antibiotics

He had a bout of bloody diarrhoea while travelling, which settled without treatment. He is alert, with a pulse of 92 beats per minute and blood pressure 126/80 mmHg. CT shows a single 5 cm abscess in the right lobe of the liver, and serology for Entamoeba histolytica is positive. Which is the most appropriate treatment?

A 34-year-old man phones his GP surgery on the fourth day of a course of clarithromycin prescribed for a chest infection. His cough is improving, but he has developed loose stools a few times a day with mild cramping. He has no blood in the stool, no fever and no vomiting, and he is eating and drinking normally. He has not travelled recently. What is the most likely cause of his diarrhoea?
A 19-year-old backpacker develops diarrhoea after eating from a street stall abroad, and several travel companions who shared the meal are affected too. What is the most likely mechanism?

A 25-year-old man develops ascending weakness over a week, starting in his legs, with loss of reflexes and mild distal numbness. He had diarrhoea three weeks ago. What is the most important investigation to monitor in the acute phase?

A backpacker returns from a trekking trip having drunk from streams, and develops two weeks of bloating, foul-smelling, greasy, loose stools that float, with flatulence and cramps. There is no blood in the stool and he is afebrile. What is the most likely cause?

UN8626.stem: A backpacker returns from a trekking trip having drunk from streams, and develops two weeks of bloating, foul-smelling, greasy, loose stools that float, with flatulence and cramps. There is no blood in the stool and he is afebrile. What is the most likely cause?

A 34-year-old woman sees her GP three weeks after returning from a trekking holiday in Nepal, where she filled her water bottle from mountain streams. For two weeks she has had loose, pale, greasy and foul-smelling stools that are difficult to flush, with abdominal bloating and sulphurous belching. She has lost 3 kg. There is no blood in the stool and no fever. Which organism is the most likely cause?
A 31-year-old woman develops diarrhoea after returning from travel abroad. She looks clinically well and there is no blood in her stool. What is the most appropriate initial advice?

UN8626.presentation: Expanding Rash After a Tick Bite
UN8626.stem: A 34-year-old man notices a slowly enlarging red ring-shaped rash on his calf about ten days after a camping trip, during which he recalls pulling off an attached tick. What is the most likely diagnosis?

Twenty pupils and two teachers fall ill with vomiting and watery diarrhoea during a school camping trip. The toilet block had no soap, and the same tap was used for drinking and washing up. The environmental health officer asks the visiting doctor how the infection most likely spread.

Which route is most likely?

UN8626.presentation: Unilateral Foul Nasal Discharge in a Child
UN8626.stem: A 3-year-old is brought in because of a persistent, foul-smelling discharge coming from only one nostril. What should be considered first?

UN8626.presentation: Suspected infectious diarrhoea on a ward
UN8626.stem: You are the doctor on a medical ward. A 66-year-old man in a six-bed bay is on day four of intravenous co-amoxiclav for pneumonia and has developed frequent, foul-smelling watery diarrhoea. A stool sample has been sent, but the result will not be back until tomorrow. What is the most appropriate immediate action?
UN8626.correct_answer: Move him to a side room now with contact precautions, gloves, apron and soap-and-water hand washing

UN8896.stem: A 19-year-old student presents with fever, confusion and hypotension. There is a rapidly spreading non-blanching purpuric rash. Neck stiffness is absent. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
UN8896.correct_answer: Immediate IV ceftriaxone (do not delay for investigations)

UN8896.stem: A 3-year-old boy has a fever and a rash of small purple-red spots that do not fade when pressed. He is floppy and very difficult to wake. What is the most important diagnosis to consider?

UN8896.presentation: Fever, Neck Stiffness and Non-Blanching Rash
UN8896.stem: A university student presents with fever, a severe headache, neck stiffness and a rash that does not fade under pressure. She is becoming increasingly drowsy. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old student presents with a 12-hour history of fever, severe headache, neck stiffness and a non-blanching petechial rash. He is drowsy with a blood pressure of 100/60. What is the most appropriate immediate treatment?

UN8896.presentation: Fever with a spreading non-blanching rash
UN8896.stem:
An 18-month-old girl is collected early from nursery because of a fever. Over the next three hours her parents notice tiny purple spots on her legs that do not disappear when pressed, and more are appearing on her trunk. She is miserable, her hands and feet are cold, and she cries when her legs are moved.

Which diagnosis must be assumed?

A 19-year-old student presents to the GP surgery with a 5-hour history of fever, severe headache, photophobia and neck stiffness, and now a non-blanching petechial rash. She is alert with a blood pressure of 112/70. What is the most appropriate immediate action?
UN8896.correct_answer: Immediate IV (or IM) benzylpenicillin/ceftriaxone and urgent transfer

UN8896.presentation: Infection Control in Suspected Meningococcal Disease

UN8896.correct_answer: Droplet precautions in a single room

UN8896.stem: A 19-year-old university student presents to ED with a 6-hour history of fever, headache, vomiting, and myalgia. He is tachycardic (HR 110 bpm), hypotensive (BP 96/58 mmHg), and has a widespread purpuric rash that is non-blanching. He is confused. What is the single most important immediate action?

A 19-year-old backpacker develops diarrhoea after eating from a street stall abroad, and several travel companions who shared the meal are affected too. What is the most likely mechanism?

UN9775.correct_answer: Offer epidemiological treatment for syphilis today

UN9777.presentation: HIV post-diagnosis — when to start treatment
UN9777.stem: A patient is newly diagnosed with HIV and is asymptomatic with a well-preserved CD4 count. What is the most appropriate approach to antiretroviral therapy?
UN9777.correct_answer: Start antiretroviral therapy regardless of CD4 count

UN9777.stem:
A man is newly diagnosed with HIV infection. He is asymptomatic and his CD4 count is 450 cells/mm³.

According to UK (BHIVA) guidelines, what is the most appropriate next step in his management?
UN9777.correct_answer: Start ART immediately, regardless of the CD4 count

UN9777.stem: A man with untreated HIV (CD4 count 90 cells/µL) has progressive pain on swallowing (odynophagia) and difficulty swallowing. Examination shows white plaques on the oral mucosa that scrape off. What is the most likely cause of his swallowing symptoms?

A 29-year-old woman has a reactive fourth-generation HIV test confirmed at the sexual health clinic. Before discussing treatment and the need for prophylaxis against opportunistic infections, the team wants to know how far her immune system has been damaged.

Which blood test gives this information?

A 26-year-old woman has a positive HIV test at a sexual health clinic during routine screening. She feels well and has no symptoms. Her CD4 count is within the normal range and her viral load is moderately raised. She asks whether she can wait a few years before taking any medication. What is the most appropriate advice?
UN9777.correct_answer: Offer antiretroviral therapy now, whatever her CD4 count

UN9777.stem:
A 38-year-old woman who stopped her antiretroviral therapy two years ago is brought in by her sister. For the past three weeks she has had a slowly worsening headache, low-grade fevers and, more recently, episodes of confusion. Her last CD4 count was very low. There is minimal neck stiffness and no focal weakness.

Which opportunistic infection should be considered first?

A 36-year-old woman was diagnosed with HIV last month and has a very low CD4 count; she has not yet started antiretroviral therapy. She now has three weeks of gradually worsening breathlessness on exertion and a dry cough. Her chest sounds almost clear, but her oxygen saturation falls markedly when she walks around the ward. Chest X-ray shows bilateral faint shadowing spreading out from the hila. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN9777.presentation: Cerebral toxoplasmosis in advanced HIV — first-line treatment
UN9777.stem:
A 38-year-old man with newly diagnosed advanced HIV and a very low CD4 count presents with headache, fever and right-sided weakness. MRI of the brain shows multiple ring-enhancing lesions in the basal ganglia, and Toxoplasma IgG is positive. The HIV team diagnose presumed cerebral toxoplasmosis and start empirical treatment.

Which is the preferred first-line treatment?

UN9779.presentation: Infection Control in Suspected Meningococcal Disease
UN9779.stem: A 4-year-old boy is brought to the paediatric emergency department with a high fever, lethargy and a spreading non-blanching purpuric rash on his legs. Intravenous ceftriaxone is given immediately and he is to be admitted. A nurse asks which infection control precautions staff should use while caring for him. What is the most appropriate answer?
UN9779.correct_answer: Droplet precautions in a single room

UN9779.stem: A patient with a persistent cough, weight loss and night sweats is being investigated for possible active pulmonary tuberculosis. Which investigation is especially important for microbiological confirmation?

A newly qualified nurse in a general practice treatment room tells a colleague that she only uses gloves, aprons and careful sharps disposal for patients known to have an infection such as hepatitis or HIV. Her colleague explains how standard infection control precautions should be applied.

Which statement is correct?
UN9779.correct_answer: They apply to every patient in every setting, at all times

UN9779.presentation: Infection control for suspected C. difficile
UN9779.stem: A 76-year-old man in a four-bed bay on an orthopaedic ward has developed three episodes of unexplained loose stool overnight after recent antibiotics. A stool sample has been sent for C. difficile testing. The nurse in charge asks what infection-control measures are needed now. What is the most appropriate advice?
UN9779.correct_answer: Side-room isolation, gloves and apron, and handwashing with soap and water

UN9779.stem: A patient is diagnosed with active pulmonary tuberculosis. What is the most appropriate standard initial drug regimen?
UN9779.correct_answer: Rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol, with pyridoxine

UN9779.stem:
A 45-year-old man who works as a bus driver is diagnosed with sputum smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis after months of cough and weight loss. His wife, who shares his bedroom, is referred to the TB service for contact screening.

By which route is she most likely to have been exposed?
UN9779.correct_answer: Inhaling droplet nuclei released when he coughs

UN9779.stem: A 46-year-old man living in a homeless hostel sees the visiting GP. For two months he has had a productive cough, occasionally with streaks of blood, and he wakes drenched in sweat most nights. His trousers have become loose. Another resident of the hostel was recently started on a long course of treatment for a chest infection. Which diagnosis is most likely?

A 52-year-old man living in a homeless hostel attends a walk-in centre with two months of cough, occasionally bringing up streaks of blood. He wakes drenched in sweat most nights, feels feverish in the evenings and his trousers have become loose. A fellow resident was admitted to hospital with tuberculosis last month. He smokes 15 cigarettes a day. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

UN9780.stem: A 27-year-old woman attends her GP five weeks after returning from backpacking in South Asia. She describes a week of tiredness, nausea, aching and a mild temperature, after which her urine became dark and her partner noticed her eyes were yellow. The liver edge is palpable and tender. Blood tests show a markedly raised ALT with only a modest rise in alkaline phosphatase. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A heavy drinker develops jaundice, fever and a tender, enlarged liver. What should be considered?

A patient develops jaundice and itch two weeks after completing a course of flucloxacillin (or co-amoxiclav) for a skin infection. Liver tests show a CHOLESTATIC picture (markedly raised alkaline phosphatase and bilirubin, with only mildly raised transaminases). Viral serology and an ultrasound of the biliary tree are normal. What is the most likely cause?

A 68-year-old man presents with two weeks of progressive painless jaundice, dark urine, pale stools and weight loss. Examination reveals a palpable, non-tender gallbladder. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A 31-year-old woman develops diarrhoea after returning from travel abroad. She looks clinically well and there is no blood in her stool. What is the most appropriate initial advice?

UN9780.presentation: Painless obstructive jaundice with suspected pancreatic cancer — imaging
UN9780.stem: A 72-year-old man presents with 2 weeks of painless jaundice, dark urine, and pale stools. He has lost 4 kg unintentionally. No abdominal pain. Examination: palpable non-tender gallbladder. What is the most appropriate imaging investigation?

A 36-year-old woman at 32 weeks attends maternity triage with severe epigastric pain going through to her back, vomiting and feeling generally unwell. Her blood pressure is raised and urine dipstick shows proteinuria. Blood tests show a low platelet count, a markedly raised ALT, a raised LDH and fragmented red cells on the blood film. Amylase, glucose and clotting are normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old man with schizophrenia had his haloperidol dose increased four days ago. He is brought in confused and rigid. Temperature is 39.5°C, he is sweating and his pulse is 120. Blood tests show a markedly raised creatine kinase and a leukocytosis. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN9906.stem: A 23-year-old woman attends a sexual health clinic with 3 days of painful genital ulcers and dysuria. Examination shows several shallow, tender ulcers on the labia with tender inguinal lymph nodes. Genital herpes is suspected. Which test is most appropriate to confirm the diagnosis?
UN9906.correct_answer: Swab of an ulcer base for HSV NAAT

UN9906.stem: A young woman has a first episode of multiple painful genital ulcers with tender inguinal lymphadenopathy and dysuria. Swabs confirm herpes simplex virus. What is the most appropriate treatment?
A man has a single painless, indurated genital ulcer (chancre) with non-tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. Treponemal serology is positive. What is the most appropriate treatment?
An 18-year-old woman notices a crop of painful small blisters on her vulva that soon burst into shallow sores, and she has swollen, tender nodes in both groins. What is the most probable diagnosis?

UN9906.presentation: Painless genital ulcer: referral for syphilis testing
UN9906.stem:
A 44-year-old man sees his GP about a sore in the groove just behind the head of his penis, which he noticed about a week ago. It is a single ulcer with a clean base and a firm, rubbery edge, and it does not hurt. He has had several new male partners over the past three months.

Which is the most appropriate next step?
UN9906.correct_answer: Refer urgently to sexual health for syphilis testing

UN9906.stem: A 23-year-old woman is seen in a sexual health clinic with her first episode of genital herpes, confirmed on a swab. She has several painful vulval ulcers and is otherwise well. She is prescribed oral aciclovir, with saline bathing and simple analgesia, and will manage at home. Which new symptom should she be told to seek urgent medical review for?
UN9906.correct_answer: Being unable to pass urine at all

UN9906.stem:
A 27-year-old woman has her third outbreak of genital herpes this year, confirmed by swab when it first occurred. She has been in a faithful relationship for two years and asks whether her partner must be giving it back to her each time.

Which explanation is correct?
UN9906.correct_answer: The virus lies dormant in sensory nerve ganglia and periodically reactivates

UN9906.presentation: Recurrent genital herpes in pregnancy — birth plan
UN9906.stem: A 29-year-old woman is 24 weeks pregnant with her first baby. She has had recurrent genital herpes for 6 years, with about two short outbreaks a year; it was diagnosed long before this pregnancy. She has no lesions or symptoms today, and the pregnancy is otherwise uncomplicated, with no risk factors for preterm birth. She asks how the herpes will affect the birth. What is the most appropriate plan?
UN9906.correct_answer: Plan a vaginal birth with suppressive aciclovir late in pregnancy

UN9907.presentation: Painless genital ulcer: referral for syphilis testing

Which is the most appropriate next step?
UN9907.correct_answer: Refer urgently to sexual health for syphilis testing

UN9907.stem: A man has a single painless, indurated genital ulcer (chancre) with non-tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. Treponemal serology is positive. What is the most appropriate treatment?

A 34-year-old man attends a sexual health clinic because of a sore on the shaft of his penis that appeared ten days ago. He had condomless sex with a new male partner about four weeks ago. The lesion is a single, firm, clean-based ulcer that does not hurt even when pressed. There are rubbery, non-tender enlarged nodes in both groins. He feels well. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old man sees his GP about a sore on his lower lip that appeared roughly three weeks after he began a new relationship and has been present for ten days. It has never been tender. There is a single firm, clean-based ulcer on the lip, and a non-tender, rubbery submandibular lymph node can be felt on the same side. He has no history of cold sores. What is the most likely cause?
A 59-year-old man notices a lump in his neck that has been present and unchanged for six weeks. He feels otherwise well with no fever or recent infection. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN9907.correct_answer: Urgent assessment of the neck lump

UN9907.stem: A 23-year-old woman attends a sexual health clinic with 3 days of painful genital ulcers and dysuria. Examination shows several shallow, tender ulcers on the labia with tender inguinal lymph nodes. Genital herpes is suspected. Which test is most appropriate to confirm the diagnosis?
UN9907.correct_answer: Swab of an ulcer base for HSV NAAT

UN9907.presentation: Asymptomatic sexual contact of early syphilis

He has no symptoms, and examination of the genitals, mouth, skin and lymph nodes is normal. He has no drug allergies. Blood is taken for syphilis serology. What is the most appropriate management?
UN9907.correct_answer: Offer epidemiological treatment for syphilis today

UN9907.stem: A 23-year-old woman is seen in a sexual health clinic with her first episode of genital herpes, confirmed on a swab. She has several painful vulval ulcers and is otherwise well. UN9907.correct_answer: Being unable to pass urine at all

UN9911.stem: A 22-year-old man telephones his GP surgery with three days of stinging when passing urine and a clear discharge from the tip of his penis. He started a new sexual relationship a fortnight ago and did not use condoms. He has no fever or loin pain. How should he be managed?
UN9911.correct_answer: Arrange testing for sexually transmitted infections, ideally via a sexual health clinic

UN9911.stem: A woman presents with pain on passing urine, frequent voiding and suprapubic discomfort, with no vaginal discharge and no fever. What is the likely diagnosis?

A woman has a thin, grey-white vaginal discharge with a fishy odour but no itch or soreness. The vaginal pH is raised (>4.5) and 'clue cells' are seen on microscopy. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 29-year-old man presents with pain on passing urine and discharge from the urethra after a recent episode of unprotected sex. Which investigation is commonly used to test for chlamydia and gonorrhoea?

UN9911.presentation: Persistent conjunctivitis in a sexually active adult — investigation
UN9911.stem:
A 23-year-old woman sees her GP with 4 weeks of a red, sticky right eye. A week of chloramphenicol eye drops has not helped. Vision is normal and there is no pain or photophobia. There are follicles on the lower lid conjunctiva and a tender lymph node in front of the right ear. She started a new sexual relationship 3 months ago and has noticed increased vaginal discharge.

Which investigation is most appropriate?
UN9911.correct_answer: Conjunctival swab for chlamydia nucleic acid testing

UN9911.stem:
A 27-year-old woman has a 1-week history of a thin, grey vaginal discharge with a fishy smell, worse after intercourse. She is not pregnant and has no itch or soreness. Vaginal pH is 5.5 and microscopy shows clue cells. Chlamydia and gonorrhoea tests are negative. She would like treatment.

Which treatment is most appropriate?

A 22-year-old woman sees her GP for the third time in four months with burning on passing urine and frequency. Urine samples sent at her last two visits showed white cells but grew no organisms, and her symptoms did not settle with antibiotics for cystitis. She now also mentions a change in vaginal discharge and some bleeding after sex. She has had a new partner in the last six months and they do not use condoms. What is the most likely diagnosis?

For many months, a 24-year-old woman has had pelvic pain that flares specifically around menstruation and also during sex; a urine dipstick has already ruled out infection as the cause. Which underlying condition fits best?

UN9975.stem: Believing that a positive screening result proves he has the disease, a man asks his doctor to confirm this. What should he be told?
UN9975.correct_answer: A positive screening result usually needs confirmatory diagnostic testing

UN9975.stem: In a screening programme, 150 people test positive on the initial screening test. Of these, further diagnostic assessment confirms disease in 30 people. What is the positive predictive value of the screening test?
A new blood test for a disease is reported to have a sensitivity of 90%. What does this figure actually tell you?
UN9975.correct_answer: 90% of people with the disease will test positive

UN9975.presentation: Positive High-Risk HPV With Normal Cytology
UN9975.stem: A 28-year-old woman's cervical screening test is positive for high-risk HPV, but the cytology shows no abnormal cell changes. What does the HPV result indicate?
UN9975.correct_answer: She has a risk factor for cervical cell changes and needs follow-up

UN9975.presentation: Effect of Low Prevalence on a Screening Test
UN9975.stem: A new screening test is rolled out across a population where the condition being tested for is rare. Even though the test's sensitivity and specificity remain unchanged, which property of the test is most affected by this low prevalence?

UN9975.correct_answer: Offer antiretroviral therapy now, whatever her CD4 count

UN9975.stem: A middle-aged man has enlarging hands and feet, coarsening facial features, a prominent jaw and new hypertension. Acromegaly is suspected. What is the most appropriate initial screening test?
A newly developed screening test has very high sensitivity. When this test is used appropriately, what is the main practical consequence of this property?

UN9976.presentation: Communicating the limitations of a negative test
UN9976.stem:
A 62-year-old man returns a home faecal immunochemical test through the bowel cancer screening programme and receives a normal result. He has no bowel symptoms. At a GP appointment for another problem, he asks whether this means he definitely cannot have bowel cancer.

What is the best response?
UN9976.correct_answer: Explain it lowers but does not exclude the risk of cancer, and say which symptoms to report

UN9976.stem: A new blood test for a disease is reported to have a sensitivity of 90%. What does this figure actually tell you?
UN9976.correct_answer: 90% of people with the disease will test positive

UN9976.stem: A 38-year-old woman is telephoned by the antenatal screening midwife after her 13-week combined screening test (nuchal translucency with blood markers) returns a higher-chance result for Down's syndrome. She is distressed and asks whether this means her baby definitely has Down's syndrome. What is the most appropriate response?
UN9976.correct_answer: Explain it is a screening result, not a diagnosis, and offer further testing such as NIPT or an invasive diagnostic test

UN9976.presentation: Antimicrobial stewardship in viral respiratory infection
UN9976.stem: The mother of a 4-year-old boy brings him to the GP surgery after three days of runny nose, mild cough and a low-grade fever. She asks for antibiotics because his nursery wants him to get better quickly. He is alert, drinking well, and examination shows clear chest, normal breathing and no signs of ear or tonsil infection. What is the most appropriate response?
UN9976.correct_answer: Explain that antibiotics are unlikely to help, and give advice on symptom care and when to seek help

UN9976.stem: A 28-year-old man presents with a 10-day history of fever, myalgia, sore throat, and a maculopapular rash. He is otherwise well. He had unprotected sexual intercourse with a new partner 4 weeks ago. He is concerned about HIV. You perform a 4th-generation HIV test (antigen/antibody combination). The test comes back negative. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN9976.correct_answer: Order an HIV viral load (PCR) test now

UN9976.stem: A 14-year-old discloses to his GP that he is being bullied and has started having thoughts of harming himself, then asks the doctor to keep this completely secret. What is the most appropriate response?
UN9976.correct_answer: Explain that some information may need to be shared to keep him safe

UN9976.stem: A 35-year-old woman whose paternal grandfather had Huntington disease is considering predictive genetic testing. Her father, aged 60, has no symptoms and has decided not to be tested. She has two younger brothers. She asks whether her result could matter to anyone else in the family. What is the most appropriate response?
UN9976.correct_answer: Explain that a positive result would also reveal her father's status

UN9976.stem: A 26-year-old woman has a positive HIV test at a sexual health clinic during routine screening. She feels well and has no symptoms. Her CD4 count is within the normal range and her viral load is moderately raised. She asks whether she can wait a few years before taking any medication. What is the most appropriate advice?
UN9976.correct_answer: Offer antiretroviral therapy now, whatever her CD4 count

UN9977.stem:
A theatre nurse attends the occupational health department two days after blood from an HIV-positive patient splashed into her eye during an emergency laparotomy. She rinsed her eye at the time but did not report the incident until today. The source patient had recently stopped antiretroviral therapy and his viral load is detectable.

What should be offered now?
UN9977.correct_answer: A 28-day course of HIV post-exposure prophylaxis started as soon as possible today

UN9977.presentation: Measles exposure in pregnancy — post-exposure prophylaxis
UN9977.stem: A 27-year-old woman who is 20 weeks pregnant was in the same room as a child with confirmed measles 3 days ago. She was never vaccinated and has never had measles. She is well. Her measles IgG antibody test is negative. Which is the most appropriate post-exposure prophylaxis?

A 24-year-old woman attends her GP the day after returning from a trip to rural India. Three days ago a stray cat scratched her forearm hard enough to draw blood. She washed the wound with bottled water, and the cat ran off. She feels well and the scratch is healing without signs of infection. Which is the best management?
UN9977.correct_answer: Urgent risk assessment for rabies post-exposure prophylaxis

UN9977.stem: A woman at 30 weeks' gestation, with no history of chickenpox, has significant household exposure to a child with chickenpox. Her varicella IgG is negative. What is the most appropriate management?

UN9977.presentation: Deciding Post-Exposure Management After Hepatitis B Exposure
UN9977.stem: A healthcare assistant is splashed with blood from a patient known to carry hepatitis B. What mainly determines whether post-exposure treatment is required?
UN9977.correct_answer: The assistant's hepatitis B immunity and the type of exposure

UN9977.stem: A healthcare worker sustains a needlestick injury from a needle used on a patient with known untreated HIV. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
UN9977.correct_answer: Wash, risk-assess and start HIV PEP as soon as possible

UN9977.stem:
A 17-year-old young man attends a sexual health clinic alone to ask about HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis. He discusses the benefits, side effects and need for regular testing clearly and makes an informed choice to start. He asks that his parents are not told, as he has not yet told them about his sexuality. There are no concerns about exploitation or abuse.

What is the most appropriate approach?
UN9977.correct_answer: Keep it confidential unless there is a serious risk of harm

UN9977.presentation: STI Screening in an Asymptomatic Patient
UN9977.stem: A 27-year-old woman who has recently started a new sexual relationship asks whether she should have a sexual health screen even though she has no symptoms. What is the most appropriate response?
UN9977.correct_answer: Discuss appropriate testing according to sexual history and risk

UN9978.stem: A 22-year-old man telephones his GP surgery with three days of stinging when passing urine and a clear discharge from the tip of his penis. He started a new sexual relationship a fortnight ago and did not use condoms. He has no fever or loin pain. How should he be managed?
UN9978.correct_answer: Arrange testing for sexually transmitted infections, ideally via a sexual health clinic

UN9978.correct_answer: Discuss appropriate testing according to sexual history and risk

UN9978.presentation: PMOS (formerly PCOS) — endometrial protection when combined pill is unsuitable
UN9978.stem: A 24-year-old woman with PMOS (formerly PCOS) has had no periods for 8 months. A pregnancy test is negative. She is not sexually active and does not need contraception. She has migraine with aura, and she declines an intrauterine device. She asks how to reduce her risk of endometrial problems. Which treatment is most appropriate?

A 19-year-old university fresher sees the practice nurse. She is starting a new relationship and wants to avoid pregnancy, but she also wants to lower her chance of catching chlamydia or other infections.

Which method meets both aims?

UN9978.presentation: Rationale for Partner Notification in Gonorrhoea
UN9978.stem: A patient is diagnosed with gonorrhoea, and the sexual health clinic asks whether their recent partners can be contacted and offered testing. Why is partner notification important?
UN9978.correct_answer: To identify and treat contacts and reduce onward transmission

UN9978.presentation: Modifiable Risk Factor for Osteoporotic Fracture
UN9978.stem: A 70-year-old woman with known osteoporosis asks her doctor which lifestyle change would most help reduce her risk of further fractures. Which is most appropriate?

After a condom split 30 hours ago, a 31-year-old woman attends a sexual health clinic. She is offered an intrauterine device but declines it and asks for a tablet instead. The nurse explains that the tablet chosen works mainly by preventing or postponing ovulation rather than by acting on the lining of the womb. Which emergency contraceptive is being described?

UN10109.correct_answer: Side-room isolation, gloves and apron, and handwashing with soap and water

Over the last 24 hours he has had five episodes of foul-smelling, loose stool with lower abdominal cramps. He has not vomited, no other patients on the bay are unwell, and his white cell count has risen. Which cause is most likely?

UN10109.presentation: Risk Factor for a Severe Diarrhoeal Illness
UN10109.stem: A patient develops profuse, foul-smelling diarrhoea two weeks after a course of co-amoxiclav for a chest infection, and stool testing confirms *Clostridioides difficile* infection. What is the most important risk factor for this infection?

A 70-year-old woman who was treated in hospital for Clostridioides difficile infection last winter asks her GP for antibiotics for a cough and sore throat that look viral. The GP advises against them and she asks how antibiotics led to her bowel infection.

UN10109.correct_answer: Antibiotics kill protective gut bacteria, letting C. difficile multiply and make toxins

UN10109.presentation: C. difficile relapse within 12 weeks — antibiotic choice

Several days after completing a course of a broad-spectrum antibiotic, a patient develops profuse watery diarrhoea and crampy abdominal pain. Which diagnosis must be considered?

UN10112.correct_answer: Exposure to infected blood or body fluids

UN10112.stem: What is the usual mode of transmission for hepatitis A?
Which of the following is a recognised and important route by which hepatitis B virus spreads between people?
UN10112.correct_answer: Exposure to infected blood or sexual contact

UN10112.stem: Long-term infection that slowly progresses towards fibrosis and cirrhosis is a recognised feature of which hepatitis virus?

A 34-year-old man attends a drug and alcohol service for a health check. He has injected heroin intermittently for several years and also has tattoos done professionally, plays football in a team, uses a public gym and lives with a partner who shares meals with him.

Which activity puts him at the greatest risk of acquiring hepatitis C?
UN10112.correct_answer: Sharing needles or other injecting equipment

UN10112.stem:
A 30-year-old man attends a sexual health clinic after condomless sex with a new partner. While his screening samples are taken, he asks whether any of the infections being tested for can be prevented by a vaccine. He is particularly worried about one that can be passed on through blood as well as through sex.

Which infection on the list can he be vaccinated against?

UN10112.presentation: Hepatitis B Exposure in an Immune Worker
UN10112.stem: A healthcare worker has a needlestick exposure to blood from a patient with chronic hepatitis B. The worker previously completed the hepatitis B vaccination course and has documented immunity on blood testing. How should this exposure be interpreted?
UN10112.correct_answer: The risk of transmission is substantially reduced by her documented immunity

UN10112.stem:
A 19-year-old man calls NHS 111, worried after learning that a friend he lives with has HIV. Over the past month they have shared meals, a bathroom and on one occasion a needle and syringe when injecting steroids at the gym.

Which of these exposures carries a real risk of HIV transmission?

UN10114.presentation: Long-Term Risk of Chronic Hepatitis C

UN10114.correct_answer: Ultrasound and serum AFP every 6 months

Which test should be sent first to find out whether she has ever been infected with hepatitis C?

A 30-year-old man attends a sexual health clinic after condomless sex with a new partner. While his screening samples are taken, he asks whether any of the infections being tested for can be prevented by a vaccine. He is particularly worried about one that can be passed on through blood as well as through sex.

Which infection on the list can he be vaccinated against?

UN10114.presentation: Hepatitis B Exposure in an Immune Worker
UN10114.stem: A healthcare worker has a needlestick exposure to blood from a patient with chronic hepatitis B. The worker previously completed the hepatitis B vaccination course and has documented immunity on blood testing. How should this exposure be interpreted?
UN10114.correct_answer: The risk of transmission is substantially reduced by her documented immunity

UN10114.stem: A traveller preparing for a trip to a country where hepatitis A is endemic has never been vaccinated against it. What is the main reason to offer hepatitis A vaccination before departure?
UN10114.correct_answer: It reduces the risk of acquiring hepatitis A infection

UN10123.stem: A 65-year-old man develops fever, cough and diarrhoea several days after returning from a hotel stay. The hotel reports that a handful of other guests have become unwell with similar symptoms around the same time. Which organism is the most likely cause?

UN10123.presentation: Influenza Complication in an Older Adult
UN10123.stem: During a winter flu outbreak in her area, the family of an 81-year-old woman bring her in because she has suddenly spiked a temperature, developed a cough, and become muddled, which is completely out of character for her. Which complication is particularly important to consider in an older adult?

A 70-year-old man has fever, productive cough and right-sided pleuritic pain. He is confused, with a respiratory rate of 32, blood pressure 88/56, and urea 8 mmol/L. What does his CURB-65 assessment indicate?
UN10123.correct_answer: High severity — admit and treat as severe pneumonia

UN10123.stem: A patient with a recent stroke and impaired swallowing develops a pneumonia, with consolidation seen in the right lower lobe. What is the most likely type of pneumonia and an important management consideration?
UN10123.correct_answer: Aspiration pneumonia — antibiotics and a swallow assessment

UN10123.presentation: NEWS2 in an older adult with infection
UN10123.stem: An 80-year-old woman admitted with a urinary tract infection is reviewed overnight on a care of the elderly ward. Her observations have changed and her NEWS2 score has risen to 10. She is not febrile. What does this score indicate?
UN10123.correct_answer: High risk of severe illness or death from sepsis, needing urgent senior review

UN10123.stem: An 81-year-old woman is admitted from her care home with three days of cough productive of green sputum, and a chest X-ray shows right lower lobe consolidation. Staff say that until yesterday she was fully orientated, but she now does not know where she is or what day it is. She has bronchial breathing at the right base and a raised white cell count. Which feature most clearly indicates more severe pneumonia?

A 67-year-old man has been nursed face-down in the intensive care unit for severe pneumonia. After he is turned onto his back, red patches are noted over both knees and the front of the chest. Half an hour later, after the areas have been offloaded, the patches are still red and do not fade under light finger pressure. The skin is intact. What does this finding indicate?
UN10123.correct_answer: Pressure injury needing assessment and continued offloading

UN10123.presentation: Older adult newly on an SSRI with confusion — key blood test
UN10123.stem: An 81-year-old woman started sertraline for depression three weeks ago. She also takes indapamide for hypertension. Her daughter brings her to the GP because over the past few days she has become nauseated, unsteady on her feet and newly confused. There are no focal neurological signs and she is afebrile. Which blood test is most important to request first?

UN10129.presentation: Acute Scrotal Pain In A Boy
UN10129.stem: A 12-year-old boy develops sudden, severe scrotal pain and swelling during a football match. On examination the affected testis sits higher than the other side and is extremely tender to touch. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A teenage boy develops a painful, swollen testis several days after his parotid glands swelled up. What complication is this?
Which clinical feature points more towards testicular torsion than epididymo-orchitis?
UN10129.correct_answer: Abrupt onset of intense scrotal pain

UN10129.presentation: Gradual Scrotal Pain With Urethral Symptoms
UN10129.stem: A sexually active 25-year-old man develops scrotal swelling and discomfort on the right side that has worsened steadily over three days, along with pain on passing urine and a clear urethral discharge. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A 17-year-old has acute scrotal pain. Which single feature most favours testicular torsion over epididymo-orchitis and mandates urgent exploration?
UN10129.correct_answer: Absent cremasteric reflex with a high-riding testis and sudden onset

UN10129.stem: A 10-year-old boy presents with acute right-sided scrotal pain for 12 hours. He is systemically well. Examination shows a normal testicular lie, an intact cremasteric reflex, and a small tender blue-black nodule visible through the scrotal skin at the upper pole of the testis. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old university student who was never vaccinated attends an urgent treatment centre. A week ago he had fever and painful swelling below both ears that made chewing difficult. Since yesterday his right testis has become progressively painful and swollen and his temperature has risen again. The testis is enlarged and tender, it lies in a normal position and the cremasteric reflex is present. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
A 58-year-old woman develops a painful, swollen calf in one leg several days after major surgery. Which diagnosis must be considered?

UN10141.stem: A 10-year-old develops, two to three weeks after a sore throat, a migratory polyarthritis (moving from joint to joint), fever, a new heart murmur, and painless subcutaneous nodules over the extensor surfaces. Anti-streptolysin O titre is raised. What is the most likely diagnosis?

An 11-year-old boy who moved to the UK from South Asia two months ago is brought to the GP with fever and painful joints. Over the past week his right knee became hot and swollen, then improved as his left ankle and then his right wrist became affected. He had a sore throat about three weeks ago. There are pink rings with pale centres on his trunk, and a new soft pansystolic murmur at the apex. His antistreptolysin O titre is raised. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 9-year-old boy recently arrived from West Africa is seen in the paediatric clinic three weeks after a sore throat. He has had painful joints that flit from knees to ankles, a faint rash of pink rings on his trunk and a few small, firm, painless nodules over his elbows. Which long-term cardiac problem is he at greatest risk of developing?
UN10141.correct_answer: Chronic rheumatic valve disease, mainly of the mitral valve

UN10141.stem: A 45-year-old woman from Bangladesh presents with progressive breathlessness and occasional haemoptysis. She had rheumatic fever in childhood. On auscultation there is a tapping apex beat, a loud S1, an opening snap, and a low-pitched mid-diastolic rumble best heard at the apex in the left lateral position. What is the diagnosis?

A 24-year-old woman has fever, sore throat and enlarged neck glands, followed by severe tiredness and an enlarged liver and spleen. Blood film shows atypical lymphocytes. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A GP practice audits a rapid throat swab test for group A streptococcus in patients with sore throats. Of those tested, 50 had a positive rapid test, and throat culture confirmed streptococcal infection in 45 of these 50. What does the figure of 45 out of 50 (90%) represent?

UN10141.presentation: Tender Shin Nodules After Sore Throat
UN10141.stem: A 29-year-old woman develops several tender, red, raised nodules on both shins about two weeks after a streptococcal sore throat. The lesions are firm swellings rather than open sores. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN10141.presentation: Haematuria Weeks After a Throat Infection
UN10141.stem: A 9-year-old boy develops visibly blood-stained urine and facial puffiness roughly three weeks after a sore throat caused by a streptococcal infection. Blood tests show reduced serum complement C3. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN10142.presentation: Antimicrobial resistance as a public-health concern
UN10142.stem: At a practice meeting, the prescribing data for a GP surgery show far more antibiotic prescriptions than neighbouring practices, mostly for coughs and sore throats. A new receptionist asks why the integrated care board is so concerned about this. What is the main public-health reason for limiting unnecessary antibiotic use?
UN10142.correct_answer: Antibiotic exposure selects for resistant bacteria that then spread in the community

UN10142.stem: A doctor diagnoses a patient with a notifiable infectious disease. The patient asks the doctor to keep it confidential and not tell anyone. What is the doctor's obligation?
UN10142.correct_answer: Notify the relevant public health authority, as required by law

UN10142.stem: A public health registrar is classifying local health programmes. One of them invites men in their 65th year for a single abdominal ultrasound to detect aortic aneurysms before they cause symptoms. Which level of prevention does this programme represent?

A 7-year-old girl is seen by her GP with fever and tender swelling of both parotid glands. She has had no MMR vaccines. The GP is confident clinically that this is mumps and has advised rest, fluids and paracetamol. No laboratory test has yet been done.

What is the most appropriate action regarding public health?
UN10142.correct_answer: Notify the health protection team now

UN10142.stem:
A 4-year-old boy is seen in a GP surgery with two days of fever, sore throat and vomiting. This morning his mother noticed a red rash that started on his chest and has spread; it blanches and feels rough to touch. His cheeks are flushed with paleness around the mouth, and his tongue is red with prominent papillae.

What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN10142.presentation: Suspected enteric fever in a food handler — notification
UN10142.stem: A 40-year-old chef returned from Bangladesh two weeks ago and presents to the emergency department with a sustained fever and abdominal pain. The registrar strongly suspects enteric fever. Blood cultures have been sent and results are expected in 48 hours. Which is the doctor's legal duty regarding public health notification?
UN10142.correct_answer: Notify the health protection team on suspicion

UN10142.stem: A director of public health reports that life expectancy differs by several years between two neighbourhoods a short bus ride apart. The neighbourhood with lower life expectancy has higher unemployment, poorer housing and lower educational attainment. What does this difference best illustrate?
UN10142.correct_answer: Health inequalities arising from the social determinants of health

UN10142.stem:
A 40-year-old man who recently returned from a stay in a region with an ongoing diphtheria outbreak develops a sore throat, low-grade fever and a grey membrane over the tonsils. Public health staff begin tracing the people he has been near.

By what route is this infection most likely to have spread to him?
UN10142.correct_answer: Respiratory droplets from an infected person

UN10410.presentation: Gradual Scrotal Pain With Urethral Symptoms
UN10410.stem: A sexually active 25-year-old man develops scrotal swelling and discomfort on the right side that has worsened steadily over three days, along with pain on passing urine and a clear urethral discharge. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A man has a purulent urethral discharge and dysuria, and a swab confirms Neisseria gonorrhoeae. What is the most appropriate treatment, alongside partner notification?
A 25-year-old man has dysuria and a profuse purulent urethral discharge. A NAAT and culture confirm Neisseria gonorrhoeae. What is the most appropriate first-line treatment?

UN10410.presentation: Reactive arthritis — identifying the triggering infection
UN10410.stem: A 24-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a swollen right knee and a painful left heel for 5 days. Three weeks ago he had dysuria and a urethral discharge that settled without treatment; he has had a new sexual partner recently. He has no diarrhoea. Knee aspirate shows no crystals and Gram stain is negative, with culture pending. Reactive arthritis is suspected. Which investigation is most appropriate to identify the triggering infection?
UN10410.correct_answer: First-void urine nucleic acid amplification test

UN10410.stem: A 31-year-old man attends a sexual health clinic worried about an infection because his right testis feels heavier than the left. He has no pain, urethral discharge or dysuria. On examination there is a firm, irregular, non-tender area that cannot be separated from the body of the right testis. The epididymis feels normal, and a torch held against the scrotum does not light up the swelling. What is the most appropriate next investigation?

UN10410.presentation: Epididymo-orchitis in a young man — microbiological testing
UN10410.stem: A 24-year-old man presents with 3 days of gradually worsening right scrotal pain and swelling, dysuria and a scant urethral discharge. He has had a new female sexual partner in the past month. The right epididymis is tender and swollen, the testis lies normally, and the cremasteric reflex is present. Torsion is considered unlikely. Before starting antibiotics, which investigation is most important?

UN10410.presentation: Epididymo-orchitis with gonococcal infection — antibiotic choice
UN10410.stem:
A 23-year-old man attends a sexual health clinic with 4 days of right scrotal pain and swelling and a urethral discharge. He had condomless sex with a new partner 2 weeks ago. The epididymis is tender and swollen, the testis lies normally, and torsion is considered unlikely. Microscopy of a urethral smear shows Gram-negative intracellular diplococci. He has no drug allergies.

Which treatment is most appropriate?

UN10410.presentation: Sudden Severe Testicular Pain in a Teenager
UN10410.stem: A 15-year-old boy develops sudden, severe pain in his right testicle with associated nausea and vomiting. Why is this presentation treated as a surgical emergency requiring immediate exploration?
UN10410.correct_answer: Testicular viability can be lost if torsion persists

UN10411.stem: A 22-year-old woman attends a sexual health clinic with a week of bilateral lower abdominal pain, pain deep inside during intercourse and bleeding after sex. She has a new sexual partner and they do not use condoms. Her temperature is 37.9°C. On bimanual examination there is tenderness in both adnexa and pain on moving the cervix. A pregnancy test is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 29-year-old woman and her partner attend the fertility clinic after two years of regular unprotected intercourse without a pregnancy. Her periods are regular, she has no painful periods or pain during intercourse, and a mid-luteal progesterone confirms ovulation. Her partner's semen analysis is normal. At the age of 19 she was admitted with pelvic inflammatory disease after a chlamydia infection that had gone unnoticed for months. Which cause of subfertility is most likely?

A 23-year-old woman sees her GP with 5 days of bilateral lower abdominal pain, deep dyspareunia and an abnormal vaginal discharge. She uses condoms inconsistently and her periods are irregular. Her temperature is 37.6°C and she is otherwise well. Bimanual examination shows cervical motion tenderness and bilateral adnexal tenderness. The GP suspects pelvic inflammatory disease. Which investigation should be performed first?

UN10411.presentation: Pelvic inflammatory disease with an intrauterine device
UN10411.stem: A 31-year-old woman has had a copper intrauterine device (IUD) for 3 years. She presents to a sexual health clinic with lower abdominal pain, abnormal discharge and cervical motion tenderness. She is afebrile and systemically well, her pregnancy test is negative and she is diagnosed with mild to moderate pelvic inflammatory disease. Swabs are taken and outpatient antibiotics are started. She wishes to keep the IUD as her contraception. What is the most appropriate management of the IUD?
UN10411.correct_answer: Leave it in place and review her response early

UN10411.stem: A 24-year-old woman has lower abdominal pain, deep dyspareunia, abnormal discharge and cervical motion tenderness, with a mild fever. What is the most appropriate management?
UN10411.correct_answer: Start empirical antibiotics for PID without waiting for swab results

UN10411.stem: A 22-year-old woman presents with bilateral lower abdominal pain, deep dyspareunia, and a mucopurulent vaginal discharge. Bimanual examination reveals cervical motion tenderness and bilateral adnexal tenderness. She is afebrile. What is the most appropriate management?
UN10411.correct_answer: Outpatient antibiotics — IM ceftriaxone plus oral doxycycline and metronidazole

UN10411.stem: A 23-year-old woman comes in with lower abdominal discomfort and an unusual discharge, and moving her cervix on examination causes marked tenderness. If her pelvic infection goes untreated, which long-term complication is she at risk of?

A woman at 36 weeks gestation presents with two episodes of painless, fresh bright red vaginal bleeding over 2 days. She is haemodynamically stable. The uterus is soft and non-tender and the fetal heart rate is normal. Her placental site has not been documented. Speculum examination shows a small amount of blood coming through a closed cervical os, with no lower genital tract lesion. What is the most appropriate immediate next step?
UN10411.correct_answer: Ultrasound scan to locate the placenta

UN10557.presentation: Infection Control in Suspected Meningococcal Disease
UN10557.stem: A 4-year-old boy is brought to the paediatric emergency department with a high fever, lethargy and a spreading non-blanching purpuric rash on his legs. Intravenous ceftriaxone is given immediately and he is to be admitted. A nurse asks which infection control precautions staff should use while caring for him. What is the most appropriate answer?
UN10557.correct_answer: Droplet precautions in a single room

UN10557.presentation: Infection control for suspected C. difficile
UN10557.stem: A 76-year-old man in a four-bed bay on an orthopaedic ward has developed three episodes of unexplained loose stool overnight after recent antibiotics. A stool sample has been sent for C. difficile testing. The nurse in charge asks what infection-control measures are needed now. What is the most appropriate advice?
UN10557.correct_answer: Side-room isolation, gloves and apron, and handwashing with soap and water

UN10557.stem:
A newly qualified nurse in a general practice treatment room tells a colleague that she only uses gloves, aprons and careful sharps disposal for patients known to have an infection such as hepatitis or HIV. Her colleague explains how standard infection control precautions should be applied.

Which statement is correct?
UN10557.correct_answer: They apply to every patient in every setting, at all times

UN10557.stem: An 81-year-old man is on day six of an admission for pneumonia, treated with intravenous co-amoxiclav and then a cephalosporin. Over the last 24 hours he has had five episodes of foul-smelling, loose stool with lower abdominal cramps. He has not vomited, no other patients on the bay are unwell, and his white cell count has risen. Which cause is most likely?

UN10557.presentation: Risk Factor for a Severe Diarrhoeal Illness
UN10557.stem: A patient develops profuse, foul-smelling diarrhoea two weeks after a course of co-amoxiclav for a chest infection, and stool testing confirms *Clostridioides difficile* infection. What is the most important risk factor for this infection?

A 70-year-old woman who was treated in hospital for Clostridioides difficile infection last winter asks her GP for antibiotics for a cough and sore throat that look viral. The GP advises against them and she asks how antibiotics led to her bowel infection.

Which explanation is most accurate?
UN10557.correct_answer: Antibiotics kill protective gut bacteria, letting C. difficile multiply and make toxins

UN10557.presentation: C. difficile relapse within 12 weeks — antibiotic choice
UN10557.stem: A 76-year-old woman had a first episode of Clostridioides difficile infection treated with a course of oral vancomycin, and her diarrhoea settled. Three weeks after her symptoms resolved, she develops watery diarrhoea again, and a stool sample is positive for C. difficile toxin. She is not severely unwell. Which treatment is most appropriate?
Several days after completing a course of a broad-spectrum antibiotic, a patient develops profuse watery diarrhoea and crampy abdominal pain. Which diagnosis must be considered?
